Sports.title: How Trabzonspor shocked Turkish rivals to make Mohamed Salah their Black Sea saviour
Sports.content:
It began with a text sent during the World Cup. Ertugrul Dogan, the president of Trabzonspor, was watching Egypt when he picked up his phone and messaged his manager, Fatih Tekke. “Coach,” it read. “Do you want Mohamed Salah?”

Tekke’s response was immediate enthusiasm, though Trabzonspor’s initial push for Salah went under the radar with Besiktas looking most likely to land the former Liverpool striker. In Turkish football, Istanbul’s Big Three – Galatasaray, Fenerbahce and Besiktas – have long held monopoly on the Super Lig’s marquee signings.

Istanbul is not the capital but it is the undisputed financial, cultural and commercial heartbeat of the country and wider region. It came as a shock, then, when Salah opted for Trabzonspor.

The club are by no means minnows. They form part of the traditional Big Four alongside their Istanbul rivals. Yet the football-crazy port city on the eastern Black Sea coast lacks the cosmopolitan lifestyle Istanbul offers. What it possesses instead is devotion. Most Turkish cities do not have a strong local football identity, with residents supporting one of the major Istanbul sides from afar. Trabzon is one of the few exceptions. The entire region eats, sleeps and breathes for its team.

Trabzon is like the Newcastle of Turkey: a proud, working-class city in the north-east with an industrial maritime past, deeply tied to its football club and trying to forge a new identity to adapt to the modern world.

Salah’s arrival has thrust a city that often feels politically and geographically sidelined onto the global stage. This transfer is bigger than football. Trabzon wants to revitalise the city as a maritime trade, tourism and logistics hub. The arrival of the Egyptian superstar ensures an even bigger spotlight on the city.

View image in fullscreen An excited Trabzonspor fan decked in traditional claret and sky blue colours sports sunglasses decorated with new signing Mohamed Salah. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

The chaotic scenes at Trabzon airport on Wednesday – when supporters turned the terminal into a sea of red flares, followed by tens of thousands packing Papara Park for Salah’s signing ceremony – demonstrated their fervour.

Salah could easily have accepted lucrative proposals in the Saudi Pro League or Major League Soccer, but their fan culture pales by comparison. Crucially, the 34-year-old remains in a highly competitive league in the Uefa zone; Trabzonspor need only navigate the playoff rounds for a place in the Europa League group stage.

“I am seeing a reception like this for the first time in my life,” Salah told the roaring crowd during his unveiling. “I came here to win trophies. I am here to bring titles to this club.”

Trabzonspor have played the role of disruptors in Turkish football – the Black Sea rebels who broke Istanbul’s stranglehold in the 1970s and most recently won the league title in 2021–22. But never before has a player of this magnitude rejected Istanbul for Trabzon.

View image in fullscreen Salah takes a photo as the fans offer a hearty welcome. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

The Turkish top flight is experiencing a renaissance. Leandro Trossard joined Besiktas after a title-winning campaign with Arsenal; Victor Osimhen continues to spearhead Galatasaray’s attack; while Nathan Aké and Mason Greenwood now line up for Fenerbahce. The league is also developing world-class homegrown talent, with Arda Güler at Real Madrid and Ferdi Kadioglu at Brighton serving as prime examples.

Trabzonspor’s pursuit of Salah was executed in the shadows. The club deployed their former winger Mahmoud Hassan – known as Trézéguet – as their secret operative. Salah’s international teammate spoke with the Egyptian captain daily, to help convince him to consider the move.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There was a cultural element, too: moving to a welcoming, Muslim-majority nation where Salah and his family could feel immediately at home. Trabzonspor locked him into a two-year contract through to June 2028 and disclosed the financial details on the Public Disclosure Platform (KAP). Salah will earn a base annual salary of €10m (£8.5m) alongside a guaranteed €7m annual signing bonus, netting him €17m per season (€34m net over two years).

Because wages in Turkey are paid net, with the club covering all tax liabilities, Salah in effect takes home 50% more than his final Liverpool contract. The deal also includes performance add-ons, a 5% agent’s fee on gross wages and an extraordinary image-rights agreement granting Salah a 20% royalty on all personal merchandise sold through the club’s official TS Club retail network.

The commercial return was immediate. Within 24 hours of Salah landing, Trabzonspor sold more than 17,000 season tickets, generating £11m. Dogan confirmed that total projected revenue from tickets, sponsorships and merchandise during the Salah era is expected to approach £22m, in effect self-funding the transfer.

View image in fullscreen Trabzonspor supporters unveil a banner celebrating Salah. Photograph: Nurgul Gunaydin/AFP/Getty Images

Crucially, Trabzonspor did not overextend themselves. Balanced by roughly €95m raised in player sales since last season, the transfer is manageable financially. Salah joins a side on an upward trajectory under Tekke. Languishing in 13th when Tekke took over in March 2025, the team recovered to finish eight points behind the champions, Galatasaray, in third and won the Turkish Cup.

Tekke added the Valencia defender Cenk Özkacar and the Manchester United loanee André Onana in goal and Trabzonspor are in talks with Darwin Núñez.

Taking his favoured No 10 shirt, Salah steps into a side in the ascendant. Yet the challenge remains steep. Galatasaray have won four consecutive league titles, while Besiktas and Fenerbahce have spent lavishly this summer. Trabzonspor will be hoping his arrival serves as a catalyst for a change in fortunes.

For Trabzon and the eastern region, however, Salah’s arrival is far more than a transfer story. The tide could be turning back in the favour of the Black Sea Storm.

Sports.title: Martin O’Neill absent from Celtic’s win at Kilmarnock as Høgh hits hat-trick
Sports.content:
Kasper Høgh scored a hat-trick, his first goals for Celtic, as the Scottish champions made light of the absence of their manager Martin O’Neill with a 5-1 win at Kilmarnock on Sunday.

Victory made it two wins out of two Premiership games for Celtic, with 74-year-old boss O’Neill missing the trip to Rugby Park after what the club had said earlier this week was a “small procedure” in hospital.

No details were given about O’Neill’s operation, which came after the veteran Northern Irish manager took charge of Celtic’s win against Dundee in their first game of the season. But the club’s assistant manager, Shaun Maloney, speaking before Sunday’s kick-off, said O’Neill was on the mend.

“He is doing better again,” Maloney told Sky Sports. “He came to the team hotel and spoke to the players but he just needs an extra few days.”

O’Neill’s mood would doubtless have been improved by the performance of his side, with Celtic 3-0 ahead before half-time thanks to Høgh. The Danish striker, who joined in July from Bodø/Glimt, needed less than a minute to score his first Celtic goal, heading in at the back post from a cross by Arne Engels.

Høgh doubled Celtic’s lead in the 33rd minute, with Camilo Durán seizing on Johnly Yfeko’s pass out of defence. He combined with Benjamin Nygren to work the ball to Høgh on the left edge of the box, with the forward finishing well.

Two minutes later, Høgh had his hat-trick. Nygren slipping the ball right for Durán, whose cross took the Kilmarnock goalkeeper Max Stryjek out of play, with Høgh nodding into an empty net.

Celtic extended their lead early in the second half after they were effectively gifted a fourth goal by Stryjek. His pass out of defence went straight to Nygren in front of goal and his shot into the top corner made it 4-0.

Michael Schjønning-Larsen pulled a goal back for Kilmarnock in the 56th minute after finishing a well-worked move. But Celtic went four goals ahead again when Luke McCowan, moments after coming on, volleyed in from close range 15 minutes from time after Kilmarnock made a mess of trying to clear the ball from a corner.

View image in fullscreen Celtic’s assistant manager Shaun Maloney took charge with Martin O’Neill still recovering from a procedure in hospital. Photograph: Robert Perry/PA

Three Hearts summer signings were on target as Wouter Vrancken belatedly got his reign up and running with an emphatic 4-0 win over Dundee United. The Belgian had suffered four consecutive defeats – three in Europe – since replacing Derek McInnes in June, but his new-look team tore United apart in their first home league game of the season.

Tom Renaud, Calvin Miller and Josh McPake all marked their first league outings at Tynecastle with goals, while last season’s talisman Claudio Braga broke his duck for the campaign.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Jambos made a fast start as Renaud, a few days after notching against Benfica, unleashed a ferocious strike beyond Jack Walton from just short of 30 yards after being teed up by Braga in the fourth minute.

Hearts were gifted the chance to double their lead when VAR spotted Daniel Bennie wrestling Jamie McCart to the ground in the box. Miller stepped up to fire the penalty straight down the middle.

Hearts killed off any hopes of a United fightback in the 56th minute when Braga drilled in a low angled shot from 12 yards out after being set up by Sabah Kerjota. McPake then marked his first competitive start for the Jambos with his first goal as he tucked a clinical low finish beyond Walton after playing a one-two with Braga on the left of the box.

In Sunday’s other 3pm kick-off, Motherwell drew 0-0 at home to Falkirk. Rangers’s encounter with Hibernian at Ibrox kicked off an hour later.

Sports.title: Alexia Putellas: ‘I’m hungry to win, to fight with my teammates for victory’
Sports.content:
Momentarily, Alexia Putellas appears somewhat nervous, stepping inside the cramped conference room in a Kent hotel to see 23 reporters squeezed inside, all eager to hear from the Women’s Super League’s newest global superstar, but she quickly composes herself. Within minutes, she is into her stride, asking for tips about roast dinners and drawing laughs from the room as she jokes that her friends who play for other English clubs have told her they are going to kick her. Welcome to the WSL.

Speaking in English throughout the 20-minute session with ever-increasing proficiency, the two-time Ballon d’Or winner and four-time Champions League winner explains why she has swapped the prestige of Barcelona – where she has been idolised over a trophy-laden 14-year spell – for a team that finished 22 points adrift of the European qualification places last term.

Backed by the ambitious businesswoman Michele Kang, the independently run London City Lionesses have made eye-catching, world-class signings this summer, including the France forward Kadidiatou Diani from Lyonnes – who are also majority-owned by Kang – Putellas’s Barcelona teammate Mapi León and the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps from PSG.

Undoubtedly, though, Putellas is the biggest of them all and the signing that will have made all of women’s football take notice. As a serial winner will Putellas have to be patient for trophies here?

“Both can live together, my mentality and the moment of the project. I’m going to bring to the project whatever the project needs from me, so I’m 100% committed,” the 2023 World Cup winner says. “I’m hungry to win, to be better day after day, to fight with my teammates for the victory. I’m going to try to give my best to the team and let’s see at the end of the season how good we were.”

View image in fullscreen Barcelona made Putellas a parting gift of a photo of herself surrounded by every trophy she’d won while at the club. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters

London City Lionesses were promoted to the WSL in 2025, finished sixth last season in their top-flight debut and are yet to win a major trophy. Asked what her expectations are, Putellas says: “I don’t have expectations. I just want the hard work we are doing to speak for itself. It’s a hard competition. Of course, I have a competitive mind and I want to win every game. But I don’t have expectations in this sport. In my opinion, you shouldn’t. Just work in the back[ground] and give everything.”

Putellas was named as the Women’s Champions League’s player of the season after helping fire Barcelona to a fourth European title in six seasons, yet at the age of 32, she still feels she can improve – “Of course, always, day after day, I want to learn things [and] just keep going, I never stop [trying to] be as good as I can,” – but specifically she thinks the WSL can add elements to her skillset.

“It will be different, but that’s why I’m here, because I’m looking forward to improving myself,” she says. “It’s being a more complete player, as much as I can. It’s about learning new things, playing with and against other players and just trying to find where my limits are. It will take time because it’s a new beginning and a big change for me.

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas will be hoping to stamp her name on more than just her contract and the camera after joining London City Lionesses. Photograph: London City Lionesses

“[In the WSL] you never know what will be the result of the game; it’s a very competitive league, week after week. I imagine all the games will push you to your limits. It’s a very entertaining league.

“The first conversation [I had with London City] was about what the club wants and how ambitious the project is. I want to be part of that journey, bring the experience I have and learn as a player and make me more complete. I made the move for that and just being in other positions that I’ve never been in. In my opinion, this league can give me that.”

When asked if she had sought advice from her former Barcelona teammates, such as the England duo Keira Walsh and Lucy Bronze, about what to expect in England, she says: “Well, some of them told me that it’s a hard league and they’re going to kick me. No, I’m just joking.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

She also chuckled when asked about London’s traffic and expensive property prices, even if she was slightly hesitant reflecting on her first taste of an English fry-up: “Erm, yes. It was quite different. Not the beans, but the sausages and eggs. It was fine.”

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas scored twice when Spain thrashed England 4-0 in June, ending the Lionesses’ chances of automatic World Cup qualification. Photograph: Francisco Ubilla/Reuters

She will have plenty of help when it comes to settling into the London City, with six Spanish teammates and a head coach, Eder Maestre, who she says did a “really good job with Tenerife”. Maestre, yet another coaching export of the Basque Country, was at Tenerife for a year and a half, finishing sixth in his only full season and taking them to fifth by the time he left for England.

Putellas knows there will be differences tactically in the English game and thinks that can help her add even more strings to her bow.

“I really believe that moving to England can give me something more,” she says. “Like, I can control the low blocks and all this stuff; I am used to it playing in Spain. I have already controlled that, so [I want] different kind of games or box-to-box and all this stuff.”

She then apologises for her English – not that any apology was needed – and explains she is still learning the language and working hard to improve it all the time. If her footballing ability continues to enhance too, then WSL defenders had better beware.

Sports.title: ‘It’s a true art form’: Nigeria goalkeeper Maduka Okoye on high fashion and life at Udinese
Sports.content:
When Maduka Okoye visited Paris fashion week for the Jean Paul Gaultier show, taking his seat in the front row alongside rapper Cardi B, the online reaction was swift. Within hours, footage of the Udinese and Nigeria goalkeeper was all over TikTok and Instagram – where his audience now stretches to nearly two million followers – transforming the appearance into a viral cultural moment that crossed beyond the boundaries of football.

Yet ask Okoye to reflect on his sudden explosion into the fashion ecosystem, and he frames it not as a pursuit of celebrity or status, but as a genuine interest in art. “Being at the Paris fashion week was really impressive,” Okoye says. “It was my first time really coming into contact with high fashion, and it was fascinating. It’s a true art form. I enjoyed it immensely and since that moment I’ve become a much bigger fan of fashion than I was before.”

In an era where elite footballers are expected to be multi-dimensional figures – balancing performance on the pitch, personal branding, digital presence, and commercial partnerships – Okoye embodies a generation navigating this global landscape with ease. Crucially, he knows exactly where to steer the ship.

While some athletes run the danger of losing their bearings when the off-pitch spotlight intensifies, the goalkeeper draws a sharp, impenetrable line between his two realms.

“What happens off the pitch is one thing, what happens on the pitch is another,” he says. “You have to separate the two. I never let these two worlds collide. Even though marketing and personal branding are part of the business today, at the end of the day I am a goalkeeper, and my main job is to protect my team’s goal. Outside football, I pursue things that matter to me but my priority and my work remain between the posts. These two worlds don’t overlap. What I do off the pitch has zero impact on what I do on it, and those two spheres will never cross.”

Reinforcing that boundary is the daily environment in which Okoye operates. Playing for Udinese, nestled in the calm, industrious region of Friuli-Venezia Giulia, creates a vivid contrast with the flashing cameras of Paris or the hyper-fast churn of social media trends. For Okoye, who grew up in Düsseldorf, Udine offers an essential sanctuary.

View image in fullscreen Maduka Okoye arrived at Udinese after spells at Sparta Rotterdam and Watford. Photograph: Foto Petrussi/Udinese FC

“I grew up in a big city, so in my heart I am and always will be a city boy, used to the metropolitan rhythm,” he smiles. “However, as you grow older, you learn to appreciate the peaceful side of life. I really like Udine. It’s a human, quiet city. You have your peace there and you can focus 100% on your work. I’m genuinely happy to live here. The serenity in Udine is good for you as a person and makes you feel very comfortable.”

That quiet focus away from the noise is paying dividends on the pitch. Having arrived after spells with Sparta Rotterdam and Watford – where he only made two senior appearances – he has established himself as a cornerstone between the posts for Udinese. In a footballing landscape often obsessed with highlight-reel saves, Okoye is staying focused.

“I believe there is always room for improvement in every direction,” he says. “I’m very happy working here with a great goalkeeping staff. I’m on a good path, learning every day, and I can’t wait to show it on the pitch during the season.”

When asked which goalkeeper impressed him most during the recent World Cup, Okoye says: “I found Spain’s Unai Simón very impressive, especially towards the final stages. Not so much for making hundreds of saves, but for the way he remained inside the game, defending deep balls against France. For me, that was goalkeeping of the highest level.

“As I said, it’s not just about spectacular saves; it’s about managing those details. Overall it was a great World Cup, and for us young goalkeepers it was a fantastic learning opportunity.”

Okoye’s drive to absorb lessons from top-tier athletes extends beyond football. During a recent visit to the British Grand Prix at Silverstone, he met rising Italian Formula One driver Kimi Antonelli, taking the opportunity to study the mechanics of another high-level sport.

“It was fantastic. The whole Formula One experience was extraordinary,” Okoye says. “I think there’s so much an athlete can learn from other sports. Meeting the drivers, especially Kimi, was great. From the outside you only see the race on TV, but behind it there’s an immense amount of work going on. It was impressive to see how much effort and preparation go into competing at that level.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Maduka Okoye enjoyed his visit to the British Grand Prix where he presented Kimi Antonelli with his pole position award after qualifying. Photograph: David Davies/PA

Udinese enter the Serie A season with stability and ambition and, in Friuli, that means looking towards Europe. “Everything is possible,” Okoye says. “But I think we should talk about that again in February or March. First we have to get the basics right and take it game by game. Then we’ll see where we are. We certainly have the quality, the players, an excellent staff, and a solid club behind us. Udinese is a club where a player can really grow and make that leap in quality.

“For me, Serie A remains one of the best leagues in the world and I’m grateful to be part of it. The higher the level of the league, the happier and prouder I am to play in it. We’re working hard and can’t wait to compete against the best.”

There is also unfinished business with Nigeria. Watching the World Cup from his living room was far from ideal. “Obviously it would have been better to be part of it, but unfortunately we didn’t qualify,” Okoye acknowledges. “We’ll try again for the next World Cup. I still enjoyed watching it from the outside; I supported Germany, hoping they’d go a bit further. Now we look to the future, and I really hope to be there at the next edition.”

As football continues to evolve into a convergence of sport, entertainment and global culture, figures such as Okoye offer a compelling blueprint for the modern athlete. He is a player capable of sitting in the front row in Paris on Monday, studying a rival on screen on Wednesday, and commanding his penalty box on Sunday – all without losing his sporting identity.

“On a personal level, it hasn’t changed me at all. I’m still the exact same person,” Okoye says. “Of course, when it comes to business and my personal image, a lot of things have changed. Fortunately, I have a great team around me and we try to make the most of these opportunities. But I repeat: who I am hasn’t changed. It’s simply part of my professional journey.”

And what advice would Okoye offer a young footballer dreaming of putting on the gloves and following in his footsteps? The Udinese goalkeeper does not hesitate: “To work hard, believe in yourself, and have faith.”

Sports.title: Fifa defends Gianni Infantino and launches attack after ‘effort to undermine’ president
Sports.content:
Fifa last night issued a thinly-veiled attack on Uefa and other leading figures in European football in a statement which alleged there is a “concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president,” as football’s civil war escalated further.

Uefa has made it clear they regard Infantino’s continued leadership of world football as untenable following his role in the World Cup sell-off plans, while the Guardian revealed on Friday the Norwegian Football Federation has publicly called on him to resign, with Fifa responding by accusing them of attempting to subvert the organisation’s democratic processes.

Fifa’s latest defence of Infantino followed Uefa’s confirmation on Saturday that a “departure payment” was made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Fifa president while he was the organisation’s general secretary over a decade ago.

The Daily Telegraph had reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum following the alleged relationship with Infantino, allegations Fifa dismissed as “categorically untrue.”

Fifa went further last night by accusing Infantino’s critics of attempting to remove him from office before next March’s presidential election.

As previously reported by the Guardian, Uefa is seeking support from other confederations to call an Emergency Fifa Congress to trigger a vote of no confidence in the president, but their own members can provide the 43 votes to call a meeting it is unclear whether they would reach the threshold of 106 of the 211 Fifa members required to unseat Infantino.

North American confederation Concacaf are aligned with Uefa, while there is some support amongst the Asian Football Confederation, but the Confederation of African Football and South American confederation Conmebol have both publicly announced their backing for Infantino.

“Echoing the recent statements of Conmebol and CAF, as well as discussions with Fifa Member Associations and Confederations from around the world, Fifa will not support, facilitate or tolerate any process concerning the election of the Fifa President that is inconsistent with Fifa’s Statutes, democratic procedures and established governance framework,” a Fifa spokesperson said. “The Fifa President was democratically elected by Fifa’s Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate.

“The Fifa president was democratically elected by Fifa’s member associations and continues to serve with their mandate. Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes.”

Uefa had responded to Fifa’s proposal to sell 20% of a new company controlling the World Cup’s commercial assets with a threat backed by all 55 European countries to boycott their tournaments unless the plans were abandoned, which they were less than 48 hours later.

Significantly however, Uefa released a new statement last Thursday after Fifa had confirmed that Infantino retained the organisation’s “full support” following a crisis meeting of their management board in Rabat the previous day, saying that nothing had changed and that the boycott threat remained in place.

Fifa is now convinced that Uefa is behind coordinated attempts to remove Infantino. It is unclear what further concessions Uefa is demanding to cancel the boycott, which faces its first test next month at the Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland.

Fifa’s statement last night also included a new attack on the media, a well-worn tactic used by Infantino.

“Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning Fifa and its president,” a spokesperson said. “Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

“Fifa welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress.

“Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, Fifa will challenge it directly and vigorously. Fifa’s responsibility is to its 211 member associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our member associations and continuing the work of making football truly global.”

Sports.title: Mason Mount injury overshadows Manchester United’s draw with PSG
Sports.content:
Manchester United managed a creditable 1-1 draw with the European champions, Paris Saint-Germain, in a Gothenburg friendly on Saturday but the result was overshadowed by an injury to Mason Mount.

The England midfielder, who joined United from Chelsea in 2023, has been hampered by injury problems since arriving at Old Trafford and he lasted fewer than 20 minutes after starting against PSG.

Mount, 27, appeared to suffer a foot injury in Sweden and, after discussions with coaches on the touchline, left the field to be replaced by Tyler Fletcher. Mount has been restricted to 54 league appearances – many of them as a substitute – during his first three seasons with United.

“He got kicked,” ⁠Carrick told reporters of Mount. “We just wanted to be careful and look after him. ‌We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.“

His side were 1-0 down to PSG at the time of his injury, having gone behind in the second minute through an Ibrahim Mbaye goal even though the French giants were missing many of their star players.

But Bryan Mbeumo equalised in the 32nd minute when Amad Diallo played him in after winning the ball back.

There were more injury concerns for United early in the second half when their 40-year-old goalkeeper Tom Heaton suffered a right hamstring problem while rushing out to make a clearance.

Mbeumo might have doubled his tally but for the fine form of PSG’s Matvey Safonov but the goalkeeper left the pitch to jeers after escaping punishment for clattering into Joshua Zirkzee way outside his area – an incident that may well have led to him being punished in a competitive match.

There were late chances for Fletcher, Shea Lacey and the captain, Bruno Fernandes, who linked up well with new arrival Youri Tielemans in an encouraging sign for the United manager, Michael Carrick.

View image in fullscreen Mason Mount (back right) started the friendly in Gothenburg but had to be removed with an apparent injury. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

“I enjoyed it,” Carrick told MUTV, United’s in-house television station. “Good challenge. Slightly different with the way they play. We should’ve scored more goals.

“It’s good for the boys sometimes to have to problem-solve and find their own way and I thought we did that. That prepares them for the season as well. In that respect there were a lot of things that maybe people don’t always see that we were quite happy with. There were some good signs there.”

United have two more friendly fixtures, against bitter rivals Leeds in Dublin on Wednesday and AC Milan in Wroclaw three days later, before launching their Premier League campaign away to newly promoted Hull on 22 August.

Sports.title: Premier League managers have never been less English, title-winning or secure in their jobs
Sports.content:
Nine of the 20 Premier League clubs will begin the 2026-27 season with a different man in the dugout than the one who ended the last campaign. The only other seasons which started with so many men making their managerial debut for top flight clubs were 1888-89 and 1946-47; the inaugural season of league football and the first following the second world war. Neither occurred under normal circumstances yet the level of turnover this summer does not feel unusual. Job security has never meant less in the Premier League. Adding in the recently appointed pair of Roberto De Zerbi and Michael Carrick – confirmed in March and May respectively – means 11 teams are led by coaches with less than a year in their hotseat. The median tenure of Premier League managers at the start of each season has never been so low.

The most recent similar season was 2016-17. Heading into that campaign, 10 clubs had managers with less than one year in the role. But with respect to the current Premier League crop, the relatively new head coaches that summer included Antonio Conte, Pep Guardiola, Jürgen Klopp and José Mourinho. All had either already won the Premier League or would go on to do so.

With Arsène Wenger still at Arsenal, four of those considered the five big beasts of Premier League management were present, with the other (Alex Ferguson) having retired three years earlier. By contrast, Mikel Arteta is the only man who has won the English league who will be starting 2026-27 with the chance to do so again. There was also only one such manager two years ago, albeit it was Guardiola with his bulging trophy cabinet.

As Arteta has a single championship win, this season begins with the fewest English league titles on the division’s collective CV in the Premier League era. The previous lowest at the beginning of a campaign was three in 1995-96 (thanks to Ferguson having two and Howard Wilkinson one) and 2019-20 (Guardiola two, Manuel Pellegrini one).

This is a natural byproduct of managers being younger and less experienced. The median age of Premier League managers is 46.9 years old. It was the same heading into 2024-25 but was last younger 20 years ago. The drop in age has not led to further opportunities for Englishmen.

Eddie Howe’s departure from Newcastle means there will be three English managers when 2026-27 gets under way. The total was the same at the start of the last two campaigns, though interestingly it will be a different trio this year (Carrick, Frank Lampard and Gary O’Neil) than 12 months ago (Howe, Scott Parker and Graham Potter). The standing of the six clubs led by these men is worth considering. Two of the current coaches are at teams that have just been promoted, while two from last season’s group were with sides that went on to be relegated. Opportunities with relatively secure Premier League clubs are now rare for English managers, never mind at those with realistic title ambitions.

The top end of the division is likely to have a Spanish feel. The Basque region of Gipuzkoa is providing more head coaches to England’s top division than England, with Arsenal, Aston Villa, Chelsea and Liverpool led by men from that relatively small area of Spain. It’s plausible none of them will win the league given the presence of Manchester City (who themselves are under new management after a decade of Guardiola) but Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola are in charge of three of the leading four clubs in the title betting market, with Unai Emery’s Villa seventh.

Managers from overseas lessening opportunities for English coaches in the Premier League is simply following the trend on the pitch: Just 8.6% of available minutes went to players from outside Britain or Ireland in 1992-93 yet a new high of 69.6% was reached last season. It is a truly global competition at every level, including ownership and sporting directors.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The influence of the latter on recruitment decisions has blurred the line between being a head coach and a manager. Liam Rosenior said he was “extremely humbled and honoured to be appointed head coach of Chelsea” when he was appointed by the Blues in January. “It fills me with immense pride to become manager of this great club,” was Xabi Alonso’s line when he secured essentially the same gig less than six months later. Based on the announcements clubs made to herald news of their appointments, the Premier League currently employs 14 head coaches and six managers.

Regardless of what the sign says on Alonso’s office door, he should reflect upon his new club giving him a four-year contract when they haven’t kept a manager for as long as two years since Conte left in 2018, or three years since Mourinho’s first spell in charge more than a decade earlier.

Rosenior learned this the hard way. He signed a six-and-a-half year deal yet Chelsea previously employed both Rafael Benítez and Guus Hiddink on interim bases for longer than the young Englishman lasted at the club. Head coach or manager, call it what you will. The profession has never offered shorter-term employment, or felt less English, in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Versatile Bruno Guimarães gives Mikel Arteta options to shuffle midfield pack | Ed Aarons
Sports.content:
If there was one of his many assets Newcastle supporters grew to love above all about Bruno Guimarães then it was best summed up by the man himself after being unveiled as Arsenal’s new £75m signing. “That’s a tough one,” said the Brazil midfielder when asked what fans in north London can expect from him. “I would say I can pass the ball, run a lot and play like a warrior. I’ll never give up.”

After more than four years on Tyneside and having seen Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali precede Eddie Howe’s departure, Guimarães – who was devastated after missing a penalty for the Seleção in their defeat against Norway in the last 16 of the World Cup – was determined to seize his opportunity.

While his emotional statement released by Newcastle as his move to Arsenal was confirmed on Saturday said they “did everything they could to keep me”, at the age of 28 he clearly felt it may never come again.

Andrea Berta’s pursuit of Vinícius Júnior came up short this week after the Brazil forward signed an improved six-year deal with Real Madrid. But at least Arsenal’s sporting director was finally able to bring in a player who was first courted by the club in the early days of Mikel Arteta’s reign, and who will add to the outstanding crop of central midfielders at his disposal.

Edu Gaspar, Berta’s predecessor, is understood to have first enquired about Guimarães when he was still at Athletico Paranaense in Brazil before he joined Lyon in the January 2020 transfer window – a few weeks after Arteta’s arrival at the Emirates.

They were also interested when Newcastle won the race to sign him in January 2022 for €40m, which came back to haunt Arsenal when he scored in a 2-0 win that went a long way to them missing out on Champions League qualification that season.

That first of nine appearances is the only time he scored against Arsenal, but Guimarães always impressed in a variety of roles whenever he came up against them, including in the Carabao Cup semi-final Newcastle won 4-0 on aggregate in 2025. He has covered more distance, won more duels and committed more fouls against Arsenal than any other side since making his Premier League debut.

It was no surprise that Declan Rice – the only player in the division to have covered more distance than Guimarães in that period and who enjoyed their fair share of battles – was one of the first to welcome him to Arsenal with a message that said “come here and please no more fights, now we’re friends”.

It is hard to argue with Guimarães that Arsenal have “one of the best midfields” in Europe because last season proved it. Yet having gone all the way to the Champions League final before spending the summer with England, after suffering with neural pain in his hamstring and lower back since December, Rice must be treated with the utmost care in the coming months. Guimarães can provide cover for him in a box-to-box role and gives Arteta options to rotate his other midfielders more frequently.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães will provide box-to-box cover for Declan Rice, rather than engage him in midfield combat. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

He did not seem to trust Christian Nørgaard, who has joined Everton, to deputise for Martín Zubimendi in the Premier League last year, and that led to the Spain midfielder running out of steam in the spring.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It was telling that the teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly started in his preferred position at the base of midfield during the title run-in, and against Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest for the Champions League final, having begun the campaign as a left-back. Guimarães showed at Newcastle he is capable of playing in a deeper role as well and Arteta must decide how to balance his plethora of options in a crucial part of the pitch.

While he could not match Mikel Merino’s goalscoring exploits for Spain,Martin Ødegaard showed signs that he is back to his best during the World Cup after another disappointing season for Arsenal that was again interrupted by injury.

Having missed out on Morgan Rogers, the onus will be on the Norway captain, Guimarães and last summer’s big signing, Eberechi Eze, to provide some creativity to an attack that struggled to break down the low block at times last season.

Arsenal are still in the market for a defender to cover the absence of William Saliba for an extended period, while they would like to bring in another forward to add to the signing of Christos Tzolis. Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez or Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain would fit the bill, although it remains to be seen if they will bring in a marquee player without offloading Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus – who has interest from Napoli. Even if they do depart, the presence of another familiar face in the Brazil centre-back Gabriel should also help Guimarães settle into his new home.

“Big Gabi was very excited,” he told Arsenal’s website. “Every time he sent me the message: ‘We’ll wait for you, when will you come?’ I’m so excited to join them, not only the Brazilians, we have an amazing squad here. I’m so excited to meet the other players, to start training. I just want to give my best.”

Sports.title: Rangers star stretchered off hours after club record transfer bid rejected
Sports.content:
Rangers star stretchered off hours after club record transfer bid rejected

Add us as preferred source

Youssef Chermiti was stretchered off during Rangers' match against Hibernian on Sunday.

The striker was replaced by Ryan Naderi after 36 minutes at Ibrox.

3 Chermiti was stretchered off hours after Rangers rejected a club-record bid Credit: PA



It came just hours after Galatasaray saw a bid rejected for the 22-year-old.

According to Sky Sports, the offer would have represented a club-record sale for Rangers.

Their current record of £19million was set in 2023 by Calvin Bassey's move to Ajax.

According to reports in Turkey, Galatasarsay's verbal approach was worth €25million (£21.5m).



However, Rangers rejected the offer, with their valuation of Chermiti closer to €40million (£34.3m).

Any potential move now looks in doubt after an injury setback for the Portugal Under-21 international.



Chermiti was stretchered off before half time after suffering a nasty-looking injury having fallen by the advertising hoardings on the byline at Ibrox.

He had stayed down off the pitch after chasing down a loose ball in front of goal.



His withdrawal came after the hosts had conceded a 12th minute penalty to trail against Hibs.

Josh Campbell converted from 12 yards to open the scoring and heap further pressure on Derek McInnes.

3 Chermiti suffered a nasty-looking injury after colliding with the pitchside advertising boards Credit: PA

A late own goal from Miguel Chaiwa appeared to have rescued a point for Rangers.



However, Callum Wright grabbed a 93rd minute winner as the home side suffered their first league defeat of the season.

It means McInnes is still awaiting his first win as Rangers manager since joining from Hearts this summer.

His side were held by Dundee United on the opening weekend of the season before losing to Jagiellonia Bialystok in the Europa League on Thursday.

Chermiti at Rangers

Chermiti signed for Rangers from Everton on a four-year deal last summer.



He had previously spent seven years with Sporting Lisbon in his native Portugal after joining the club's academy in 2016.

3 Galatasaray's £21.5million bid for Chermiti has been rejected Credit: PA

The forward has also been capped by his country up to Under-21 level.

Since joining Rangers, Chermiti has scored 15 goals in 42 appearances for the club.

Sports.title: Arsenal wonderkid tipped to be better than Ethan Nwaneri and fulfil his potential
Sports.content:
Arsenal wonderkid tipped to be better than Ethan Nwaneri and fulfil his potential

Max Dowman is destined to live up to his potential - he's only going to get better and will be given more chances to shine.

That's the view of Arsenal cult hero Perry Groves, who rubbished any speculation that the 16-year-old could grow impatient over game time in the coming months.



4 Arsenal starlet Dowman is considered to be one of the world's top prospects Credit: Getty

Dowman enjoyed a record-breaking breakthrough 2025/26 season in which he become the youngest player to win the Premier League.

The versatile teenager, who can operate as both a right winger or attacking midfielder, also holds the record as the youngest goalscorer in competition.

That is in addition to being the youngest player to start a Premier League game, while also being the youngest to feature in the Champions League - doing so aged 15 and 308 days old.



In total, Dowman featured 13 times last campaign as Arsenal ended 22 years of top-flight woe, with the player since featuring heavily in pre-season.

With Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke yet to be involved in pre-season action having been given an extended break following England's run to the World Cup semi-finals, Dowman could start in next week's Community Shield clash against Manchester City.



To the Max

Arsenal and England fans are hopeful he can be the future of the two teams in the years to come.

But speaking on the Sunday Session, legendary broadcaster Ian 'The Moose' Abrahams questioned whether Dowman will become frustrated in the upcoming season.



He argued that he may struggle to deal with Saka and Madueke ahead of him in the pecking order as he continues to force his way into Mikel Arteta's thinking.

Abrahams likened his situation to that of fellow Hale End graduate Ethan Nwaneri's, insisting the 19-year-old opted to join Marseille on loan January because of a lack of first-team chances.

Nwaneri was considered Arsenal's jewel of their academy when he became the Premier League youngest's player when he came on against Brentford in September 2022 at the age of 15 years and 181 days old.

4 Nwaneri was on target in Arsenal's Emirates Cup defeat to Borussia Dortmund on Sunday Credit: Getty



He then scored nine goals from 37 games during his breakthrough 2024/25 campaign, before falling down the pecking order last term.

But Groves insisted that Dowman is only going to be given more minutes by Arteta as he showcases his talent every time he graces the pitch.

He said: "It won't be a problem, Max Dowman when you compare [them], he's a different level to Nwaneri.

"I haven't seen a player of that age with that amount of natural ability.



"And the other thing with Max Dowman, normally players with that low centre of gravity and brilliant ball carriers, they're normally about 5ft 8in, 5ft 9in - he's 6ft tall - and he's got a bit of an edge.

"The game against Girona [4-1 pre-season win], where he scored a goal and made one, the goal that he scored, Alex Moreno, who used to play for Aston Villa, he was trying to rough him up.

4 Dowman and Nwaneri could battle for minutes against each other in the upcoming season for the Gunners Credit: Getty

"And Max Dowman palmed him off, he put a palm in his chest and Moreno fell on the floor and pretended like he had been hit on the head.



"So I must admit, I don't think that you're gonna have a problem with Max Dowman.

"He will get more minutes, he's always going to be on the bench, he'll play in the Carabao Cup games, so I can't see a problem with him this season at all."

Dowman distractions?

Abrahams once again raised concern that some of the country's greatest prospects have ultimately failed to live up to their early hype, as he pointed out off-field distractions could soon come into play.

He remarked: "I probably will be proved wrong in having any concerns about him, but I've done this job for 35 years.



"I've seen so many really good, unbelievable prospects, 'This guy is the best that this clubs ever produced' or 'This country has ever produced.'

4 Dowman wrote himself into the Premier League history books in March - becoming the youngest ever goalscorer Credit: Getty

"And for one reason or another, some of them may be footballing reasons, some of them may not be footballing reasons, it may not quite have happened for them.

"I hope this happens for him, I hope he becomes a Ballon d'Or winner in four or five years time, I hope he goes on to dominate for club and country.



"I think he has got pretty much everything, but he is only 16-and-a-half, he's still got to do several things which he hasn't even thought about yet.

"Growing, girls, cars, money... all those sorts of things don't matter to him at the moment, because all that matters to him is football and maybe his education up until now.

"But all those life things will come into play later on, and how will he deal with those?

"And I'm hoping that he'll be able to deal with it, so we can all say that this is the best player that England has ever produced."

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes labelled ‘just like Alexander Isak’ as new Arsenal signing slammed for Newcastle exit
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes labelled ‘just like Alexander Isak’ as new Arsenal signing slammed for Newcastle exit

Bruno Guimaraes shouldn't have been able to engineer a nice Newcastle exit - his departure was no different to Alexander Isak.

That is the view from talkSPORT's Inside The Toon host Shaun Custis, who believes the former Magpies captain conned the fans into believing that he was embedded as part of the Geordie nation.



5 Bruno Guimaraes was presented to Arsenal fans ahead of the club's 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund Credit: Getty

Guimaraes has officially completed a £75million move to Arsenal 34 months into the five-year contract extension he signed at St James' Park in October 2023.

The 28-year-old had agreed personal terms with the Gunners by the start of July and made steps to ensure the deal got over the line.

The Brazil international used super agent Kia Joorabchian to act as an intermediary to handle a lot of the day-to-day negotiating.



Such moves helped knock down Newcastle's original £100m valuation of their captain, while Guimaraes also asked the club to delay his pre-season travel plans as a switch to north London edged closer.

After the deal was confirmed, the midfielder released an emotional statement labelling his Toon exit as one of his toughest decisions.



However, talkSPORT host and Magpies fan Custis took a withering verdict of the post, considering it's stark contrast to his smiley-faced unveiling at his new club.

He told Sunday Edition: "Looks really upset to be joining Arsenal, because he also released a video which Newcastle United put out of being upset about leaving Newcastle and how sad he was and how he was half-Geordie, half-Brazilian, and we've achieved great things together. So he's leaving..."



Custis was then asked whether the transfer was harder to swallow from someone like Guimaraes, who even had a Newcastle-esque tattoo on his calf to commemorate the club's Carabao Cup triumph in 2025.

He replied: "I think it's harder when you get the, 'I'm a Geordie', you've kissed the badge, 'I'm the captain, I love you, we're embedded here, it's part of my life,' et cetera, et cetera, et cetera.

5 Arsenal have completed one of the most high-profile signings of the summer Credit: Getty

"Let's not pretend he's just wanting to leave now because Eddie [Howe] left. He wanted to leave before the end of the season.



"We knew this was bubbling up. He was getting ready."

Guimaraes claimed that his Newcastle exit came down to a 'difference of ideas' between himself and the club.

Asked whether Howe, who departed the Toon by mutual consent last month, would have stayed had his captain not been part of the recent exodus of Tyneside stars, Custis replied: "No, not particularly.

"I think he'd run his course. I don't think that necessarily. I get they're going a bit of a different direction, but you also need some experience as well.

"And we were, as usual, conned into believing that Bruno was embedded as part of the Geordie nation."



5 Guimaraes earned 'adopted Geordie' status at Newcastle Credit: Getty

No better than Isak?

Guimaraes, who scored 30 goals and registered 25 assists in 153 Premier League appearances for Newcastle, led the dressing room charge against former teammate Isak 12 months ago.

The Swede infamously posted a bombshell statement after being named in the PFA Premier League Team of the Year last August.

Isak referenced 'broken promises' at Newcastle and became public enemy No.1 at St James' when he sealed a British transfer record £125m switch to Liverpool on deadline day.



Just minutes after the striker's public statement, Guimaraes made his feelings clear by uploading a picture of himself in Newcastle's kit.

Custis admitted he's at a loss to explain how Guimaraes has now engineered a nice departure as opposed to an Isak-type departure.

5 This is what Guimaraes posted on social media shortly after Isak released his statement on why he wanted to leave last summer Credit: Instagram

5 He has now followed the Swedish striker in leaving Tyneside for another Premier League club Credit: Getty



"Of course he is [more likely to win things at Arsenal]. But why sign a long contract then, saying you're going to stay?

"It really does bother me this bit - [That fans believe that] there is much difference between what he did and what Isak did.

"Isak wanted to go, told Newcastle he wanted to go, but they said, 'No, you can't unless we get big, big money for you.'

"So he couldn't move. Bruno says, 'I want to go.' And they go, 'All right then, you can go.'



"Even though the manager says we didn't want to let him go. And there was no question in our planning of allowing him to go.

"But he has somehow managed to engineer a nice departure as opposed to an Isak-type departure.

"Don't pretend you're embedded in the nation and that you wouldn't want to be anywhere else and all of that."

Sports.title: Inside Marcus Rashford’s Man United return as he lands new squad number ahead of awkward reunion
Sports.content:
Inside Marcus Rashford’s Man United return as he lands new squad number ahead of awkward reunion

Marcus Rashford could make his long-awaited return to action for Manchester United this week.

The forward has not played for the Red Devils since December 2024 having lost his place under former manager Ruben Amorim.



3 Rashford could make his first United appearance since December 2024 on Wednesday Credit: Getty

Rashford has since enjoyed loan spells at Aston Villa and Barcelona across the last 18 months.

The 28-year-old could be set to appear for United on Wednesday, though.

Rashford return

He has joined up with the squad in the Republic of Ireland ahead of their pre-season friendly against Leeds United.



Rashford was given extended time off following his World Cup exploits earlier this summer.

United face their Premier League rivals at Croke Park in Dublin, with kick-off at 7:30pm.



They then conclude their preparations for the new season against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland on Saturday.

Rashford could face an awkward reunion with Amorim if he features against the Italian giants.



Milan appointed Amorim as manager in June, five months on from his Old Trafford exit.

The Portuguese coach handed Rashford just six appearances during his time as United boss, with the England international scoring three goals.

However, he was dropped by Amorim before being loaned to Villa in February 2025.

3 Rashford has joined up with his United teammates in Ireland Credit: Getty



His subsequent spell at Barcelona saw Rashford score 14 goals and provide 14 assists in 49 appearances across all competitions.

Barca also won the LaLiga title, but opted to sign Anthony Gordon from Newcastle instead of triggering Rashford's buy clause.

According to Fabrizio Romano, Rashford will be given the No.14 shirt upon his United return.

The shirt number was most recently worn by Christian Eriksen between 2022 and 2025.



Rashford had previously been United's No.10, but the shirt was given to Matheus Cunha upon his arrival at the club last summer.

talkSPORT verdict

talkSPORT's Perry Groves believes it is down to Michael Carrick whether Rashford plays for United this season.

3 Rashford is set for a reunion with former United boss Amorim against Milan on Saturday Credit: Getty

Appearing on Sunday Session with Sam Ellard, he was asked if the academy graduate will still be at the club when the transfer window closes.



Groves replied: "Well, that’ll be up to Michael Carrick. That’s because Man United played really well last season, ended up coming third and Michael Carrick got them out of trouble."

Comparing Rashford to Gordon, he added: "Michael Carrick came in and he had a football brain and just simplified it all and he quite frankly now has more say who’s going in and who’s going out.

"So with Marcus Rashford it’s, I think, really interesting for Man United fans because if you had the top Marcus Rashford and the top Anthony Gordon, at their peak, Marcus Rashford beats Gordon every single time on productivity from that left hand side.

"You know how good he is, but Man United fans have got to try and process the way he left and played there, when he wasn’t running about. You could say his body language was awful.



"We don’t know what was going on off the pitch rather than on it because he didn’t look like as a person he was in the best space.

"And he played the ‘you shouldn’t have a go at me because it really hurts me because I’m a product of the academy,’ played that card.

"You’re like, ‘well if it means that much to you, run around and give it everything you’ve got.’"

Sports.title: Newcastle could hijack Aston Villa transfer and get revenge for Johan Manzambi saga
Sports.content:
Newcastle could hijack Aston Villa transfer and get revenge for Johan Manzambi saga

Newcastle will rival Aston Villa in the race to sign Bayern Munich midfielder Joao Palhinha, talkSPORT understands.

The 31-year-old has returned to Bayern Munich having spent the 2025/26 season on loan at Tottenham.

2 Bayern midfielder Palhinha could be in line for another move to the Premier League Credit: Getty

Palhinha chipped in with seven goals and three assists from 45 games across all competitions.

And it was the Portugal international's strike in the 1-0 win over Everton on the final game of the campaign that kept Spurs in the Premier League.

However, despite becoming a fan favourite in north London, Roberto De Zerbi's side decided against activating his £26million buy option.

While he has been involved in pre-season duty for Bayern, the club have made it clear he is not in their long-term plans.

The club's director of sport, Max Eberl, named the ex-Fulham star as one of three players the Bundesliga champions are willing to sell.

Joao about that?

A return to England could now be in the offing, with Villa in talks to sign the player as they look to bolster their midfield having sold Youri Tielemans, while Amadou Onana suffered an ACL injury on World Cup duty.

Villans director of football Damian Vidagany recently told Bild: "We are in talks, but there is currently no agreement.

"I believe Aston Villa would be a great club for him."

Though talkSPORT understands that Newcastle are also keen, with the two clubs set to be involved in another transfer battle following the Johan Manzambi saga earlier this window.

Newcastle had agreed a £51.2m deal with Hoffenheim to sign the Switzerland international, only for the Villans to hijack the deal.

2 Palhinha featured in 33 Premier League matches last season - starting on 23 occasions

Like Villa, the Toon have made it a priority to strengthen their midfield having sold skipper Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali for a combined £175million.

And Palhinha has been identified as a real option for new boss Matthias Jaissle, as he looks to add much-needed experience to his squad.

So far, Newcastle have made two midfield signings in Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba, but both are aged 20 or below.

Newcastle also remain interested in another former Spurs star in Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg.

Talks are being held to sign the 31-year-old, who had his loan stay at Marseille from Spurs turned into a permanent switch last summer.

Believed to be available for between £10m-£15m, Hojbjerg boasts a wealth of Premier League experience having played 254 top-flight games in his career.

Sports.title: ‘Very fulfilled’ ex-Bundesliga and USMNT coach gives up soccer to run three McDonald’s restaurants
Sports.content:
Nouri shared the sideline with Klinsmann and Berhalter, but feels more fulfilled now he's managing McDonald's restaurants day-to-day

‘Very fulfilled’ ex-Bundesliga and USMNT coach gives up soccer to run three McDonald’s restaurants

For many people, little in life would come close to coaching your boyhood team. But for Alexander Nouri, managing McDonald's restaurants might just top that feeling.

Following a 13-year professional soccer career, in which he played mostly in the German lower leagues and also had a brief spell with the Seattle Sounders, Nouri took up coaching.

4 Former soccer coach Nouri now runs McDonald's restaurants Credit: Getty

He earned his licence in 2016, alongside former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann, who was top of the class.

Nouri had a stint as head coach at Werder Bremen, and helped his boyhood team escape a relegation battle before turning them into contenders for European football.

He then took roles with FC Ingolstadt and Hertha BSC, before landing as assistant coach to Gregg Berhalter with the US Men’s National Team in 2021.

But around a year later, following a short stint with Greek third-tier side Kavala, Nouri called time on soccer.

In the years since, he's swapped the touchline for a titan of the fast food industry.

Former USMNT assistant swaps coaching soccer for McDonald's management

"It didn’t feel right anymore," Nouri said of coaching soccer, in a recent interview with The Athletic.

"And the job is so demanding that it needs 100 per cent of you. If you do it with 98 per cent, it’s not right."

Instead of throwing himself back into professional sports, Nouri has recently found something new to put his energy into: Running three branches of McDonald’s in north-west Germany.

"I just felt at this moment, this was the end of that life story (in football). And so I have to begin something new," he explained.

"It wasn’t a decision only of myself. It was a decision with my family, and we made it together after years of constant moves and uncertainty in professional soccer.

4 Nouri runs three branches of McDonald's in north-west Germany Credit: Getty

"We felt it was the right time to build a more stable future together."

To become a McDonald's franchisee, Nouri went through a tough application process.

It took around a year, and included several rounds of interviews, training for the new role and a five-hour assessment, which required the former USMNT assistant to come up with a business plan.

Nouri passed all those tests, and took charge of his first two restaurants in January.

He added a third in June, and now has around 150 employees.

In overseeing the three chains, Nouri sees plenty of similarities with soccer, and often applies some of the lessons he learned as a coach.

4 Nouri has taken lessons learned from the likes of Klinsmann into his new role Credit: Getty

"I was lucky to experience all of these great things, like working alongside Jurgen Klinsmann. Gregg Berhalter is a good friend of mine; he taught me lessons that continue to shape my leadership today," Nouri told The Athletic.

"I learned a lot from these guys. I learned from Jurgen to have your confidence and your point of view, but always challenge it with different angles or perspectives, and then good things come together if you have different perspectives and, at the end, make a decision.

"The ‘growth mindset’, I learned from Jurgen and from Gregg. They always brought external expertise into the organisations to challenge their own processes and everything, and to experience that alongside those personalities was learning for me.

"And that helps me now in my job right now as well."

4 Nouri coached now Bayern Munich and Germany star Gnaby at Werder Bremen Credit: Getty

Soccer coaching is often seen as the pinnacle. But for Nouri, managing McDonald's is more rewarding. He even has time to help run youth tournaments, for the next generation of stars.

"I’m very fulfilled in myself. I have a clear vision, to be able to work towards this vision with people you love, with your family; that’s something very special," he said.

"I believe in karma. I really want to be a good employer. I love what I’m doing."

Sports.title: £42m star removed from team moments before kick-off in decision that could provide Liverpool transfer boost
Sports.content:
£42m star removed from team moments before kick-off in decision that could provide Liverpool transfer boost

Paris Saint-Germain transfer target Mika Godts was forced out of Ajax's first Eredivisie game mere minutes before kick-off took place.

The Belgian wonderkid, who has been dubbed the ‘next Eden Hazard’, could inadvertently spark a transfer merry-go-round with his future.

3 Godts went through his full pre-match warm-up routine before pulling out Credit: Getty

The 21-year-old, previously tipped for stardom by Lionel Messi, has been actively pursued by PSG since the end of last month.

Luis Enrique's side have already strengthened in wide attacking areas this summer, having signed Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco.

Despite this, PSG are still eyeing a deal for Godts, which may suggest that the club are anticipating at least one of their own to leave.

talkSPORT previously revealed that Liverpool are plotting an audacious double transfer raid on the Champions League winners for wingers Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye.

A move for either one of the PSG stars would appear much more feasible should Godts join the Ligue 1 champions, who already have Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Desire Doue, and now Akliouche on their books.

And speculation that Godts could be on the brink of a transfer ramped up after his omission from Ajax's first match on Sunday.

Fabrizio Romano reported two days ago that PSG are set to offer €45million (38.6m) fixed fee plus add-ons for a package in excess of €50m (£42m).

No risks taken on Godts amid PSG transfer interest

The Belgium international was named in Míchel's starting XI for their opening Eredivisie game of the 2026/27 season.

However, Godts was a late withdrawal, with Ajax posting on social media that the reason was that 'he was not fit enough to start.'

ESPN cameras from the dressing room showed Ajax's No.11 wearing his match shirt and having a private chat with his manager before the decision was made for Abdellah Ouazane to be named as his replacement.

3 Godts has attracted serious interest from PSG as they plan on further upgrading their wing options Credit: Getty

It is yet to be confirmed what injury Godts sustained and how long his potential absence could be if negotiations with PSG drag on.

Ajax head coach Michel addressed the rumours surrounding his talisman's future before kick-off when he looked set to play.

"I see a happy player and someone who trains well," the former Girona chief told reporters.

"I don't know exactly what is going through his head because of all those rumours, but I see that he is ready to give one hundred per cent today and help us win the match."

Godts was a rare bright spark for Ajax last season, registering 17 goals and 12 assists in 31 appearances to earn a senior Belgium call-up.

He was a surprise omission from his country's final World Cup squad, with Rudi Garcia leaving his post after they lost 2-1 to Spain in the quarter-finals, and Mark van Bommel has since taken the reins.

3 Liverpool are hopeful of completing a double deal for PSG pair Barcola and Mbaye Credit: Getty

Liverpool transfer latest

The Reds will be keen to make inroads on improving their attacking options as they edge closer to announcing Ronald Araujo's arrival.

talkSPORT revealed on Friday that Liverpool have agreed a loan deal to bring the 27-year-old Barcelona captain to Anfield.

He is set to be the latest new face on Merseyside this summer, with Jeremy Jacquet officially completing his move from Rennes after a deal for the 21-year-old was agreed earlier this year.

Liverpool have since unveiled the signing of Spain's Victor Munoz, having hijacked Newcastle's move for the World Cup winner.

Sports.title: Arsenal star cuts holiday short and trains before pre-season game despite not being in squad
Sports.content:
Arsenal star cuts holiday short and trains before pre-season game despite not being in squad

David Raya has given Arsenal a huge boost ahead of next week's Community Shield by cutting short his holiday to return to training.

The 30-year-old was given an extended break by the Gunners having been part of Spain's squad that won the World Cup in July.



4 Raya is back training having cut short his holiday ahead of the new season Credit: Getty

Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi were all due to report back next week after lifting football's biggest trophy.

FIFA rules state that players involved in tournaments are allowed a minimum of three weeks rest period.

The Gunners had eight players who made it to the final weekend of the World Cup.



The Spain trio were joined by the England quartet of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke, and Eberechi Eze.

William Saliba was also involved for France, but he will be sidelined for a significant period.



This would have put their earliest return at August 10.

But goalkeeper Raya was spotted back training on the Emirates pitch ahead of Sunday's pre-season clash against Borussia Dortmund.

However, the former Brentford shot-stopper was omitted from the matchday squad for the Emirates Cup fixture.



And he watched on helplessly from the stands as the Bundesliga outfit broke the deadlock early on through Samuele Inacio.

Dortmund then doubled their lead on the half-hour mark as Kepa was beaten from range following Konstantinos Karetsas's long range stunner.

4 Raya won the World Cup alongside Arsenal teammates Merino and Zubimendi Credit: Getty

Kepa Arrizabalaga has now shipped in five first half goals in a matter of a days having conceded three times in Wednesday's 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin.



Speaking after the 3-2 defeat to Dortmund, boss Mikel Arteta also declared that Saka has reported back for training early.

He said: "Bukayo was here yesterday, a bit earlier than expected, which is great to see.

"I think it's a really good sign, and tomorrow everybody will be available to start the training programme."

A Ray of hope

With Raya and Saka already back in training, they could both involved in Wednesday's final pre-season game against Como in north London.



Cesc Fabregas returns to his former stomping ground as an opposing manager for the first time in his career.

4 Raya is regarded as one of the world's top goalkeepers Credit: Getty

And attention will then switch to the first silverware on offer, with Premier League champions Arsenal to battle FA Cup holders Manchester City in the Community Shield in Cardiff next Sunday.

Arsenal boast a brilliant record in the annual curtain-raiser having lifted the trophy on 17 occasions, with only Manchester United winning it more times [21].



They have won each of their last five Community Shield matches - with two coming against the Citizens.

The latest came in 2023, with Leandro Trossard scoring a late equaliser to send the game to penalties - which Arsenal won 4-1.

Gunning for history

Raya goes into the 2026/27 campaign on the cusp of creating Premier League history.

The ex-Blackburn man has won three consecutive Golden Glove awards having kept 48 clean sheets in his last three seasons.



4 Raya won the World Cup alongside Arsenal teammates Merino and Zubimendi Credit: Getty

Only Joe Hart and Petr Cech [both four] have won the honour more times.

However, Raya can become the first goalkeeper to win the award in four straight years.

Sports.title: Chelsea's pre-season friendly against Malaysian side descends into farce - with players leaving pitch and fans denied penalty shootout that was 'written in the contract'
Sports.content:
Chelsea's pre-season friendly against Johor Darul Ta’zim of Malaysia ended in bizarre fashion after opposition players left the field against an apparent agreement.

The Blues were playing their second friendly game of the weekend at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, with the match finishing 3-3 following what was, at times, an ill-tempered affair.

Liam Delap had scored twice for the Blues, with an own goal in the 89th minute ensuring Xabi Alonso's second-string side drew the match.

After 90 minutes, supporters inside the ground waited for a penalty shootout, as has been the way with a number of games in pre-season – but that never happened.

Johor Darul Ta’zim opted to leave the field rather than prepare for the spot kick, with Chelsea head of first team operations, Kevin Campello, heard saying it was 'written in the contract'.

The shootout, though, never took place, with no official explanation as to why.

Chelsea were due to take on Johor Darul Ta’zim of Malaysia in a penalty shootout after their friendly on Sunday

The Blues were left confused as their opponents left the field after full-time against an apparent agreement

Shootouts have been taking place in a number of games even when there is a positive result in 90 minutes, with Arsenal beating Borussia Dortmund on penalties at the Emirates on Sunday despite losing the game 3-2.

Not many first-choice players had played in the game, with the likes of Estevao and Liam Delap some of the only senior pros involved.

Midfielder Dario Essugo captained the side, after another team had beaten Ruben Amorim's AC Milan 3-0 the day before.

That team included the likes of Cole Palmer and Moises Caicedo, while Joao Pedro scored twice in the game to continue his impressive pre-season form.

The Blues will take on Spanish side Real Sociedad next Saturday in their final pre-season game, before visiting Fulham for their first match of the new season the following week.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford returns to Man United nearly TWO years after last appearance - but he still faces an uncertain future ahead of his reintegration
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford returns to Man United nearly TWO years after last appearance - but he still faces an uncertain future ahead of his reintegration

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Marcus Rashford has joined up with Manchester United's squad in Ireland as he faces up to the prospect of being reintegrated at his boyhood club.

While it is still far from certain that Rashford remains at United following the summer transfer window's deadline of 11pm on September 1, the England international has now joined up with team-mates at their Ireland training camp just outside of Dublin.

Rashford, 28, spent last season on loan at Barcelona and has not played for United since December 12, 2024, when he fell out of favour under then-head coach Ruben Amorim.

For a long while it appeared that Rashford, who returns to the United fold having won LaLiga last season in Spain, was never going to play for United again but that hard-line stance appears to have softened in recent weeks and months and it is now seen as a viable option for him to become part of Michael Carrick's plans.

After arriving at United's Carrington training base on Sunday following a three-week break after the FIFA World Cup, Rashford, along with eight of his team-mates, jetted out to Maynooth to join up with United's 22-man squad which drew 1-1 with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on Saturday.

United's hierarchy have long been open to letting Rashford leave but his £325,000-a-week salary, which was agreed when he signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford in 2023, has proven prohibitive, especially after Barcelona passed up on the opportunity to make his loan permanent and instead signed his England team-mate Anthony Gordon.

Marcus Rashford has returned to Man United, nearly two years after his last appearance

Rashford is pictured back in Manchester United's training kit on Sunday in Dublin, Ireland

Barcelona sought a second loan for this upcoming season and that was flatly denied by United, paving the way for Rashford to return to United's set-up.

But sources close to Rashford maintain that it is not a guarantee he will start the season with United and that all options remain on the table.

Daily Mail Sport previously revealed that a number of clubs from the Premier League – including two with a particular interest – as well as from Italy, Germany, Turkey and Saudi Arabia are still weighing up a move, most likely on loan.

But Rashford is not interested in Turkey and Saudi Arabia as landing spots.

Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and his United career appeared to be over

Rashford posed for photos with fans and signed memorabilia as he arrived at United's base

Carrick is an admirer of Rashford and given United have been in the market for a left winger all summer - Crysencio Summerville, one of the players on United's list, joined Al-Hilal for £68million from West Ham this window - and his presence in the dugout has elevated the prospect of Rashford's reintegration.

Wednesday night's game against Leeds United in Dublin will come too soon but Rashford, who arrived in Ireland on Sunday afternoon alongside Matheus Cunha, who was handed Rashford's No 10 squad number upon arrival from Wolves, Senne Lammens, Kobbie Mainoo, Karl Darlow, Matthijs de Ligt, Benjamin Sesko, JJ Gabriel and summer signing from Tottenham Hotspur, Tynan Thompson, will be back involved in full squad training with United for the first time in more than 18 months.

It means that Rashford's return in a United shirt could well come against AC Milan, now managed by Amorim, the manager who cut him loose, in Poland next weekend.
