Sports.title: Andoni Iraola's football is tailor-made for Alexander Isak but Liverpool's defence looks completely unprepared for Premier League season - with ineligible teen star impressing again in 3-2 defeat by Monaco
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola's football is tailor-made for Alexander Isak but Liverpool's defence looks completely unprepared for Premier League season - with ineligible teen star impressing again in 3-2 defeat by Monaco

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Alexander Isak has done very little to justify his British record transfer fee after moving from Newcastle United to Liverpool for £125million last summer.

In fairness, he's been plagued by injuries - breaking his leg just three months into his Liverpool career. But even when he did feature, he looked a shadow of his former self - beleaguered by the weight of his transfer fee and struggling for sharpness.

Last term, he scored just four goals in 22 appearances. That said, those numbers are slightly skewed given he only played 1,033 minutes - the equivalent of 11 full 90s.

Making just his second pre-season appearance on Sunday after returning from the World Cup - where he scored once in four outings for Sweden - Isak gave a much stronger account of himself in a 3-2 defeat against Monaco.

Alexander Isak scored in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat against Monaco on Sunday

Helped by Andoni Iraola's dynamic one-touch football, Isak was much more involved in play than he was under Arne Slot. The 26-year-old capped off a scintillating Liverpool move, taking Ryan Gravenberch's lay-off in his stride and burying it into the bottom corner with his right foot from 18 yards.

It was a move of intricate detail, with five one-touch passes releasing Isak into space in the penalty area. Those moves are a hallmark of an Iraola team, playing into Isak's strengths as a lethal finisher and intelligent mover.

Gakpo makes his case

Cody Gakpo was an integral part of Liverpool's attack for an hour, despite being linked with a move to Premier League rivals Spurs. He was the catalyst for much of Liverpool's link-up play, kickstarting the tiki-taka football to create space.

The Dutchman also found himself in space at the far post and was denied by a great stop from Lukas Hradecky when attempting to convert Lewis Koumas' tempting cross. It was a lively performance on the left.

Cody Gakpo impressed for Liverpool as the Premier League season nears, despite being linked with a move to Spurs

Equally, on the opposite side, Koumas was given the nod over Rio Ngumoha and impressed as Iraola seeks solutions to replace Mohammed Salah. The 20-year-old was lively, registering four shots, constantly looking for the ball and dipping a nice cross into the penalty area. He is, though, a little raw. Federico Chiesa came on for the final 15 minutes.

Liverpool’s defence rings alarm bells (again)

Jeremy Jacquet was left out of the Liverpool side again as he continues his recovery from shoulder surgery. The 21-year-old arrived from Rennes in a £60million deal in July, having pre-agreed a move to Merseyside in January, but he has yet to feature in pre-season.

With Liverpool’s opening game of the season just 14 days away, his lack of minutes is a concern - particularly given the limited options available to play alongside Virgil van Dijk.

Liverpool only have Joe Gomez and Giovanni Leoni, both currently injured, to call upon as understudies after Ibrahima Konate left for Real Madrid. Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who started alongside van Dijk on Sunday, was not granted a work permit and will have to join a European club on loan. Wataru Endo also spent time at centre-back, but that should be a last resort during the season.

Their defensive woes were on show against Monaco, conceding three times to squander a two-goal lead. Liverpool were fragile at the back once van Dijk and Ndukwe made way. Their defence was weak last season, and that has yet to be rectified, albeit not helped by Jacquet's absence.

Liverpool's options at centre-back, beyond Virgil van Dijk, are increasingly limited

Liverpool are being proactive, however, making a move for Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona. His impending arrival cannot come soon enough and will be pivotal in securing the Liverpool backline.

His experience would add further solidity to a Liverpool defence that conceded 53 goals in the Premier League last season, while also ensuring they have sufficient depth should Jacquet’s recovery take longer than expected. He is an out-and-out defender, which will complement van Dijk well.

It is only pre-season, but Iraola has already made Liverpool a more entertaining attacking side. Now he needs to reinforce the defence.

Ndukwe's work permit blow

Liverpool will be frustrated that Ndukwe cannot form part of their centre-back contingent this season. The Austrian teenager, signed from Austria Wien, has dazzled during pre-season and did not look out of place partnering van Dijk in the Liverpool backline.

In a 45-minute showing against Monaco, he was composed, unbeaten in his duels and flawless on the ball. One turn on the ball, in particular, was astonishing. However, he is ineligible to play competitive fixtures in England as he does not yet qualify for a work permit.

Teenage defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe has a bright future at Anfield - but he needs to play abroad first to get a work permit

Competitive first-team appearances in a European top-flight will aid his case for a permit, which means he will spend this season - certainly the first half of it - out on loan to appease the Home Office. If this audition was anything to go by, he will have plenty of options.

Sports.title: Journey to Wembley: Daily Mail Sport's special 50th anniversary love letter to the FA Cup begins at 'Little Wembley', the home of Nelson FC - the ninth-tier side who were first EVER team to beat Real Madrid on home soil
Sports.content:
The ground at Nelson FC is called ‘Little Wembley’ and however resplendent the scene at its far grander namesake where the FA Cup final is played, 286 days and 600 or so games from now, it will do well to match the inestimable beauty of Saturday, when the arc of the old competition’s journey began once more.

The oasis of green in sun-starched east Lancashire has owed a lot to the club recently inviting the local fire service to carry out a practice drill which entailed spraying a lot of water on the pitch.

Limited supplies are also being piped a few hundred yards from Pendle Water, the river you cross to reach the ground, which once powered the local cotton mill, whose 200ft chimney and stone-built workers cottages form the backdrop to one of the tournament’s 208 Preliminary Qualifying Round ties.

By 11am groundsman Trevor Stamworth is marking out the pitch, which locals took to calling 'Little Wembley' decades back because of its quality. Staff are setting up in the little bar area, where sepia images provide reminders of Nelson’s small but very significant part in football history – a 4-2 win over Real Madrid in 1923, during a tour of Spain, which made them the first British side to beat the club on their own turf.

A couple of deckchairs are set out in the front gardens of the workers’ cottages which form a warm-up area beside the pitch and Nelson manager Arron Ripley arrives at 1pm to lay out the team’s jerseys in the dressing room and hone a pre-match pep-talk which will include him reminding his players that only one in 3,400 people in Britain get to play in the FA Cup, so they should seize this day.

‘You’re just looking for the small details that might get through,’ 32-year-old Ripley reflects as we sit in the dug-out, watching his players warm-up. ‘We look to put detail on things in many ways. ‘A friend of mine who’s an analyst, puts together clips for the players and we’ve got GPS vests for every game. Our video recorder’s broken at the moment, but we usually watch games back.’

Daily Mail Sport headed to Nelson for the opening round of FA Cup ties

Nelson's 'Little Wembley' ground perfectly captures the magic of the FA Cup

Groundsman Trevor Stamworth marks out the pitch ahead of the match against Stockport Georgians

This bucolic scene on a peerless summer’s day creates the impression that there has not been a cloud in Nelson’s sky, though the reality is very different. The club has been the subject of various failed ownership experiments in recent times, leading to the club being in a state of financial peril, two years ago. The lumpy pitch always flooded, the team lost almost every week and they got barely 50 through the gate.

This coincided with local businessmen Chris Price, who is in the industrial cleaning business, learning that it might be for sale. He and a friend Stewart Fort, an engineering entrepreneur, bought it for the best part of £30,000, and have together set out on a mission to build a thriving community club and take it from tier 10 to the tier eight Northern Premier League whilst doing so.

The fruits of their labour and invention are all around the place, from the new club shop and stand, both built out of converted shipping containers, the smart, timber-built food facility and the small ‘Sponsors Lounge’, where Fort is helping lay out the knives and forks at midday. Price and Fort estimate they’ve put in £700,000, so far, with the £162,000 the FA has contributed a testament to the role the governing body is not always given full credit for.

From a near certain plunge to the West Lancashire League – a relegation spared by another club folding – Nelson won promotion to the North West Counties Premier Division last season and have started the new campaign with a win. The talk is of promotion again. But roads to recovery are neither easy nor linear in football.

Despite the co-owners laying out £32,000 on pitch drainage and £52,000 on new dressing rooms, seven of the ground’s eight floodlights have suddenly failed and contractors are currently battling to get new cables laid and get those lights back on.

Nelson aim to have 260 paying fans through the turnstiles each week

Co-owners Chris Price and Stewart Fort - who bought the club for just shy of £30,000, have turned Nelson into a local success story

Nelson's ground is called Little Wembley due to the high-quality playing surface

Fans enjoyed beers pitchside on a glorious day in east Lancashire

Here, in a microcosm, is evidence of why the FA Cup, which seems to have become a minor consideration for football’s great and good, matters so very much. Price and Fort are not petro-dollar billionaires or captains of finance and while they find the money for capital projects, the football side of things must fund itself. The more advertising boards they sell, the more resource will be available to Ripley to find players who, at this level, are paid an average of £100 a week.

‘Reaching the First Round Proper would earn us nearly £25,000 and that would make a massive difference to us,’ says Fort, as he reflects on some of the unglamorous work of the past few years here, including shifting 27 tons of muck out of the goalmouths to create the flat surface he looks out across. ‘The bigger picture is finding the 260 or so people we aim to get through the turnstiles every week. But this competition is everything for us.’

Ripley feels the significance of the income just as acutely, given that Nelson’s new ambition puts him under the same pressure that every manager knows - and contributed to the club parting company with him, just before Christmas 2024. ‘They sacked me after we’d lost five games but after my replacement didn’t get us promoted, they brought me back and last season we managed it,’ he says, ‘So yes, there’s all the pressure that comes at any ambitious club.’

That promotion has delivered Nelson to this, their first FA Cup appearance since 2017, since tier nine clubs are the lowest level who enter. ‘Over £1,000 winnings if we win today and that all goes into pot,’ Ripley says.

His managerial ethos entails being ‘very locally-driven’, with only one of his squad living more than half an hour from Nelson, and putting the time in to knowing who you’re up against. Ripley is very much part-time, too – a digital project manager with filling station operator EG – but he watched opponents Stockport Georgians beat Wythenshawe Town in the Midland League Premier a few days earlier.

The preparation shows. Nelson are stronger and quicker to the ball and, vitally, have Sefton Gonzales, a powerful and combative centre forward who works as a storeman, in their ranks. They lead through Lewis Brown, one of a Nelson midfield tandem who dominate the early stages, though no manner of opposition scouting can quell Stockport’s Lucas Berry, a former Salford City academy player who leaves the home team’s defence standing as he equalises.

Nelson's Sefton Gonzales celebrates scoring the winner with a back-flip

The victory for the hosts set up a meeting with eighth-tier Witton Albion in the next round of the competition

The club have spent £52,000 on new dressing rooms

A compelling game of combative and technically proficient football evolves on the Little Wembley baize, and it morphs into a question of which of the two outstanding goalscoring threats - Gonzales or Berry – will ultimately prevail. Berry spins and scores again after Luke Hepple has sent Nelson 2-1 up, but it is Gonzales who controls in close space and fires Nelson’s winner before sending his 6ft 2in frame through an improbable backflip.

The 3-2 scoreline blinks out from the new digital screen where they’re proud to display an image of the FA Cup and 87-year-old Eric Manning, whose meticulous, handwritten reports of the team’s games are typed up and published in the weekly Nelson Leader, can start reflecting on history repeating itself.

Next up, in the Preliminary Round, Nelson play eighth-tier Witton Albion, who they improbably beat on the way to a 3-2 loss at Port Vale in one of their most memorable Cup runs, in 1951. Manning missed the Port Vale game because his parents insisted on taking him on holiday.

Daily Mail Sport's Ian Herbert interviews Nelson manager Arron Ripley

We will be with Nelson at Witton, as the next in a series of pieces in which we take a club, any club, from the Preliminary Qualifying Round of the FA Cup, and follow them through the competition until they are defeated, then transferring allegiance to the victors…- and so on until Wembley.

The same project which Daily Mail football writer Brian James embarked on, exactly 50 years ago this month, for what became his legendary book, Journey to Wembley. We hope it will build a picture of the real football - our football – full of its hope, dreams, triumphs and setbacks.

Another of Nelson’s great historical claims is a 100% home record against Manchester United, given that they once beat them in the old Second Division and have never played them since.

‘We invited them over to play us and to see if we could extend that record,’ says Price. ’They’ve politely declined. We live in hope and they’d be so welcome!’ But a venture deep into the Cup would mean much more. ‘We want people to know what’s going on down here at our little place,’ Price says. ‘We believe that if we build, they will come.’

Sports.title: England star Jude Bellingham joins his mum to watch his brother, Jobe, play for Borussia Dortmund against Arsenal
Sports.content:
England World Cup hero Jude Bellingham's post-season break took him to the Emirates on Sunday afternoon as he watched his brother line up against Arsenal.

Jude is on a three-week sabbatical after helping the Three Lions finish third in North America at the World Cup, with England's players due back training at their clubs this week.

But, before he heads back to Spain to start the new season with Real Madrid, he has found time to pop to Arsenal's stadium to watch Jobe Bellingham line up for Borussia Dortmund in a pre-season friendly.

Jude was seen sat in the stands at the Premier League champions' ground next to his mother Denise as Jobe, 20, played the full 90 minutes.

Jobe has been tipped to follow in the footsteps of Jude, 23, having followed him from Birmingham City to Dortmund – though via Sunderland.

The younger Bellingham brother signed for Dortmund for £32million last summer, making 45 appearances in all competitions though without a goal.

Jude Bellingham joined his mother Denise to watch brother Jobe play for Borussia Dortmund against Arsenal

Jobe (right) has been tipped to follow in his brother's footsteps and is currently playing for his former club

He is a regular at England Under-21 level, and has been tipped to make his senior debut alongside his brother in the near future.

Both players came from humble beginnings at Birmingham, with the Championship side retiring Jude's shirt number – 22 – when he left for Dortmund when he had just turned 17 in 2020.

He travelled over to St Andrew's for a pre-season friendly against Madrid's arch rivals Barcelona last week, giving Blues fans plenty to cheer about as they were given a rare opportunity to see the LaLiga champions in action.

Before kick-off, Birmingham City's official social media account showed Bellingham taking his seat and waving to fans in a touching video captioned: 'Jude. He's home.'

As he raised his arms aloft to greet the adoring fans, Blues supporters loudly bellowed 'Jude' to honour their former starlet and fervently chanted 'he's one of our own' in a special moment for the England midfielder at St Andrew's.

The £113million midfielder cheered jubilantly as he watched his boyhood club triumph over Madrid's rivals, winning on penalties after drawing 2-2 in normal time.

Bellingham is expected to play a key role at Madrid again this season, with Jose Mourinho taking over as manager again after the club opted to move on from interim manager Alvaro Arbeloa.

He will rejoin the England camp towards the end of next month for the next international break, which is three weeks long.

Sports.title: Beware Premier League rivals: Enzo Maresca's Man City are made for Erling Haaland and could help him produce his best season yet, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Back home 5,000 miles away, there ought to have been a certain Norwegian licking his lips at what Manchester City served up before they headed home from Asia. Presuming he has a subscription for the club’s in-house TV channel, that is.

This performance was made for Erling Haaland. The attacking style Enzo Maresca hopes to implement is made for Haaland. Atletico Madrid struggled for answers in how to counter City’s wingers – boldly direct all game – as they fizzed balls across the six-yard box.

That is Haaland’s zone and even before Omar Marmoush netted effectively the same goal twice in two minutes just before the hour – Antoine Semenyo hitting an area, the Egyptian tapping in – there came very real evidence that Haaland is going to be labelled a tap-in merchant. And City will not mind that one bit: that is where their goals are coming from this season.

It looks a game plan reliant on a man with a killer’s instinct, knowing exactly where to plonk himself. Haaland is the best in world football at that and City’s idea is clearly to lean into his strengths even further than they had done already.

Maresca had twice shown frustration before Marmoush’s double when Savinho had seemingly laid certain goals on a plate for a striker, only for nobody to arrive. The Italian bowed his head once and then outstretched the arms as Marmoush and others failed to fly in.

‘We cannot create the amount of situations and not finish the action,’ Maresca said. ‘There we need to be clinical. We need to improve. We are getting better there. With Erling we can be even more dangerous.’

Omar Marmoush produced two close range finishes from crosses aimed towards the six-yard box

Enzo Maresca's gameplan looks to have been devised with Erling Haaland in mind

Rayan Ait-Nouri scored Manchester City's third goal in their 3-1 victory over Atletico Madrid

Words were had at half time and it was noticeable that not only Marmoush but Phil Foden would later be readier to meet Semenyo’s crosses, crashing into the box in the way that had been replicated over and over in training the evening before. The victory was topped off by Rayan Ait-Nouri’s late third.

‘The players want to play,’ Maresca said as he left the door open for Marmoush’s potential exit, with Tottenham monitoring his situation.

‘They want to play. When they don’t play, they’re not happy. Omar’s desire is probably to play more minutes. It doesn't mean that he isn't going to play more minutes here but it's also his decision.’

Spurs target Savinho shows what he can offer City

Spurs still hold a keen interest in landing the £70million-rated Savinho, who had intimated a willingness to seek a new challenge earlier in the summer.

But the Brazilian has shown Maresca what he can offer out on the right wing with this style of play. There were the dangerous cutbacks, the sort reminiscent of a bygone era in the early years of Pep Guardiola, that suggested more of an end product than had been evident in his first two seasons.

That was the positive side of a lively Savinho, who relentlessly beat his full back around the outside. And yet, there were reminders of his profligacy that has seen him score just seven times in 84 games across all competitions.

When pouncing on a mistake, the 22-year-old should have driven towards goal and forced Jan Oblak to commit, instead deciding to check back and attempt a curling effort into the far corner from outside the box. It whipped wide.

And one of Maresca’s other disappointments came as Semenyo hit a dangerous area, only for City’s other winger to still be on his heels. There is work to do and decisions to be made before the end of the transfer window.

Savinho produced dangerous cutbacks and reliably beat his full back, but still showed reminders of his profligacy

City will need Anderson to quickly get up to speed

Despite dominating, City had fallen behind before Marmoush’s brace. A scrappy opener by Jorge Dominguez, a 16-year-old defender who towers over most. The teenager stabbed past Gianluigi Donnarumma from the second phase of a corner. City should have cleared their lines but it wasn’t the end of the world.

What will have concerned Maresca more were the spaces between the lines that Rodrigo Mendoza, a 21-year-old signed from Elche in February, was afforded. Mendoza proved a problem for Mateo Kovacic, ghosting off the back of the central midfielder and creating two decent chances. City will need to be more robust in that area of the pitch when they meet Arsenal in Sunday’s Community Shield.

Elliot Anderson is not linking up with the team until Wednesday and so it is likely that Kovacic will feature alongside Tijjani Reijnders in Cardiff. The pair have been strong on the ball in South Korea while having obvious things to work through defensively from a positioning sense.

As Barcelona expect to wrap up a deal to land metronome Rodri, City will need Anderson to quickly get himself up to speed.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi lands back in Rosario after father Jorge's death at 68... as Inter Miami teammate pays heartfelt tribute during game
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has returned to his hometown of Rosario following the death of his father, Jorge.

Messi missed Inter Miami's Leagues Cup clash with Monterrey to fly back to Argentina where, according to reports in South America, the 39-year-old will attend a private memorial service.

Jorge Messi - who also served as his son's agent and business manager - died at the age of 68, two months on from the family revealing he had been rushed to hospital with an ongoing 'health situation'.

He reportedly passed away in a hospital in Rosario, close to the family home, at around 10pm local time on Friday August 7.

In the absence of their captain, Inter Miami players honored Jorge Messi by wearing black armbands, while fans paused for a moment of silence before kickoff. Earlier on Saturday, the team had posted a tribute which read: 'Our hearts are with our captain, Leo, and the entire Messi family.'

Against Monterrey, stand-in captain Rodrigo De Paul - Messi's international teammate - scored the opening goal and then pulled off his jersey to reveal another which read: 'Messi 10.' Unfortunately for Inter Miami, Monterrey scored late on to snatch a 2-1 win.

Lionel Messi has returned to his hometown of Rosario following the death of his father, Jorge

The soccer legend's father, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, died at the age of 68

Rodrigo De Paul paid tribute to the Inter Miami captain during Saturday's clash with Monterrey

In the first official statement, Messi's first team Newell's Old Boys wrote in Spanish: 'Club Atletico Newell's Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario.'

The club continued: 'Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini.

'His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory. Thank you for teaching him to love these colors.'

Later on Saturday, both Barcelona and the Argentina national team added their own tributes.

'Stay strong, Leo Messi and family. We are with you in this difficult moment. We send you our most heartfelt embrace,' Argentina wrote on X.

A spokesperson for FC Barcelona, meanwhile, said in a statement: 'The President and the Board of Directors of FC Barcelona express their deepest condolences on the passing of Jorge Messi, the father of former Barca player and legend Lionel Messi, and, on behalf of the entire Barca family, extend their condolences to the Messi family.

'FC Barcelona thanks Jorge Messi for his commitment to our Club, for entrusting us with the beginnings and the most glorious years of his son Leo's football career. May he rest in peace.'

Sports.title: Arsenal pushing for more signings as Mikel Arteta tells fans club are 'looking forward'
Sports.content:
Arsenal pushing for more signings as Mikel Arteta tells fans club are 'looking forward'

Mikel Arteta has been asked if fans can expect more signings before the transfer window closes with Arsenal still in the market for a new defender

View Image Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal are in the market for more signings (Image: Carlos Jasso/AFP)

Mikel Arteta has admitted that Arsenal are pushing to sign more players before the end of the transfer window.

‌



The Gunners have spent more than £100million on new players this summer. Piero Hincapie's loan move from Bayer Leverkusen has been made permanent in a £34.5m deal, Christos Tzolis made the £34m switch from Club Brugge, Illan Meslier has signed after his Leeds contract expired, and Bruno Guimaraes has joined for £75m from Newcastle.

‌



But Arsenal, who go into the season as the reigning Premier League champions, are not expected to stop there and want to bolster their squad with more additions in the coming weeks. Indeed, following the Gunners' 3-2 pre-season defeat to Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, Arteta revealed the club remain active in the summer window.

‌



"Well, that's what we're trying to do [sign more players]," Arteta said. "If we have the right player in the market to make us much better. We are very looking forward to that."

Arsenal have conceded six goals in their last two pre-season matches; three against Dortmund and then three in the 3-1 defeat to Real Betis last Wednesday. In both matches, the Gunners looked open at the back and in truth Dortmund and Betis could have scored more than three each.

Article continues below

RT's question on a defender

You always say that you're open to strengthening the squad. You conceded three goals in the past two games. Is a defender something that you'd actually actively like to sign this summer? I wouldn't go there just to put an isolated there. We conceded some poor goals the other day, some poor goals today. In the way we competed, especially. But that's a very collective responsibility. So, we need to improve with the players that we have. And we want to improve for sure.

Sports.title: ‘Incroyable!’ Jockey banned 15 days after forfeiting first place by easing up before the line
Sports.content:
‘Incroyable!’ Jockey banned 15 days after forfeiting first place by easing up before the line

Italian-born Sebastiano Deriu earned the wrath of punters after his error on the Christopher Head-trained Palais Byzantin at Le Lion D'Angers on Sunday

View 4 Images Sebastiano Deriu (yellow and white) takes a glance over his shoulder while the winner (left) emerges to his right

A young jockey was banned for 15 days on Sunday after he forfeited first place by easing up before the winning line.

‌



Italian-born Sebastiano Deriu, who works for Christopher Head, is in his third season riding in France.

‌



He rode his first winner there in 2024 and so far has six successes to his name. Deriu partnered his last winner in early July but had not been in action since and his appearance at Le Lion D’Angers was his first in over a month. He was declared on Palais Byzantin, a two-year-old colt who had finished placed in two previous starts, including at Listed level at Vichy last time out.

‌



Big Buck's dies aged 23 as Paul Nicholls pays tribute to one of his greatest horses READ MORE :

As a result he went off the 7-5 favourite to open his account in the 7f race, which represented a drop in class for the son of Galiway.

Everything appeared to be going to plan as Palais Byzantin pulled his way to the front and was committed by Deriu entering the straight.

View 4 Images Palais Byzantin appears to have the race in the bag, at least his jockey thinks so

‌



The colt responded to kick clear of the rest of the field but, taking two glances over his left shoulder, Deriu seemed to assume he had done enough.

Ten strides from the line he inexplicably decided to stop pushing his mount and eased up only for Goldy Glory, under Martin Protti, to emerge from the opposite side to where he had been looking and get up to snatch victory to a cry of “Incroyable!” from the commentator.

View 4 Images Palais Byzantin is caught on the line by Goldy Glory

‌



Among the comments on social media, one punter described the ride as “a collector's item!”

“In the end, it's always the bettor who gets the short end of the stick in the story ... Give him 3 or 6 months suspension, that'll teach him the trade,” they said.

Another said: “Should we send them our bank details or what?”

‌



View 4 Images Christopher Head (centre): trainer of Palais Byzantin (Image: PA)

The local stewards initiated an inquiry into the finish to examine why Deriu had ceased urging the colt approximately 100 metres from the finish line.

The panel found him guilty and issued a 15 day suspension for easing up on Palais Byzantin and forfeiting first place.

Sports.title: Gstaad ruled out of Deauville clash with Bow Echo after suffering 'deep cut' at Goodwood
Sports.content:
Gstaad ruled out of Deauville clash with Bow Echo after suffering 'deep cut' at Goodwood

Gstaad has been ruled out of the Prix Jacques le Marois after picking up an infection following his narrow defeat in the Sussex Stakes at Goodwood

View 2 Images Bow Echo and Gstaad will not meet in France next Sunday (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

Gstaad will miss a potential fourth meeting with Bow Echo in the Prix Jacques le Marois next Sunday after developing an infection following his narrow loss in the Sussex Stakes at Goodwood.

‌



Aidan O'Brien's Irish 2,000 Guineas winner has finished behind Bow Echo on three occasions this campaign, taking the runner-up position in the 2000 Guineas, the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and in a memorable Sussex Stakes just over a week ago.

‌



O'Brien made clear he would not shy away from another encounter with George Boughey's outstanding colt later in the summer – but while the latter has the option of travelling to Deauville, Gstaad is set to be aimed at the Prix du Moulin at ParisLongchamp on September 6 following a minor setback.

‌



Big Buck's dies aged 23 as Paul Nicholls pays tribute to one of his greatest horses READ MORE :

When questioned about the Marois as a possibility at the Curragh on Sunday, O'Brien said: "I don't think so. He got galloped into in Goodwood and he got a little bit of an infection in his hind part from it.

"We put him on antibiotics and with the antibiotics we put him on usually we'd be able to run him in seven days, but they had to give him an extra strong antibiotic because the cut was deep so it took 14 days, it wouldn't be out of his system in time.

‌



He added: "It will probably be the Moulin now before he runs. That's probably where he'll go."

The Ballydoyle trainer also delivered updates on two of his Royal Ascot-winning juveniles in Great Barrier Reef and Victorious, with the latter potentially sidelined for the remainder of the season.

View 2 Images Gstaad: sustained a cut in the Sussex Stakes (Image: Evan Treacy/PA Wire)

Article continues below

"Great Barrier Reef had a spot of ringworm, that's why he didn't come here for the Phoenix Stakes (today). It's gone and it's dead, but you have to give them a couple of weeks when that happens," O'Brien added.

"With the horse from Goodwood (Richmond Stakes winner Man's Best Friend) today was coming a bit too quick, so it will be between him and Great Barrier Reef for the Prix Morny we think.

"Victorious was a little bit off, so she'll have a little bit of time off and whether we run her for the rest of the season I'm not sure, but if there's anything (wrong) we'll wait with her because she's travelled and she's a lot of experience. If we're not 100 per cent happy with her she's finished for the season."

Sports.title: Arsenal respond to Gabriel Martinelli transfer approach as Mikel Arteta lays out demands
Sports.content:
Arsenal have received an approach from Galatasaray regarding a possible move for Gabriel Martinelli. However, the Gunners are not expected to consider the Turkish club's advances unless a replacement is lined up.

The Mirror's sister-title football.london report that the 25-year-old is currently in Mikel Arteta's plans but the ambitious move for Vinicius Junior indicated a desire to strengthen out wide with other clubs taking note of Martinelli's potential availability.

Christos Tzolis has already joined this summer and has been Arteta's chosen left winger throughout pre-season. The former Norwich City man scored in the win over Girona and assisted Piero Hincapie's headed goal in the defeat to Real Betis.

Arsenal's champion squad will leave Mikel Arteta having to digest harsh reality READ MORE :

A desire for more consistent output appears to be the reason behind Arsenal's pursuit of another attacker with Martinelli managing just one Premier League goal across 30 outings last season.

‌



He produced an impressive Champions League campaign during the league phase, but failed to find the net in any knockout fixture en route to the final.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

That impact when it matters seems to be what Arsenal are looking for. Should they identify a suitable option, it would likely trigger a change in approach regarding Martinelli's situation.

The player is thought to be content in north London and retains aspirations of competing at the highest level, but the guarantee of consistent game time and the prospect of being displaced by another new signing could alter that outlook.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is looking at more Arsenal new signings

Arteta addressed the media following the clash in Girona, hinting that further transfer activity could be on the horizon over the coming weeks. Bruno Guimaraes has already been confirmed as an Arsenal signing, though additional deals are still anticipated.

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously," the Spaniard added, speaking after a 4-1 pre-season victory over Girona.

"We want to get better like anybody else, and you just can see the transfer market and our opponents, what ‌we are doing. We won't sit still, and we are very ambitious with what we are doing.

‌



"The margins are very small. Because we want to get better, and the level is going to increase. We need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we ‌don't have in the team."

Mason Mount injury latest as Man Utd sweat on star after pre-season blow

Mason Mount has impressed in pre-season but he gave Manchester United a scare by picking up an injury just 20 minutes into Saturday's 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain

Manchester United have been given a boost after learning that Mason Mount's injury is not serious. The United midfielder came off after just 20 minutes during Saturday's 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain.

It left Michael Carrick sweating on the fitness of Mount, 27, with less than two weeks to go until the Red Devils start their Premier League season away to newly promoted Hull City. But the midfielder left the stadium in Gothenburg, Sweden walking freely, suggesting that his pre-season wasn't over.

Mount has now flown to Ireland ahead of United's next training camp in County Kildare. He'll be joined by Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martinez, who were each given additional time off following the World Cup.

Having only started two of Carrick's 17 games in charge last season, Mount has given a good account of himself in pre-season. Playing in a deeper role, the former Chelsea star has put together an encouraging run of performances.

Sports.title: 'I quit after competing at Commonwealth Games – I'm now famous and worth £74m'
Sports.content:
'I quit after competing at Commonwealth Games – I'm now famous and worth £74m'

Another Commonwealth Games is in the history books and stars will be looking towards what's next - but they'll have a task matching what this Hollywood actor went on to do

View 2 Images Jason Statham at the 1990 Commonwealth Games (Image: BBC)

Jason Statham competed as an elite athlete before a remarkable career change made him a Hollywood star. He represented England in diving at the 1990 Commonwealth Games.

‌



The 59-year-old competed in three events at the games in Auckland. Statham came eighth in the one-metre springboard and earned 11th place in both the three-metre and 10-metre events.

‌



Diving events were dropped from the recent Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, despite being a highlight of Statham’s sporting career more than three decades ago. The Transporter star was ranked 12th in the world for platform diving during his career but the Olympic Games eluded him after competing in trials ahead of the 1988 Seoul Games and the Barcelona Olympics four years later.

‌



"It’s a bit of a sore point I never got to the Olympics,” Statham said at the Mechanic: Resurrection premiere in 2016, following Team GB claiming a medal at the Rio Games in each of his three former events. “I just heard they got seven million or something for the diving per year.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Meet the University of Birmingham student seeking European Athletics Championships glory on his home track READ MORE :

"They deserve it. The divers we’ve got now are just terrific.” He added: "I started too late. It probably wasn’t my thing. I should have done a different sport."

‌



Staham’s passion for diving began after watching someone regularly practice a high-dive during a family holiday. He joined the British National Diving School in 1985, but believes that falling short of sporting success gave him extra motivation as he began to move away from diving.

“I think what I didn’t achieve (in sports) has probably helped me focus more and take my acting career more seriously,” Statham told the BBC in 2008. He initially began working as a model for top brands such as Tommy Hilfiger, Levi's and French Connection before meeting film director Guy Ritchie.

View 2 Images Jason Statham became a top movie star after his diving career (Image: Simon Ackerman/Getty Images)

‌



Statham was given his first role in Ritchie’s 1998 hit Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, alongside his childhood friend Vinnie Jones. The pair also worked together with Ritchie in Snatch, before Statham earned a reputation as a bankable movie star.

Following his many notable film roles, CelebrityNet Worth estimates Statham to be worth £74.26million ($100m). However, the actor has previously reflected on what he gained from his earlier sporting career.

“It was a great experience, you know, to travel the world and compete at a certain level. It teaches you discipline, focus, and certainly keeps you out of trouble," Statham told IGN in a 2003 interview.

Article continues below

"Diving was obviously a hobby of mine, and being an amateur sport you can't earn any money at that," he said. "So I used to put money in my pocket while working on the street corners, selling perfume and jewellery, and other goods that were supposedly expensive."

Statham has since earned riches from his acting career but has not forgotten his diving skills. Last year, holiday snaps emerged of him diving off a yacht while with his family in Positano, Italy.

Sports.title: Chelsea and Real Madrid eye Martin Zubimendi as Arsenal set price after Bruno Guimaraes transfer
Sports.content:
Chelsea and Real Madrid eye Martin Zubimendi as Arsenal set price after Bruno Guimaraes transfer

What happens between now and deadline day remains unclear, but reports from Spain have claimed that Zubimendi's future could be something to keep in mind over the next few weeks.

The report adds, however, that Arsenal are unlikely to authorise Zubimendi's departure this summer for anything less than €90million (£77million).

Chelsea are also said to be showing interest in signing Zubimendi, with their new manager, Xabi Alonso, believed to be eager to bring the Spain international to Stamford Bridge.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Sports.title: Coleman: Ireland's new generation not scarred by past World Cup play-off pain
Sports.content:
Seamus Coleman insists the Republic of Ireland's new generation will not be scarred by the bitter pain of World Cup play-off defeat as they attempt to book a ticket for this summer's finals.

Ireland face the Czech Republic at Prague's Fortuna Arena on Thursday evening attempting to go one better than they did in 2009 against France and in 2017, when Denmark shattered their dreams with a 5-1 demolition job in Dublin.

However, Everton defender Coleman, who was not in the squad on that fateful night in Paris and was injured for the game with the Danes, is confident there will be no hangover, with the Czechs standing between Heimir Hallgrimsson's men and a winner-takes-all match with either Denmark or North Macedonia in Dublin on Tuesday.

Asked if the pain of those near-misses was fuelling the latest bid to make it to the finals for the first time since 2002, the 37-year-old said: "It's difficult to say if it's fuelling the players, they're all so young.

"Obviously the nation was hurt massively, but in terms of the current group of players I don't think they're dwelling too much on that hurt.

"To be honest, we're just riding the wave of the confidence we've got as a group - which I think this young group deserves - from the last two games and we're looking forward to Thursday night and then see what comes after that.

"But to see how the nation is feeling now is incredible and we've got a duty to try and make them even happier."

Image: Troy Parrott's goals inspired Ireland to stunning wins over Portugal and Hungary that secured a play-off spot

Ireland are only in Prague because they backed up a scratchy Group F victory over Armenia with an unexpected 2-0 win against Portugal in Dublin before going to Hungary and coming out on top in a five-goal thriller in which Troy Parrott scored the decisive goal with the last kick of the game.

Coleman is one of only two players - 34-year-old Robbie Brady is the other - in the current squad to have been to a major tournament, and the experience they had in earning their trip to Euro 2016 in France could prove invaluable this time around.

Image: Coleman and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson are bidding to lead Ireland to World Cup qualification for the first time since 2002

Martin O'Neill's team reached the finals by beating Bosnia and Herzegovina 3-1 on aggregate in a play-off after a hard-fought 1-1 draw in Zenica in the first leg.

Coleman said: "Maybe two years ago it would have been a lot for the young lads to take.

"But everyone now has stepped up and are prepared for what's to come and we absolutely, no doubt about it, understand it's going to be a tough game for us, but it's also going to be a tough game for them as well."

Head coach Hallgrimsson, who is without suspended defender Liam Scales and injured midfielder Josh Cullen, as ever exuded calm as he fulfilled his media duties on Wednesday morning, simply asking for more of the same from his players.

He said: "We all know by now why we got good results and good performances, and that's the key, not be over-ambitious tomorrow, stay on point, focus on why we are here and trying to improve that, not only this game, continuously."

Czech boss says Soucek still key player despite not being captain

Image: West Ham's Tomas Soucek is no longer captain of his country

Czech Republic boss Miroslav Koubek said "full-fat" Tomas Soucek remains a key player for his country despite being stripped of the captaincy.

The 31-year-old West Ham midfielder has been replaced as skipper by Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci after being removed from his position amid the fall-out from the 2-1 defeat by the Faroe Islands in October.

However Koubek, who himself took over from Ivan Hasek as head coach in December, still counts Soucek among his most important players ahead of Thursday night's World Cup play-off semi-final against the Republic of Ireland in Prague.

He said: "Tomas Soucek is an outstanding player with a great career. He doesn't have the captain's armband at this moment for reasons you all know, but nothing changes.

"It does not mean he will lose his value. He is still a 'full-fat' player, if I can use these words."

Image: Miroslav Koubek's first game in charge of the Czech Republic is against Ireland

Soucek's removal as captain has prompted speculation in the Czech media that he could even lose his place in the team, although Koubek remained coy over his team selection.

The 74-year-old said: "I don't read the newspapers, so I don't know. You will see tomorrow."

Koubek's side will welcome Ireland to the Fortuna Arena, the home of domestic champions Slavia Prague, knowing they will have to find a way to stop in-from striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in his country's last two qualifiers against Portugal and Hungary to get them to the play-offs.

Asked about his analysis of Heimir Hallgrimsson's team, he said: "One thing I noticed: they put a lot heart into their game. Ireland will definitely be a very tough opponent.

"But we will have a similar mindset, it will be a hard match, definitely.

"As for Parrott, he is outstanding, he is doing great. He is very fit, we know how he works. We do have some information, so now it will all be about eliminating him in a smart way. We will just have to stop him."

Krejci, however, has little doubt that it will be he and his team-mates who ultimately fight it out with either Denmark of North Macedonia for a trip to the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

He said: "We will make it. We will reach our goal. We will qualify for the World Cup."

Sports.title: JEFF POWELL: Frank Warren talks up new golden age of British heavyweight boxing as prodigy Moses Itauma prepares for Filip Hrgovic showdown
Sports.content:
Frank Warren has signalled a new ‘golden age' for British heavyweight boxing as his prodigy Moses Itauma prepares for his unexpected world title fight with Filip Hrgovic at London’s O2 on August 29.

The 21-year-old Itauma was already set to face the 31-year-old Croatian in a championship eliminator when the fight was promoted into a battle for the IBF title after undisputed heavyweight king Oleksandr Usyk vacated all four alpha-belts.

Hrgovic’s only defeat in 21 fights came when he was knocked out in the eighth round two years ago by Daniel Dubois, who went on to become the WBO champion by stopping Fabio Wardley in a bloodied slugfest this May. Those two Englishmen will meet again in a rematch in October.

Hall of Fame Promoter Warren also has in his stable Tyson Fury who is heading for his long, long awaited Battle of Britain with Anthony Joshua in November at either Wembley Stadium or New York’s fabled Madison Square Garden.

‘These are amazingly exciting times for heavyweight boxing in this country,’ says Warren. ‘We have a whole programme of mouth-watering fights pencilled in our calendar at Queensberry.

'Although Moses is in his toughest fight yet I expect him to become the second youngest ever world heavyweight champion behind Mike Tyson.

Moses Itauma is preparing for his unexpected world title fight with Filip Hrgovic

‘He would then have to deal with a mandatory defence against (American) Frank Mitchell, who I don’t think is as talented as Hrgovic.

'Win that and we should be looking at an IBF - WBO title unification fight between him and the winner of Dubois v Wardley. All of those are huge punchers and that fight would sell-out Wembley in a heart-beat.’

All the above are on Queensberry's books except Mitchell and Joshua and Warren says: ‘I expect Tyson to beat AJ on seniors night and quite possibly carry on to fight whichever of the young bloods comes out on top as the new undisputed heavyweight champion.

‘Imagine Itauma the hottest most talked about heavy on the planet against Fury the box office Gypsy King.

'Is there a stadium big enough for that.By the last Saturday night this month the UK will know for sure what Itauma is all about. And as it happens even at his age he has the maturity and the level head to carry it all off. Even though every fight in his sights now will be as dangerous as they come.

‘Buckle up.'

Sports.title: Heavyweight boxer Joseph Parker is CLEARED of doping after proving positive drugs test was caused by exposure to his nutritionist taking cocaine
Sports.content:
Heavyweight boxer Joseph Parker is CLEARED of doping after proving positive drugs test was caused by exposure to his nutritionist taking cocaine

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ex-heavyweight boxing champion Joseph Parker has been cleared of breaking drug rules after proving his adverse test finding was due to his nutritionist taking cocaine.

Parker, 34, was found to have traces of the Class A drug in his system on the day of his defeat by Fabio Wardley last October following a test conducted by the Voluntary Anti-Doping Agency (VADA).
