As a result, the system now loses approximately 12 million fewer gallons of water per day than it did in 2015.

In addition, work is progressing on the Western Water Resilience Programme, while plans are advancing to construct new treatment plants and expand water catchment systems, including the Hermitage Dam.

Expanding water catchment capacity is one solution that motorist Miguel Brown believes could help Jamaica better withstand future droughts. Brown, who regularly uses a car wash to maintain his vehicle, argued that the island has ample underutilised land that could be used to capture and store rainwater for use during dry periods.

“We have a lot of springs, we have a lot of rivers, we just need somewhere for the water to stay so we don’t have the problem every year,” he reasoned.

He noted that he washes his car twice a month but is willing to cut down to once a month to help conserve.

“All of us know that we have to save in a crisis like this; in the dry season, we have to save. Once everybody has the understanding and sees what is happening — the entire Jamaica should see what is happening in the dry times and we must get used to it by now,” said Brown.

Conrad Malcolm washes his car once per week. He said he is prepared to clean his car himself using recycled water from home or seek out car wash operators who have access to untreated water and are prepared for the drought.

He urged greater investment in water storage facilities, given the increase in the number of households.

“We have more households coming up and each household will use more water. We need to invest in more water facilities. There are rivers; we have the sea; we can treat the water. We can do much better to alleviate the problem rather than every year we are at the same place,” he stressed.

World.title: Plie’s AMALGAMATION Gala set for 10th anniversary finale in Jamaica
World.content:
Plie Collective .

Jamaica is set for an electrifying celebration of dance excellence as Plie’s AMALGAMATION Gala returns to the Little Theatre on August 29 and 30.

Marking the 10th anniversary of Plié for The Arts, this milestone edition promises to be its most spectacular staging yet.

Held under the distinguished patronage of Misty Copeland, AMALGAMATION Gala 2026 will close its Caribbean tour in Jamaica after performances in Trinidad and Tobago and Barbados.

This year’s gala will honour Desmond Richardson, the iconic American dancer, choreographer, co-founder and co-artistic director of Complexions Contemporary Ballet.

The full company will headline the programme, bringing the Caribbean première of Dwight Rhoden’s show-stopping Love Rocks, set to music by Lenny Kravitz, along with Rhoden’s other breathtaking works Ave Maria and Mercy.

Audiences will also see New York City Ballet’s Christopher Grant in a duet with the stunning Ashley Green of Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater. The ever-spectacular Caught by Parsons Dance, as well as Suite Etta, a stunning piece performed by Adji Cissoko, recently named associate artistic director, and her electrifying dance partner, Shuaib Elhassan from Alonzo King LINES Ballet.

Adding to the excitement, the Plié Caribbean Collective, now featuring exceptional dancers from across the region, will share the stage with these international stars. The Collective will perform powerful works from its repertoire with the Caribbean première of On the Verge of Ascending, created by Swedish choreographer Jon Ole Olstad and Carmina Burano choreographed by Ilya Jivoy delivering a true fusion of Caribbean talent and global brilliance.

At the heart of AMALGAMATION is a bold vision of bringing the best of the world together with the best of the region.

Beyond the stage, the gala creates opportunities for training and artistic exchange through workshops and masterclasses led by participating global companies. As part of the celebration, Complexions Contemporary Ballet will host free masterclasses, with outstanding participants eligible for immersive scholarship opportunities with the company.

With a different experience offered each night, AMALGAMATION has grown into a regional destination event with global ambition. Founder and Artistic Director Marisa Benain says the gala is built to stand among the world’s best: “The Amalgamation Gala offers audiences a programme and an experience that is hard to match anywhere in the world. We have what it takes to produce a dance gala at an international standard, and our aim is always to make each Amalgamation Gala more spectacular than the last.”

World.title: Jamaica leads Caribbean in Airbnb emergency housing
World.content:
This house in Parottee, St Elizabeth, crumbled during Hurricane Melissa.

MORE than two-thirds of the 1,500 nights of emergency housing provided for families displaced by natural disasters across the Caribbean by Airbnb.org since 2020 have been utilised in Jamaica.

Christoph Gorder, executive director of Airbnb.org — the independent non-profit founded by Airbnb to provide emergency housing in times of crisis — puts the figure at more than 1,000 nights.

“The vast majority of that housing was provided in the wake of Hurricane Melissa, reflecting the scale of the storm’s impact,“ Gorder said in an e-mailed response to the Jamaica Observer.

He said the non-profit is proud of the role its community has played in supporting people in Jamaica during emergencies.

“And as our partnership with the Caribbean Disaster Emergency Management Agency (CDEMA) and other partners like IOM, Church World Services, and All Hands and Hearts demonstrates, we stand ready to help in the future,” Gorder said.

Last month, Airbnb and Airbnb.org signed an agreement with CDEMA to accelerate access to temporary housing for disaster victims across the agency’s 20 Caribbean member countries. The agreement is designed to help mobilise available housing support after a disaster, helping close temporary housing gaps that often emerge in the immediate aftermath of a crisis.

The partnership is anchored by a memorandum of understanding (MOU) that addresses roles, coordination, and activations during the critical early days of a disaster response. CDEMA will help coordinate with local responders to identify people with emergency housing needs, while Airbnb.org will support these efforts by helping provide free, available emergency housing.

Airbnb.org leverages the Airbnb platform to help connect people who need a place to stay with listings on the platform, enabling guests to book homes that meet their needs, including kitchens, laundry rooms, and pet-friendly spaces. All stays are offered at no cost to guests and funded by Airbnb.org.

According to CDEMA’s Executive Director Elizabeth Riley, the partnership represents a valuable addition to the region’s disaster preparedness and response framework.

“As we enter the 2026 hurricane season, the MOU strengthens our ability to support people affected by disasters through innovative solutions and enhanced regional collaboration. By combining CDEMA’s regional coordination capacity with Airbnb.org’s emergency housing support, we are expanding the resources available to communities when they need them most,” Riley said. “It also reflects a shared commitment to ensuring that affected populations can access timely assistance and recover more quickly following disasters.”

Additionally, Airbnb, in collaboration with CDEMA and the Caribbean Tourism Organization (CTO), launched a hurricane safety guide to support communities and educate the public about what to do before, during, and after a hurricane. It also includes emergency contact information for multiple Caribbean islands. Airbnb said it will provide the hurricane safety guide to hosts in the region so they can share with their guests.

“Safety in the Caribbean is a top priority for Airbnb. By collaborating with expert organisations like CDEMA and the CTO, we are ensuring our hosts and guests have access to vital, locally sourced resources to prepare for and navigate hurricane season,” said Carlos Muñoz, Airbnb’s director of public policy for the Caribbean and Central America.

World.title: SALMON FINDS A WAY
World.content:
Jamaica’s Joseph Salmon competes in the men’s discus throw qualification at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon, on Saturday. Salmon qualified for today’s final with a mark of 62.10m. (Photo: Paul A Reid)

OREGON, USA — Inspired by his teammate Michael Andre Edwards’ last-round heroics in the men’s triple jump final on Friday evening, world leader Joseph Salmon pulled off a similar nervy feat on Saturday to qualify for today’s men’s discus throw final on the final day of the World Athletics Under-20 Championships here at Hayward Field.

After two fouls and on the brink of failing to qualify, Salmon threw 62.10m on his final attempt in Group B, qualifying to join Kamari Kennedy who had qualified in the first group with 60.65m. Both surpassed the automatic qualifying mark of 60.50m.

Meanwhile, Jamaica will hope to defend both 4x100m relay titles today after qualifying on Saturday.

All four Jamaican relay teams, including the two 4x400m teams, advanced to their finals.

On Friday, Edwards pulled off a final-round miracle to win the men’s triple jump, and Salmon said although he was not expecting to need all three qualifying attempts, he was inspired by what he saw.

“I am really confident. What Michael did [Friday], he gave me a boost, gave me a boost, man so we’ll see. It’s going to be a show [Sunday],” he said after qualifying.

Salmon fouled his first two attempts, saying his technique was not the best, while his second attempt was ruled a foul for stepping over the board.

“In the third round I got everything together and just sent it out there,” he said, adding that he was not thinking about any particular distance but was simply focused on qualifying. “I am pleased to say I’m not really throwing at my full potential but just to get into the final.”

Kennedy was delighted with his third throw, which was over the qualifying mark.

“I was really happy. I’m glad that I got the qualifying mark and so now I can prepare for the finals,” he told the Jamaica Observer.

Kennedy had failed to advance from the first round of the shot put earlier in the championships but said the discus qualification made up for that disappointment.

Strong legs from lead-off runner Kyle Bodden and anchor Sanjay Seymore helped the Jamaican men’s team win their heat of the 4x100m in 39.51 seconds.

Nyrone Wade, who was part of the team that won in Lima, Peru, two years ago, and Nathaniel Martin were also part of the team that beat Japan, which finished second in 39.65 seconds, and Hong Kong, which set a national Under-20 record of 39.66.

The women’s team of Samoya Brown, Theianna Lee Terrelonge, Natrece East and Renecia Edwards finished second in their heat in 43.61 seconds, behind Australia which ran a national Under-20 record 43.44. Nigeria was third in 43.65.

East told the Sunday Observer that the team was happy to advance to the final.

“I think we performed well. I mean, it’s the first three that advance to the finals so we did enough to make it to the finals. And, I feel like when we run in the finals we can do better,” she said.

East said they were going after medals and, while admitting the baton exchanges were good, hoped they could be better today.

“Yeah, I feel like they were good. I mean, there’s always room for improvement so in the final we have to make even better changes and we will be good.”

Earlier, the team of Daniellia Dixon, Kristen Herbert, Davine Dickenson and Shanika Lindsay finished third in the women’s 4x400m, qualifying in 3:35.93 behind Germany, which won in 3:34.35, and Slovenia, which ran a national Under-20 record 3:35.60.

The men’s team of Nishawn Walker, Jordan Rehedul, Jaeden Campbell and Jabulani McLeod also placed third in their semi-final heat in 3:06.44. The USA led with a World Under-20-leading 3:04.55 while South Africa was second in 3:05.08, with both teams being gold-medal prospects.

World.title: COCKTAILS With…
World.content:
(Photo: Marz Jackson)

ANNALISA “@annaixe” GUTHRIE

Designer | Creative Practitioner

We’re stirring things up.

The Style Observer serves up Cocktails With with a twist.

For Independence 64, designer Annalisa Guthrie is toasting the icons, influences, and cultural greats who helped shape Jamaica — and, in turn, shaped the woman she is today.

Known for her knack of transforming the most unexpected materials into high-fashion statements, Guthrie is turning heritage into a silhouette, history into a statement, and Jamaican pride into something wearable.

Style Observer: What was the inspiration behind the new looks?

Annalisa Guthrie: “Our greatness today is a result of who we have been and who we continue to be. Here’s my way of celebrating the greats who helped shape the culture; the same culture that has made me who I am and what I’ll always be proud to be — Jamaican,” she shared.

SO shares the three-piece collection.

Asymmetrical Mesh Merino Dress

A staple in Jamaican fashion is the mesh marino, most commonly worn in the context of streetwear, and which has been styled in many ways, especially by male reggae artistes. I thought it would be interesting to make something of a gown out of different cut-up pieces of several merinos, but in a very raw and rugged way to keep in line with the tradition of “tun yuh hand and mek fashion”. I didn’t want this piece to feel as refined, but I still wanted it to feel flattering and unique and fashionable for the female form while still being raw.

Dancehall Queen 2.0

Nineties dancehall fashion has always been the blueprint for so many internationally, and I thought it was very important to pay tribute to not only original Dancehall Queen Carlene and some of her iconic golden looks, but also to pay homage to Spice, the queen of dancehall. The bejewelled bra has diamond shapes that meet the eye immediately, but If you look closely at the end of the chains you can see symbols (clubs, hearts and spades) to represent the symbols in a card pack — a nuanced way to honour Spice as “queen inna di deck”.

Bandana

For far too long I’ve heard criticism about the Bandana being outdated or not seen as beautiful, despite it being our national dress. I think it is our responsibility as artists to create and help others view things through a different lens. I made this video originally for the purpose of reimagining the Bandana print in a way that felt reverent, but modern. It was meant to be the main attraction. Jamaican folklorist Louise Bennett-Coverley championed for our cultural pride in a way that inspired me deeply and she wore the bandana proudly. I wanted to honour her by carrying the torch and using my creativity to represent her national pride in present day. I hope people are able to feel her spirit and reignite their own love for this little island when seeing this piece take form.

CREDITS

Visuals: Marz Jackson, @marz_jackson

Hair: Angel-Lee, hairbyangellee

Model: Annalisa Guthrie

World.title: Jamaica’s Edwards snatches triple jump gold at World U20 Champs
World.content:
In this March 2026 file photo, Jamaica College star Michael-Andre Edwards displays his gold medal after winning the Class 1 Boys’ triple jump final, with a leap of 16.25m., to close out his Champs career. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

OREGON, USA – Michael Andre Edwards thought he would be able to jump “about 16.80m” but surprised himself with a dramatic final round 17.08m (1.1m/s) leap to snatch the gold medal at the World Athletics Under- 20 Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon.

Edwards, who started slowly, trailed his good friend American Miles Nesmith going into the final round, when he produced the jump of his life on the biggest stage.

After his dramatic win, he said he never expected he would be jumping this far this soon but never thought 17.00m was out of his reach.

He twice bettered his previous personal best of 16.30m set in July, with 16.71m in the fifth round and then his big jump a round later. He joins national under-20 record holder Jaydon Hibbert,17.87m, and James Beckford, 17.29m, as the only Jamaican juniors to jump over 17.00m in the triple jump.

Edwards is also the second Jamaican man to win the triple jump after Hibbert won it in 2022.

This was Jamaica’s first gold of the champions and third medal after Gary Card and Shanoya Douglas won silver medals in their respective 100m finals on Thursday.

Nesmith, who was second to Edwards at the Penn Relays in April, took the silver medal with a personal best 16.79m (1.0m/s) and China’s Zhuoyue Wang was third with 16.36m (0.9m/s).

Edwards, who needed just one jump, 16.00m, to qualify from the prelims, started slowly with a 13.76m (1.4m/s) but qualified for the final with a 16.23m (-0.3m/s) in the third round before he got into second place with 16.71 (0.5m/s) in the fifth round.

-Paul A Reid

World.title: Hurting Jamaica
World.content:
An inflatable obstacle course at the entry fee-free Harmony Beach Park in Montego Bay, St James.

FALMOUTH, Trelawny — Minister of Tourism Edmund Bartlett has criticised people who he says are creating a false impression internationally that Jamaicans are being denied access to the country’s beaches.

Speaking at the 2026 Artisan Village Food Festival in Falmouth on Thursday, Bartlett argued that the facts do not support the narrative being circulated overseas and the false claims are damaging Jamaica’s reputation and costing the Government money to correct.

“We have 70 [public bathing beaches] in Jamaica, all around the island. And of that 70 only 10 of them are paid beaches. And then only five of that you would pay a decent money to go to,” Bartlett said.

“And yet, some of us, when you hear what we say to the international media… you would believe that every beach in Jamaica is just locked off, and that’s not fair to Jamaica. That’s not fair to us,” added Bartlett.

He argued that concerns may arise about access to specific beaches, but insisted that isolated issues should not be used to broad-brush the country.

“So we say, if you have an issue with one, or two, all right, let’s talk about that. Let’s deal with it because everywhere in the world you go, there’s an issue. But we must deal with it and resolve it, and not define ourselves by it,” argued Bartlett.

The tourism minister said the Government has had to invest in advertising and promotional campaigns to counter misinformation in the international media.

“You know as minister of tourism how much trouble I get on international press to go and explain to them that it is not true? Then we have to spend money with advertising agents… to tell them seh nothing nuh go so,” Bartlett said.

He urged Jamaicans to resolve national challenges internally rather than tarnishing the country’s image overseas.

“So we have to help ourselves. Where we have a problem, let us resolve it. Let us see where the difficulties are, talk about it, deal with it at home, solve it at home. And, as Miss Lou seh, ‘Don’t wash your dirty linen abroad,’ because when you believe you are hurting your neighbour, you’re not hurting your neighbour, you’re hurting your country and, in the end, yourself,” Bartlett added.

He lamented what he described as a tendency among some Jamaicans to highlight only the country’s shortcomings.

“Some of us enjoy beating up little Jamaica. Some of us enjoy saying all the negative things about the country, and some people I hear say things like Jamaica refuse to make its people enjoy the beaches. I never hear anything like that,” he said.

Bartlett urged Jamaicans to use the country’s 64th anniversary of Independence to embrace a new conversation and project a more positive image of the nation.

“And as we do that, the second thing I want to concern my mind and to get you into my thoughts on is how it is that we project ourselves as a people and as a country,” Bartlett said.

“The world views us through our own eyes and through our prisms. The world sees us the way we see ourselves, but most importantly, the way we express who we are to the world,” he added.

Bartlett said Jamaica’s 64th Independence anniversary should mark the beginning of a more positive national outlook.

“So, on this 64th birthday, let us resolve to have a new conversation, a new narrative, a positive contribution to ourselves, as together we grow. As we recover from Melissa, we recover stronger and better, and we build this great little piece of rock. In the words of Miss Lou, ‘We little but we tallawah,’” he said.

Official data show Jamaica possesses approximately 1,022 kilometres of coastline, of which approximately 29 per cent (300 kilometres) consists of sandy beaches.

World.title: Israel rejects Trump’s peace plan for Gaza
World.content:
Hamas has said that it would begin disarming, but in recent days an Israeli official said the country still had “serious security concerns.”

The rejection is a blow to peace negotiations the Trump administratoin has been brokering since September. The U.S. president had described the plan, now rejected by Israel, as a “critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government” and giving Israel “the security it deserves.”

Israel appears unlikely to pull back significant forces or make other concessions ahead of legislative elections scheduled for October. Netanyahu faces a tough reelection battle, with his far-right coalition partners urging him to keep up the pressure on Hamas and leave forces in Gaza. Opponents also accuse him of failing to prevent the Oct. 7, 2023, attack when Hamas-led militants attacked Israeli communities, killing about 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and taking 251 others hostage. Israel responded with a punishing military offensive that has killed more than 73,000 people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry.

Netanyahu said on Sunday that he is now in discussions with U.S. officials about how to move forward. “They have ideas, some of which are acceptable to us and some of which are unacceptable to us, and we know how to stand up to these things,” he said.

World.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange overnight strikes, WHO confirms warehouse destroyed
World.content:
Another overnight strike on the Zhytomyr region injured three people, Ukrainian emergency services said.

Meanwhile, five people died in a Ukrainian overnight drone attack on the Russian city of Belgorod, the regional crisis centre said on Sunday. Acting governor Alexander Shuvayev said earlier on Sunday that three people were killed and 25 others injured in the “massive terrorist drone attack” by Kyiv. The death toll later rose to five.

Zelenskyy condemned what he described as “ballistic terror” attacks on Odesa, Kharkiv, Pavlohrad, and other regions. “Every such attack on human life serves as a constant reminder – we need more pressure, more sanctions against Russia, and more air defense for Ukraine,” he said.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director-general of the World Health Organization, said on Sunday that a WHO warehouse in Dnipro in Ukraine was destroyed by a strike on Friday.

The warehouse held humanitarian supplies for frontline health facilities. No casualties were reported, as a WHO staff member and drivers managed to evacuate 130 of approximately 300 pallets and left the area before the attack.

“I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care MUST STOP. Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare,” Tedros said.

World.title: Germany battling “daily” hybrid warfare attacks, minister warns
World.content:
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt speaks to the media during a news conference at Leipzig airport on Aug. 5, 2026. | Jens Schlueter/Getty Images

Last week’s drone incident in Lepizig just the latest example.

Germany is being hit by hybrid warfare attacks from foreign powers on a “daily” basis, the country’s interior minister has warned, after a drone packed with explosives was found at Leipzig Airport earlier this week.

Espionage, sabotage, cyber attacks and covert actions “with the aim of destabilizing Germany or directly harming it” are a “constant reality,” German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told BILD in an interview on Sunday.

Dobrindt suggested on Thursday that a drone incident at Leipzig Airport may have been an attack by a state actor. The minister has stopped short of specifying which foreign powers are behind the hybrid attacks.

World.title: Magyar’s party backs former supreme court head for Hungarian president
World.content:
The Hungarian Parliament is set to vote on András Baka's candidacy next Tuesday. | Tibor Illyes/EPA

Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s ruling Tisza party said on Saturday that it had nominated former Supreme Court President András Baka to become the country’s next president.

Baka, who worked as a judge on the European Court of Human Rights before being elected to head the Supreme Court, was removed from his post by the Fidesz government in 2011 — a move the ECHR ruled was unlawful.

“Throughout his career, Dr. András Baka has considered the principle of the separation of powers to be of paramount importance and has consistently stood up for the rule of law and judicial independence,” Tisza said in a Facebook post.

World.title: Sánchez-Meloni clash brings back borders — and headaches for tourists
World.content:
Madrid has pushed back forcefully against that narrative, and noted that the migrants could not leave the North African territory because they lack valid IDs required to travel on ferries to mainland Europe.

Spanish authorities and the European Commission this week confirmed that none of the 72,000 people who surged into Ceuta have crossed the Strait of Gibraltar. During a meeting of EU interior ministers on Tuesday, Italian Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi publicly praised Spain for its handling of the situation and expressed Rome’s “sincere solidarity” with Madrid.

Yet despite requests from Madrid, the Italian government has declined to end border checks even after it became clear that there was no risk of the Ceuta crisis spilling into the rest of Europe. Rome’s inaction prompted Spain to issue a statement on Friday threatening to adopt “proportional measures” if Rome did not change course by Aug. 9.

After Meloni’s office responded by declaring “Italy does not accept ultimatums or demands from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Madrid moved to reintroduce its own controls.

Magnus Brunner, the European commissioner for internal affairs and migration, sought to mediate in the dispute.

“I was in contact with both the Spanish and Italian Interior Ministers today. Both confirmed that the internal border controls are temporary,” Brunner said in a post on X. “I stressed the progress we’ve made on tackling illegal migration and that trust between Member States is our most valuable currency.”

World.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 12, wound over 80 overnight
World.content:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the drone attacks killed three people — a 3-year-old child and the child’s grandparents — in a village in the Kyiv region. The six ballistic missiles struck civilian infrastructure in Kyiv, killing one person, he said.

“More pressure is needed. New sanctions that will prevent the production of these ballistic missiles,” Zelenskyy said on X. “And we definitely need more protection for our people,” he added, appealing to allies to provide missile interceptors to strengthen Ukraine’s defenses against Russia’s aerial assault.

In the Zaporizhzhia region, in southeast Ukraine, three people were killed and four were wounded following the overnight attack, regional governor Ivan Fedorov said.

A further five people were killed and nearly 50 people wounded in the regions of Kharkiv, Donetsk and Kherson, according to regional authorities.

Separately, Zelenskyy visited Serbia on Saturday — his first trip to the country since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine — to meet with President Aleksandar Vučić and Prime Minister Đuro Macut.

Zelenskyy said the talks had focused on rebuilding infrastructure, readying a free-trade agreement this year, and preparing for the winter to come.

This article has been updated.

World.title: Gabriel Attal alleges Russian interference in French presidential race
World.content:
Gabriel Attal attends a session of questions to the government at the National Assembly, in Paris on Jan. 6, 2026. | Christophe Petit Tesson/EPA

Attal becomes the latest contender to file a complaint over alleged Russian interference ahead of the April 2027 presidential vote.

Former prime minister and presidential candidate Gabriel Attal has filed a complaint over an alleged Russian disinformation campaign ahead of next year’s French presidential election, local news outlets reported on Saturday.

Attal’s lawyers told French media that the complaint, filed on Friday, denounces “acts of foreign interference, manipulation of information, fabrication of content likely to undermine the fundamental interests of the nation and the sincerity of the upcoming presidential election.”

They told BFMTV that several accounts on social network X, some of which impersonated French and international media, had disseminated fake video reports and newspaper articles attributing false statements to Attal that were “intended to discredit him as a candidate.”

World.title: Latest news bulletin | August 9th, 2026 – Evening
World.content: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond in this Euronews news bulletin. In just a few minutes, our newsroom brings you the latest news and breaking news across world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel, with the context you need to make sense of a fast-moving day. Reported with the independence and the European perspective that define Euronews, this regular round-up gives you a clear and reliable overview of the stories shaping our world right now, wherever you are watching from.

World.title: Over 20,000 flee wildfires as British Columbia declares state of emergency
World.content:
Over 20,000 people have been forced to flee fast-moving wildfires raging across western Canada, prompting British Columbia to declare a state of emergency on Saturday as officials warned of "explosive" conditions that could put more communities at risk.

 

Residents were evacuated from Summerland, home to about 12,000 people, and Peachland, home to 8,000, along the Okanagan Lake.

The so-called "Bald Range Fire" was discovered on Friday and nearly doubled in size overnight into Saturday, forcing even emergency officials to flee.

“I had to leave the Emergency Operations Centre to come and get my family to leave this area. We’re heading south,” Erick Thompson, an emergency official with the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen said in a video posted early Saturday.

In a news conference on Saturday, Premier David Eby said a firefighting official compared the fire to a "bomb going off".

BC wildfires escalated fast, like a 'bomb going off'

"The fire goes across the top of the trees," Eby said recounting the official's description, adding that "he described flames on 100-foot (30.5 metres) tree, flames going 200 feet (61 metres) above that, and the fire creating its own weather system, which creates lightning, which then feeds on itself".

While tens of thousands fled, search and rescue teams continued efforts to look for residents that were trapped as the fire advanced.

"Air evacuations are underway for people who remain isolated behind the fire perimeter," Eby said.

Hot spots from the Bald Range wildfire burn on the mountainside above houses in Summerland, British Columbia, late Saturday, Aug. 8, 2026. Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press via AP

National police are also investigating a potential death near Summerland, but current hazardous conditions have prevented authorities from confirming the death.

No official figures have been released yet on casualties or damage caused by the fires.

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney thanked firefighters and first responders on X for "working tirelessly to keep people safe".

"The federal government stands ready to help and support the Government of British Columbia in these efforts," Carney added.

As of early Sunday, a total of 102 wildfires were reported across the province, the BC Wildfire Service reported.

Many wildfires remain out of control amid extreme heat, strong winds and prolonged drought conditions across the country.

So far this year, wildfires have burned nearly 4 million hectares across Canada, according to the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre.

Researchers warn that human-caused climate change doubled the likelihood of extreme fire conditions behind this years Canadian wildfires.

World.title: Over 1 million evacuated as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
World.content:
China's east coast has been preparing for the storm's arrival in recent days, with work and transport services suspended in some areas along its predicted path.

 

The centre of the typhoon moved over the coastline near Yuhuan City in Zhejiang Province at about 5:30 pm (09:30 GMT), China's National Meteorological Centre said in an online post.

Maximum wind speeds near the centre were more than 150 kilometres per hour at the time it made landfall, the NMC said. Parts of central and eastern Zhejiang could receive 250 to 500 mm of rain.

Authorities relocated more than 900,000 residents from the city of Wenzhou and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

Nearly 1,400 flights in and out of Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled on Sunday, state broadcaster CCTV reported.

Hangzhou's airport in nearby Zhejiang province saw 270 inbound and outbound flights cancelled, the report said.

Heavy rain, strong winds

The effects were felt as far away as Hong Kong on China's southern coast, where the weather observatory posted a record high temperature of 36.9°C, caused by warm air pushed over the city by Typhoon Dolphin.

With the storm "moving towards the vicinity of Zhejiang and moving inland, its outer subsiding air will persistently bring extremely hot weather to the territory today to Tuesday", the Hong Kong Observatory said.

A woman struggles with her umbrella in strong wind and rain ahead of Typhoon Dolphin at Huangpu District of Shanghai on Sunday, 9 August 2026. Wang Xiang/Xinhua via AP

Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain and strong winds to Japan's Okinawa before reaching China.

Seven people in Okinawa suffered minor injuries, including a man aged over 100 who was blown over by gusts, fell to the ground, and hit his head, according to the island's government.

By Sunday afternoon, 5,290 households in Okinawa were without electricity, according to regional utility Okinawa Electric Power.

In Taiwan, dozens of ferry services were suspended, and more than 180 flights were cancelled as the storm brought downpours and strong winds to the island's north on Sunday.

Red alert issued

China's NMC issued a red typhoon alert — its most severe warning — on Sunday morning, forecasting "extraordinary torrential rain" in some areas of central and eastern Zhejiang.

Heavy precipitation is also expected to fall in Shanghai and parts of Fujian, Anhui and Jiangsu provinces through Monday afternoon, it said.

Typhoon Dolphin was expected to weaken after making landfall while moving in a northwesterly direction over eastern China.

In Fujian, nearly 99,000 people were relocated from "risky areas" on Saturday evening ahead of the storm's arrival, state news agency Xinhua reported.

Services on more than 200 ferry routes were suspended in Zhejiang and Fujian, Xinhua said. Work on offshore projects was halted, while 474 construction vessels had been called to port by Friday morning, Xinhua said.

Some train services in affected areas were also suspended on Sunday to ensure passenger safety, state media reported.

Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme heat events more frequent and more intense worldwide.

Typhoon Dolphin's arrival in China comes two weeks after Typhoon Noul lashed southern Guangdong province, declared by authorities at the time as the strongest storm to hit China this year.

Three people were killed, and hundreds of homes were damaged by Typhoon Noul in the Philippines before it reached China.

World.title: 13 killed in Ukraine and 90 injured as Russia intensifies overnight bombardment campaign of Ukrainian cities
World.content:
Russia and Ukraine exchanged strikes overnight that killed civilians and injured many others on both sides, local authorities reported.

 

Large-scale Russian missile strikes on Ukrainian cities have become almost routine in recent weeks, with Moscow exploiting Ukraine’s critical shortage of interceptors for the US-made Patriot systems — the sole air defence weapon in its arsenal able to shoot down ballistic missiles.

In the latest attacks, Ukrainian drones killed five people and injured two dozen others, including a four-year-old boy, in Russia’s border region of Belgorod, according to the regional administration.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says four people were killed in the Kyiv capital region, a three-year-old boy and his grandparents, in one strike, and later another fatality was reported in a separate strike, also on civilian infrastructure.

Emergency services personnel work to extinguish a fire of residential buildings following a Russian missiles attack in Odesa, Ukraine, Sunday, Aug. 9, 2026 Ukrainian Emergency Service via AP/Ukrainian Emergency Service via AP

“More pressure is needed — new sanctions that will prevent Russia from producing these ballistic missiles. And our people absolutely need more protection. Anti-ballistic systems, interceptor missiles for Patriot, SAMP/T, NASAMS, and HAWK systems, as well as our F-16s,” wrote Zelenskyy in a post on the Telegram messaging app.

In Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, Russian missiles struck a high-rise apartment block in the Saltivskyi district, killing three people and injuring 37, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov.

At least six other deaths were reported in strikes on other frontline cities, including Sumy, Kherson and Donetsk in the eastern industrial Donbas region.

Eight more people were injured in Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa after “dozens of missiles and drones” struck the city and surrounding region, according to local administration head Oleh Kiper.

Ukrainian officials say 13 people were killed and approximately 90 others were injured in Russian attacks over the past 24 hours.

Rescuers evacuate an injured civilian after a residential building was hit following Russia's drone attack in Kharkiv, Ukraine, Sunday, Aug. 9, 2026 Andrii Marienko/Copyright 2026 The AP. All rights reserved.

Zelenskyy has for months lobbied other countries, especially the United States, to send Ukraine more Patriot systems, made scarcer by the Iran war, arguing they are crucial for defending civilians.

Failing that, Zelenskyy wants to make Patriot ammunition in Ukraine or get approval from Elon Musk to use his Starlink satellite communications system to guide strikes inside Russia that can hit its missile launchers.

Meanwhile, Kyiv has kept up long-range drone strikes against Russian energy infrastructure, as well as the country’s largest online retailer, Wildberries, and other targets deep inside Russia, sparking a fuel crisis.

Russia’s defence ministry on Sunday claimed its overnight strikes hit drone warehouses in the Kharkiv region, as well as fuel depots and stores of other materiel belonging to Ukraine’s armed forces at the port of Odesa.

Emergency services personnel work to extinguish a fire of residential buildings following a Russian missiles attack in Odesa, Ukraine, Sunday, Aug. 9, 2026 Ukrainian Emergency Service via AP/Ukrainian Emergency Service via AP

It said its forces had shot down 153 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday, including over Russian-occupied Crimea and the Black and Azov seas.

In Russia's Belgorod region, authorities said Ukrainian drone strikes damaged 29 apartment blocks and five private houses, as well as administrative buildings and unspecified “commercial facilities.”

Debris from Ukrainian drones also fell on two enterprises and a private home in the Russian city of Novorossiysk, mayor Andrey Kravchenko said on Sunday.

A major fuel terminal is located at Novorossiysk that links Kazakhstan's oil fields to markets around the world, and which has previously been a target for Ukrainian strikes, as Kyiv looks to suffocate the Kremlin’s energy sector, which it believes to be the financial arm of its invasion.

World.title: Israel 'rejects' the US ceasefire plan for Gaza accepted by Hamas
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the latest US roadmap accepted by Hamas to launch the second phase of the Gaza peace plan, taking fresh distance from President Donald Trump as he faces razor-tight elections.

 

After more than a week of gradually escalating criticism of the plan, Netanyahu explicitly opposed it in the face of pushback from his right-wing base.

The Israeli government says any withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Gaza Strip is conditional on the Islamist group being "genuinely" disarmed.

"Israel rejects the 15-point document" presented at the end of July by Donald Trump’s Peace Council, Benjamin Netanyahu said during a cabinet meeting.

The Israeli army would carry out "no withdrawal as long as Hamas is not genuinely disarmed and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and our citizens," Netanyahu said.

US efforts ditched

Israeli PM described Trump, with whom he has also had a growing break on Iran, as "our greatest friend in the White House" — but quickly made clear he was willing to challenge him.

He said Israel was raising its objections to the Gaza plan with the United States.

"They have ideas; some of them are acceptable to us, and some are not, and we know how to stand our ground on these matters," he said.

Hamas, days after selecting a new leader, Khalil al-Hayya, announced it supported the Gaza plan. It called on the United States to pressure Netanyahu.

"We expect the mediators and the American guarantor to pressure Netanyahu and his government to adhere to the roadmap and not obstruct the process for internal political and electoral reasons," Bassem Naim, a member of Hamas's political bureau, told AFP.

Growing friction with Trump

Netanyahu until recently campaigned on the strength of his relationship with Trump, who since his first term has taken unprecedented steps to back Israel, including moving the US embassy to Jerusalem.

Trump joined Netanyahu in late February in attacking Iran. But the two diverged when Trump sought a ceasefire with Iran in April, as the war sapped his popularity at home and sent oil prices soaring.

Netanyahu told his cabinet that "with an agreement or without an agreement, as long as I am prime minister, Iran will not have nuclear weapons", a goal he has long alleged Tehran is pursuing.

Netanyahu last week also ordered fresh strikes on Lebanon in response to what Israel called a ceasefire violation by Iran-backed Hezbollah, just as Israel and Lebanon were holding US-mediated talks.

The Gaza plan was the latest stage in a US-brokered ceasefire announced in October that has reduced but not ended Israeli operations in Gaza.

Trump had described, as a "major milestone," the agreement by Hamas to surrender weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing body.

Netanyahu's base scorn plan

The plan said Israel would begin pulling out forces in tandem with the disarmament, a timeline adamantly rejected by Israel.

After meeting Netanyahu last week, Trump's body implementing the deal, dubbed the Board of Peace, backtracked and said Israel would only need to withdraw after "complete" disarmament, but it was apparently not enough for the Israeli leader.

Netanyahu said that Hamas must give up all of its weapons.

"We are talking about real disarmament, not fictitious disarmament," Netanyahu said.

Polls show that the Gaza plan is widely unpopular with Netanyahu's right-wing base and far-right members of his cabinet, who have urged him to call a new vote to kill the Gaza plan.

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader, is running even or trailing in some polls ahead of the 27 October elections, the country's first since the devastating 7 October 2023 attack by Hamas.

World.title: Party in the dry Danube riverbed: many call it a natural disaster
World.content:
In Budapest, the emergence of the so-called Ínség-szikla (Famine Rock) by the Liberty Bridge signals that there is too little water in the Danube. The stretch of riverbed beneath the central pillar of Margaret Bridge is surfacing more and more often each year, and an ever-larger area is left dry.

 

Photographer Zsanett Zsebők shared a video on Facebook of a Saturday night pop-up party, unleashing a flood of comments. Those with a more relaxed outlook say a spontaneous party like this is very cool, even if it takes place on the dried-out central section of the Danube Riverbed. Others see it instead as a horrifying natural disaster that is increasingly reshaping summers in Europe, especially in Hungary.

In 2018, the underwater extension of the Margit Island shoal on the other side of the Margit Bridge, towards the Parliament, became accessible even in shoes. Since then, this has been happening more frequently, for longer periods, and over a larger area.

László Wild, the heritage architect who led the most recent reconstruction of Margaret Bridge, said in an earlier interview that the Danube Riverbed along the Budapest section is in an incredible state of disorder.

In previous years, the same metal rubbish bins that were common in Budapest before the Second World War have always turned up here; even the remains of the pillars from the scaffolding that was presumably used by Ernest Goüin’s team until 1876, during the years of the bridge’s construction.

As the dried-out area expands, more and more people are walking across from Margaret Island. From there, the city’s panorama can be seen from a new angle, looking particularly beautiful in the evening lights. At first, concern about global warming merely left passers-by somewhat taken aback, but now the party crowd has appeared as well.

Legend has it that not only did the band keep playing on the sinking Titanic until the very last moment, but some guests even joked that they wanted to get ice for their cocktails from the iceberg itself. The receding Danube evokes the same duality: in some people it sparks worry and anxiety, in others it brings out the urge to live in the carpe diem spirit.

World.title: Cypriot natural gas flowing to Europe in 2028, says Cyprus Energy Minister
World.content:
Michalis Damianos, Cyprus Minister for Energy, stresses that the Cypriot natural gas now being developed could start flowing to Europe as early as the spring of 2028, something that will help make the European continent more energy independent and also stabilise prices.

 

He also referred to the latest developments regarding Cyprus's electricity interconnection with Greece and the entry of the French company Meridiam, following the sustained interest shown by the French President Emmanuel Macron.

Natural gas 'as soon as March 2028'

European consumers can expect natural gas from an undersea field off Cyprus, which will help meet their energy needs as soon as March 2028, the island nation's energy minister has said.

Michalis Damianos said that the Eastern Mediterranean is rapidly emerging as an alternative source of energy for European countries, as Russia's war in Ukraine and turmoil in the Middle East force the continent to seek new supplies.

Damianos said that partners TotalEnergies of France and Italy's Eni took the final investment decision last month to move ahead with developing the "Cronos" gas field off Cyprus's southern coast. The project will mark the first time that gas from Eastern Mediterranean fields feeds European markets.

"This is important for Europe right now, because of the war in Ukraine and the situation in the Middle East, the fact that Cyprus will be an alternative source of natural gas," Damianos told the Associated Press in an exclusive interview on Friday.

According to the Eni-TotalEnergies consortium's timetable, work to build a pipeline from "Cronos" to existing infrastructure at Egypt's giant "Zohr" gas field, 105 kilometres away, will start later this year and last up to 18 months.

Once completed, the gas will be transported to the processing plant at Damietta on Egypt's northern coast, where it will be liquefied for shipment to Europe.

'First natural gas on stream'

Sending gas from "Cronos" to Egypt for processing was the most economically viable option, at a cost of around $2bn (€1.73bn), or half the estimated cost of developing other gas fields in Cypriot waters because of its proximity to existing infrastructure.

Although the agreement provides that all of the more than 3 trillion cubic feet (84.9 billion cubic metres) of gas from "Cronos" will go to Europe, it includes a clause allowing about one-fifth of that volume to be used to cover part of Egypt's domestic energy needs.

"It is a relatively small reserve," Michalis Damianos said. "Our revenues as a country will not be huge, so its importance does not lie in the money, but in the fact that we are starting to become producers and to bring our first natural gas on stream."

Cyprus's Energy Minister Michalis Damianos on the sidelines of his interview with the Associated Press AP Photo/Petros Karadjias

"Cronos" is one of six gas fields discovered so far within Cyprus's Exclusive Economic Zone, off its southern coast. Two of them, "Glafcos" and "Pegasus", have combined estimated reserves of 6.9 trillion cubic feet (195 billion cubic metres).

ExxonMobil and QatarEnergy, which have been licensed to exploit these fields, say they expect gas from "Glafcos" and "Pegasus" to start flowing by 2033.

"What we can say is that Exxon is the kind of company that keeps to schedules and sometimes even delivers earlier," Damianos said.

The energy minister said that ExxonMobil plans to expand its exploration activities off Cyprus and is expected to obtain an additional licence to search for hydrocarbons.

Another gas field, the first to be discovered off Cyprus about 15 years ago, is "Aphrodite", which holds estimated reserves of 5.6 trillion cubic feet (158 billion cubic metres).

Damianos said that the final investment decision by the Chevron-led consortium on developing the field is expected in the summer of 2027. Under the agreement with Chevron, a pipeline will link the field directly to facilities in Egypt in order to cover that country's domestic energy needs.

Part of the "Aphrodite" field lies in Israeli waters and there is hope that an arbitrator will decide what share Israel is entitled to by next month.

Separate project to connect Israel

Damianos also hailed the entry of French investment company Meridiam as a financier of the "Great Seas Interconnector" project, a power cable that will connect Europe's electricity grid with that of Cyprus and, eventually, Israel.

This ambitious project will not only put an end to the energy isolation of Cyprus and Israel, but will also be a key building block of the "IMEC Initiative", a new energy and trade route to the Gulf and India that the European Union is pursuing.

However, the project has now become mired in bureaucratic procedures because its actual cost exceeds the original estimate of $2.2bn (€1.91bn). A European Investment Bank report, expected to be published in the coming months, will provide clarity on its price tag.

Cyprus's Energy Minister Michalis Damianos during his interview with the Associated Press AP Photo/Petros Karadjias

This is important for Cyprus because, under the current agreement, Cypriot energy consumers would have to cover up to 63% of the cost of building the cable, which would mean a significant increase in electricity prices.

Additional private investment is being sought to offset that burden on Cypriot consumers, while the possibility of further EU funding is also being examined, Damianos said.

The EU has already committed €658 million ($760 million) to the project.

"This is a very important project for Europe because it links Cyprus, which is isolated, with the European grid. And the idea is to then go on and connect with Israel," Damianos said.

World.title: Major oil find off Polish-German border: Warsaw seeks drilling, Germany objects
World.content:
It could be one of the most significant resource discoveries in Poland’s history: about six kilometres from the Polish port city Świnoujście, and thus within sight of the German holiday island of Usedom, lies the Wolin East oilfield.

 

Initial estimates suggest the newly discovered field contains around 22 million tonnes of crude oil and some five billion cubic metres of commercially recoverable natural gas.

The discovery stems from exploratory drilling carried out by Canadian company Central European Petroleum (CEP) in July last year at a depth of more than 2,500 metres.

'Historic moment'

The Canadian company’s chief executive, Rolf G. Skaar, has described the discovery of Wolin East as a "historic moment" for the company and for Poland’s energy sector.

The find has also been seen in Poland as a major opportunity for domestic energy supplies. According to Poland’s chief geologist, Krzysztof Galos, speaking in July 2025, regular production could begin in 2028 or 2029 at the earliest.

Over several years, the deposit could cover around four to five percent of Poland’s annual oil demand. Wolin East could therefore make an important contribution to reducing Poland’s dependence on energy imports and strengthening the country’s security of supply.

In Świnoujście, however, concern is growing about tourism and the environment: authorities and residents are insisting that the region’s appeal be preserved and nature protected.

German campaign alliance against oil extraction in the Baltic Sea

The prospect of extracting fossil fuels is meeting particularly strong resistance from Germany. The non-governmental organisation BUND (German Federation for the Environment and Nature Conservation) in the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania has joined forces with environmental group Deutsche Umwelthilfe (DUH), WWF and the citizens’ initiative Lebensraum Vorpommern in an alliance calling for a general ban on new oil and gas projects in the Baltic Sea.

According to the organisers, some 88,000 signatures had been collected by the end of July this year. The petition is due to be submitted to the European Commission in Brussels in September.

The organisations warn of potential damage to the Baltic’s fragile ecosystem, including underwater noise, pollutant discharges and the risk of an oil spill in protected marine areas.

State election outcome could influence conflict

DUH’s federal managing director, Sascha Müller-Kraenner, is calling for joint action by the federal government, the state and the EU to protect the Bay of Pomerania and the Baltic Sea as a whole:

"So far, the exploratory well has not led to an authorised production project, and that must remain the case. The federal government, the Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state government and the European Union must jointly send a clear message: there must be no new oil and gas extraction directly off Usedom.

Just weeks before the state election, the political parties in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania must also take a clear position and explain how they intend to protect the coast from a new fossil industrial project."

The upcoming state election could play a decisive role in shaping how the conflict develops between Poland’s energy interests and German environmental organisations’ calls for stronger protection for the Baltic Sea.

World.title: Turkey's new opposition party offers hope, but its future is already in jeopardy
World.content:
The launch of the Yeni Party in Turkey promises to energise the country's struggling opposition. But while some polls show it leading, it remains vulnerable – already beset by arrests it says are "politically motivated".

Advertising

In a glitzy video, set to pumping music and shared widely across social media, Ozgur Ozel launched the Yeni Party – "New Party" – vowing to usher in a new era in Turkish politics and end President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s long rule.

Ozel founded the New Party after a court removed him from leading the main opposition party, the Republican People’s Party (CHP).

His rival, former party leader Kemal Kilicdaroglu, 77, who lost every election during his decade in charge of the CHP, replaced him.

Many in the country believe Erdogan played a role in the removal of Ozel, as his popularity grew thanks to tireless campaigning.

Riding the wave

The New Party is settings its sights beyond the CHP’s usual supporters.

"It covers the whole political spectrum in Turkish political life," explains Ozel's advisor Ilham Uzel.

"There are critical elements like democratisation, rule of law, secularism and a pro-Western approach, so we maintain these main pillars. But it is not confined to social democracy; we reach out to every section of Turkish society, including Islamists and conservatives, nationalists and liberals. We have Kurdish supporters."

The New Party is riding a wave of excitement. Ninety-one out of 135 CHP parliamentary deputies have defected to its ranks, joined by dozens of mayors and it is swiftly becoming the main opposition in parliament.

Turkey opposition worries that Europe is sacrificing democracy for security

Some polls show the party soaring above 30 percent, leaving Erdogan’s Justice and Development Party behind, while the CHP’s support has collapsed.

The New Party’s broad approach is finding fertile ground. "Even those who still support the governing coalition, the AK Party and MHP, are unhappy with how things are or how politics is practised, especially regarding economic issues. So there is a push towards change," says political commentator Sezin Oney.

"There is a yearning to change things at the grassroots, and the New Party may be the only party that can represent a new way of doing politics. But they have to live up to it, of course."

Corruption charges

Erdogan has remained in power for more than 20 years partly by exploiting divisions within the opposition, which is made up of conservatives, hardline secularists, and both Kurdish and Turkish nationalists.

The New Party has a key advantage over the strongly secular CHP, whose history is linked to past policies targeting Turkey’s large Kurdish minority and religious conservatives.

"CHP is identified with many bad experiences that the Kurds and conservative people had in past decades," said Mesut Yegen of the Diyarbakir-based Kurdish Studies Center.

"If you look at what Ozgur Ozel says during his speeches, you may clearly see the Yeni Party doesn’t have the baggage of CHP."

Erdogan has also often exploited the CHP’s history, painting it as anti-religious and hostile to Kurdish minority rights. The New Party faces the tricky task of keeping CHP loyalists on board while reaching new supporters.

But for now, simply staying out of jail may be the most pressing concern for its representatives.

Turkey marks a decade since the coup that never was, but never really ended

Several mayors who joined the New Party have been arrested on corruption charges, widely seen as politically motivated. In the past two years, 26 opposition mayors and hundreds of officials have been imprisoned on corruption allegations, compared to two mayors from Erdogan’s AK Party.

"They are cracking down on our party – every other day, mayors are arrested," says Uzgel. "They filed another charge against our leader. Nobody is safe in this authoritarian regime. So Mr Ozel is on the spot, definitely."

Ozel is protected by parliamentary immunity, but Oney warns he may be running out of time.

"Ozgur Ozel might be imprisoned himself once his immunity is removed by a parliamentary vote, that's a possibility. The only immunity he can have is the immunity bestowed upon him by the people. So only public opinion is protecting him. How much can it protect him? We'll see."

With parliament about to break for summer until October, Ozel has a brief window to strengthen his party and rally public support.

World.title: Denmark: Several wounded in suspected gang shooting
World.content:
Police said they believed that the incident was linked to a "settling of scores" within criminal networks.

Several people were wounded on Sunday in a shooting in Denmark.

Police said in a statement they believed that the incident was linked to a "settling of scores" within criminal networks.

"At this time, we cannot provide further information about their condition. The police presumption is that this is a settling of scores within the criminal milieu," the statement read.

Officers had been called to multiple locations in Holbaek, some 70 kilometers (45 miles) west of the capital, Copenhagen.

The incident was reported to police around 3:45 p.m. local time (1345 UTC).

It was initially unclear how many people had been injured or how severe the injuries were.

Police said that the perpetrators were seen leaving the scene in a white car, according to preliminary information.

World.title: Germany news: Berlin to step up drone security research
World.content:
08/09/2026 August 9, 2026 Transport minister wants Deutsch Bahn bonuses tied to punctuality targets

Deutsche Bahn is known for common delays and cancelations Image: picture alliance/Schoening

Germany's new transport minister, Steffen Bilger of the conservative Christian Democrats (CDU), said on Sunday that he planned to step up pressure on notoriously delayed railway operator Deutsche Bahn.

He told the mass-market Bild newspaper that bonus payments for Bahn managers would be impacted if government-set punctuality targets are not met.

"There will be a concrete impact on the bonus payments of rail managers if the targets set by the federal government are not met," Bilger said. "I think rail customers and taxpayers have a right to have success genuinely measured."

Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government is preparing a new financing agreement for the state-owned company that is to tie funding to specific targets.

Bilger was appointed transport minister late in July [FILE: July 20] Image: dts Nachrichtenagentur/IMAGO

Bilger took his ministerial post after Merz reshuffled his Cabinet last month, a move sparked by the resignation of senior conservative lawmaker Jens Spahn over a surrogacy scandal.

Deutsche Bahn is mired in a major structural crisis around delays and cancellations. In 2025, only 60% arrived on time or experienced delays of under six minutes, not including trains that were canceled or ended their journeys prematurely.

The center-left Social Democrats (SPD), who are junior coalition partners in Merz's government, expressed support for the planned measure.

"I expressly welcome the fact that Transport Minister Bilger wants to link the bonus payments of rail managers to punctuality," the SPD's Isabel Cademartori told the Tagesspiegel newspaper.

"People expect the railway to become more reliable," she said. "As politicians, we are providing record investments in infrastructure and expect this to be reflected in punctuality."

World.title: German kidnapped in Niger released — Algeria
World.content:
Algeria says a German citizen has been released after a "criminal armed group" kidnapped him in Niger two weeks ago.

Algeria said on Saturday that a German citizen kidnapped by an armed criminal group some two weeks ago in neighboring Niger was safe and in the hands of the Algerian military.

The German national was taken in charge by the Algerian army's security services on Friday, according to a statement from the Defense Ministry shared on the official Algerian news agency.

He has now been taken on a special flight from Guezzam in the far south to the Boufarik military base near the capital Algiers, it said, adding that he was in "good health" and would be handed to German authorities "at a later date."

No details were provided on how the German national was freed.

A spokesperson for the German Foreign Ministry told DW it was aware of the case, but added that the government "does not comment on cases involving the abduction of German citizens abroad."

Niger, which has been under military rule since a July 2023 coup, has in the past few years been wracked by violence from jihadis linked to the al-Qaeda or the "Islamic State" (IS) terrorist groups.

World.title: Canada: British Columbia wildfires burning out of control
World.content:
Wildfires have grown in number and intensity across British Columbia, where a state of emergency has been declared. Evacuations are underway, but firefighters say almost half of BC's 102 fires are out of control.

Wildfires raging in the western Canadian province of British Columbia gained momentum, growing significantly in both scale and intensity in a situation already declared a state of emergency on Saturday by British Columbia Minister of Emergency Management and Climate Readiness Kelly Greene.

By Sunday morning, the BC Wildfire Service reported 102 active blazes in the province (up from 70 on Saturday), nearly half of them out of control.

"Over the last 24 hours, extreme fire behavior was seen in southern BC due to the continuous hot and dry conditions," the service said, adding that response efforts were being hampered by "elevated fire behavior coupled with severely poor visibility."

Some 20,000 people have been forced to evacuate because of the fires Image: Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press/AP Photo/picture alliance

The Bald Range fire — which exploded Saturday and enveloped the 12,000-resident Summerland area — had consumed nearly 10,341 hectares (25,552 acres) of land by early Sunday.

The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said Sunday that it was "investigating to confirm" a possible fatality.

Officials have yet to provide casualty or damage figures, nor have they published a list of missing persons.

British Columbia Premier David Eby, who warned of the dangerous and unpredictable nature of the blaze on Saturday, said, "air evacuations are underway for people who remain isolated behind the fire perimeter."

"To everyone affected, you are not facing this alone," said Eby in a statement, "the entire province is with you."

Canadian media reported the airlifting of more than 50 people from the community of Faulder.

In all, more than 20,000 people have been forced to evacuate the area.

On Saturday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney took to X to thank firefighters and first responders for "working tirelessly to keep people safe."

Carney also pledged solidarity, writing: "The federal government stands ready to help and support the government of British Columbia in these efforts. I'm keeping everyone forced from their homes in my thoughts and hoping they can return safely soon."

World.title: Divers in Italy find ancient Roman shipwreck, amphorae off coast of Sicily believed to be 2,100 years old
World.content:
The wreck is believed to be more than 2,000 years old. Italy's culture minister says it is "one of the most important underwater archaeological" finds in years.

Divers have discovered an ancient Roman shipwreck off the coast of Sicily, Italian police said.

The shipwreck is believed to be 2,100 years old.

The wreck had been found approximately three nautical miles off the coast of Mazaro del Vallo in western Sicily at a depth of 46 meters (150 feet), police said in a statement .

The cultural protection arm of the Italian police (Carabinieri) called it a "significant underwater archaeological site." It added that initial surveys had "identified a Roman shipwreck presumably dating to between the 2nd and 1st centuries BC."

Italian Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli has called the find "one of the most important underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years."

The site also contains "hundreds" of amphorae, which would likely have been used to transport wine.

The diver who found the wreck said he stumbled across hundreds of 'perfectly intact' amphorae Image: Italian Carabinieri Press Office/AFP

How was the ancient Roman shipwreck discovered?

The shipwreck was found after a tip-off from local fishermen. Calling it the "most incredible discovery of my life," Giacomo De Mola described on Instagram how he had stumbled upon the ancient wreck, which he said at first looked like "a simple rock."

"Visibility isn't great. I see a large dark mass and think, 'Just another big rock…' I get even closer. And my heart stops. It wasn't a rock. Beneath me lay an immense expanse of amphorae — hundreds of amphorae that have lain on the seafloor for over 2,000 years. A Roman ship slumbering in the silence of the Mediterranean," De Mola said.

In the post, the diver also included footage of the find.

Local media report that the ship is 21 meters long and 6 meters wide, and that it was mainly transporting Dressel 1A amphorae, tall cylindrical ceramic jars that were mainly used to carry wine.

De Mola said Lamboglia 2 amphorae, presumably from North Africa, as well as a Neo-Punic amphora, were also found.

"An extraordinary testament to the Mediterranean trade routes of over 2,000 years ago," the diver said.

08/09/2026 August 9, 2026 Syria says it reached deal with Russia on future of Tartous and Hmeimim bases

Following 18 months of negotiations, Syria and Russia reached a memorandum of understanding to settle the future of Russian bases at Tartous and Hmeimim, the Syrian Foreign Ministry announced.

According to the ministry's statement, cited by the official SANA news agency, the Syrian state will take over management of civilian facilities, including the Hmeimim airport and the commercial berth at the Tartous port. This will allow the facilities to be gradually integrated into the country's civilian administration.

Meanwhile, military facilities will be repurposed as joint training and qualification centers under new arrangements that preserve the interests of both sides. The transition is expected to be completed within three months, the ministry said.

The Hmeimim airbase and the Tartus naval base are Russia's only two official military bases outside of the former Soviet Union.

During the 13-year civil war in Syria, Russia was a key ally of former Syrian leader Bashar Assad, providing vital military support that helped keep Assad's forces in power.

World.title: Ukraine and Russia exchange attacks as Kyiv buys new ATACMS
World.content:
Overnight drone and missile attacks killed several and injured dozens more in both Ukraine and Russia. As Kyiv seeks to defend itself it has now reportedly finalized a deal to buy US missile systems from Turkey.

Overnight drone and missile attacks have killed several people and injured dozens more according to various local authorities in Ukraine and Russia.

In the southern Russian city of Belgorod, near the Ukrainian border, at least five people were killed and 25 injured.

Belgorod's acting governor said that several apartment blocks had been hit overnight and images posted to social media showed several fires.

Belgorod is a key logistics hub for Russian offensives in Kharkiv and the Donbass.

Russian authorities, who said more than 150 Ukrainian drones had been downed by their forces overnight, also reported attacks on the Black Sea ports of Novorossiysk and Gelendzhik.

Novorossiysk is home to key Russian oil export facilities.

'Russia continuing its war on global food security' says Zelenskyy

Russian attacks targeted oil refineries in the Sumy region as well as the port city of Odesa, where President Voldymyr Zelenskyy said at least eight people had been injured.

The Odesa strikes targeted oil facilities in the southern port.

Odesa is also one of Ukraine's most important agricultural export hubs.

Zelenskyy said that with Sunday's attack, "Russia is continuing its war on global food security."

Two people were also killed and at least 21 injured in a Russian attack on Kharkiv in eastern Ukraine, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov.

Across the border, Russia claimed its forces had taken control of two villages in eastern Donetsk, though the claim could not be independently verified.

Ukraine calls on allies to help with air defenses To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Kyiv arming itself against 4-year Russia invasion

As Russia's war on Ukraine drags on toward the five-year mark, Kyiv is again short on defensive weapons.

Kyiv has desperately sought to acquire more medium and long-range weapons systems from the US with mixed results.

Now, Ukraine is turning to Turkey for help as the US reportedly depletes its own stockpiles with its still unresolved war in Iran.

On Sunday, Ukraine's military news outlet Militarnyi reported that it would be purchasing 70 ATACMS and 12 M270 multiple-launch rocket systems from Turkey in an order that will also include more than 2,500 227mm rockets with cluster-munitions payloads.

The US, which has 30 days to approve the sale, estimates its total value at $283 million (€245 million).

The ATACMS in question are of an older design, with a range limited to 165 kilometers (102.5 miles).
