World.title: EKRE head: Ülle Madise's election in the Riigikogu could be contested in court
World.content:
Martin Helme said his party would not support Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise as a potential candidate in the presidential election and that the chancellor's conflict of roles in the election could lead to the result being challenged in court.

"Ülle Madise has now essentially declared herself a presidential candidate because she is bargaining with the Riigikogu to secure cross-party support. She does not have that support, because at the very least our party does not support her election," Helme wrote on social media.

"At the same time, she has a very serious conflict of interest by indicating that she wants the support of all parties while serving as chancellor of justice, who oversees the work of parliament," he said, adding that such a conflict of roles could result in the election result being challenged in court if Madise is elected.

The EKRE chair said Madise's potential candidacy creates a bad impression.

"The chancellor of justice is playing a game in which she acts as though she is not a candidate, thereby avoiding the debate and heightened media and public scrutiny that should be a matter of course for someone seeking high office. At the same time, she is consistently signaling that she is interested in the office, provided the votes for her are already secured," Helme said.

He said Madise has systematically passed up opportunities to say that she will not run and is not interested in doing so. "Today (Saturday — ed.), she once again confirmed that she is interested in the presidency, except that she wants to see sufficient support first."

"This kind of game allows her to pop up as a candidate at the last minute and, assuming the votes are indeed secured, walk straight in through the back door of Kadriorg. As I said, all of this is very poor form and flagrantly at odds with the basic principles of democracy," the EKRE chair added.

Helme said EKRE is the only party to have approached the presidential election seriously and professionally, while also treating voters with respect. He emphasized that the party nominated Mart Helme as its candidate in the spring.

"I continue to urge people to support Estonia's only official presidential candidate, Mart Helme," he concluded.

Eesti 200 Chair Kristina Kallas said Thursday that Madise currently has the support of 67 members of the Riigikogu and that Züleyxa Izmailova, who left Eesti 200 and joined the Social Democrats, does not support Madise. Izmailova, however, told ERR that the vote is secret and that she would not stand in the way of electing a president.

The Riigikogu's Council of Elders will discuss the presidential election Tuesday.

At least 21 members of the Riigikogu are required to nominate a presidential candidate. A candidate would need at least 68 votes to be elected president by the Riigikogu.

Key dates:

• Aug. 21-24: Candidate nominations

• Sept. 2: First round of voting in the Riigikogu

• Sept. 3: Second and third rounds of voting in the Riigikogu, if necessary

World.title: Estonia's warming bodies of water catering to fish parasites
World.content:
Although many parasites have always coexisted with fish in Estonia, encounters with heat-loving parasites in particular can pose a serious threat to populations of cold-water salmonids.

An expedition by Estonian University of Life Sciences researchers to Greenland and the Faroe Islands found that the parasite that causes a dangerous and currently incurable kidney disease in salmonids has spread much farther north than previously known. However, Anti Vasemägi, professor of fish genetics and genomics at the Estonian University of Life Sciences, said it is not known when the parasite, Tetracapsuloides bryosalmonae, reached the area. The parasite was first detected in Estonia nearly 30 years ago.

"But we still don't know, for example, when it reached Estonia. In Iceland, meanwhile, the parasite has spread rapidly over the past couple of decades, and this has also been linked to rising water temperatures," Vasemägi said.

Vasemägi noted that in Estonia, both warm-water fish and heat-loving parasites are currently thriving.

"When a cold-water fish encounters a parasite that prefers warmer water, it can end badly for the fish. In Estonia, this parasite causes the greatest mortality among juvenile trout, specifically in rivers where water temperatures have been altered by human activity. As we know, people have built many dams on rivers, straightened large sections of rivers and even cut down trees along riverbanks. All of this warms the water and raises its temperature," Vasemägi said.

According to Vasemägi, recent studies indicate that many parasites found farther south are reaching Estonia via migratory birds.

"For example, our new project funded by the Estonian Research Council will examine the spread of parasites associated with cormorants and a possible increase in their abundance in coastal waters."

The Estonian Federation of Fishing Clubs said there is nothing particularly unusual happening in Estonia. Vasemägi also noted that parasites are found in all fish species in Estonia and that fish generally cope well with them.

"It can be said that an extremely small proportion of our fish parasites can be dangerous to humans, and only if the fish has not been properly prepared. The rule of thumb is that people should avoid eating raw fish and fish roe, but fish that has been sufficiently heated or salted poses no danger to humans. So if fish is properly baked, boiled, salted or dried, there is no danger," Vasemägi said.

Vasemägi added that if anglers notice anything unusual about a fish, they can always send a photo to researchers at the Estonian University of Life Sciences and ask for advice.

World.title: Estonia's parties betting on tax cuts, AI and demographics ahead of 2027 elections
World.content:
Reviving Estonia's economy, reversing the decline in the birth rate and ensuring national security emerged as the key issues ahead of the 2027 elections at Opinion Festival's party chairmen debate.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) highlighted national defense and revitalizing the economy as his most important goals.

"When I formed the government, I promised two things: first, that Estonia would be firmly defended. To the extent that it is in our hands, it certainly is. We have had to do many different things to fund defense spending, and we are probably now paying a price for that in terms of popularity — there is no doubt about it. But I think that when history looks back, what matters is what you have done, not what people happen to be saying at the moment," the prime minister began.

Michal's second point was economic growth, which he said cannot be credited solely to the government or politicians.

"It is certainly cyclical, and as a small, open economy we are particularly dependent on our partners. But economic growth means that people and businesses have more money on payday. At the beginning of this year, Estonia saw the largest tax cut in its history, which certainly provided this momentum. We want to pursue the same policy — Estonia is defended, the economy grows and the people of Estonia become wealthier," Michal emphasized.

The prime minister's third priority was looking to the future, including a clean natural environment, new technologies and innovation.

"And also a sound set of values. I am under no illusions — I understand that these elections will be a repeat performance by the same old EKRE-IKE band (former coalition of EKRE, Isamaa and the Center Party — ed.) /.../ We want to preserve the same liberal democratic values on which Estonia was built. Estonia has been a forward-looking country, not one that looks to the past for solutions," Michal concluded.

Opinion Festival 2026. Prime Minister Kristen Michal and Eesti 200 head Kristina Kallas. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Isamaa

Urmas Reinsalu, chair of the Isamaa party that currently tops party ratings, said trust needs to be restored in society, starting with the country's economic outlook.

"Generating economic growth cannot simply be a slogan; it has to begin with restoring optimism among investors and entrepreneurs. Isamaa's first message is that, unfortunately, the government has done everything it can to suppress that economic growth. Economic policy cannot be based on simply making the economic outlook more fragile. That has to change fundamentally; we need a fundamentally different approach," Reinsalu said.

Reinsalu's second priority was providing families with a sense of security and restoring the purchasing power of families and individuals, while also giving people the freedom to start families and develop themselves.

"Third is an unconditional commitment to Estonia's national defense. Isamaa has always supported — whether in opposition or in government — the steps necessary to restore and ensure Estonia's military security, internal security and civil protection. We intend to continue doing so unconditionally after the elections," Reinsalu said.

Parempoolsed

Non-parliamentary Parempoolsed chair Lavly Perling said she had been making the same point for four years: words are not enough; they must be turned into action.

"When we talk about defense spending, it cannot be the case that only 27 percent of the taxes collected for it actually get there. Words are not enough; decisions and actions are needed. We have said very clearly that our Estonia is free, prosperous and Estonian-minded. How do we achieve that? Through lower taxes and greater freedom — more freedom, fewer taxes. When we talk about tax increases, we are talking about taking away people's freedom to decide for themselves how to use their own money," Perling said.

Perling said government spending needs to be cut to restore people's sense of security.

"We need to start talking about the fact that our state budget is on an unsustainable course. Everywhere you turn, you are starting to hear what I have called a marketplace of promises. Urmas promises lower taxes and more benefits, while on the other side we once again hear the same kinds of promises we heard four years ago. We are not offering sweet talk; we are saying that we need to start making difficult decisions. We need to do that so the next generation inherits a prosperous and exciting Estonia — that is what drives our decisions," Perling emphasized.

EKRE chair Martin Helme said Estonia's biggest concern is its natural population growth, as well as demographics more broadly.

EKRE

"If we look at what has just happened again in Spain, the immigration crisis that EKRE was talking about 10 or 11 years ago has not gone anywhere. Over the past decade, more than 50 million Africans and Muslims have arrived in Europe. This is no joke. We talk about having an immigration crisis in Estonia, with various illegal immigrants scurrying back and forth; the situation remains critical and is getting increasingly horrific. Addressing immigration at the level of the nation-state and the national border is extremely important. Hiding behind the Schengen border means, quite frankly, abandoning your responsibility for Estonia's security and the safety of its people," Helme said, adding that immigration is only one part of the problem, because if Estonia fails to raise its birth rate, the country has no future.

Opinion Festival 2026. Kristina Kallas and EKRE chair Martin Helme. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

"If Estonia has no future, it no longer makes any difference who carries on here — whether Chinese, Arabs or Ukrainians. Everything else, whether tax debates or security debates, becomes irrelevant, because if there are no Estonians left here, all of this becomes someone else's problem. Natural population growth is therefore critically important, and that means family and population policy," Helme explained.

Helme said the coalition had failed on national defense because it had spent large amounts of money without having anything to show for it.

"First you drove the Estonian economy into contraction for 13 consecutive quarters, and now you are crowing because it has posted a small increase for a second quarter in a row. The people who messed things up cannot be the ones to fix them. Donald Trump shows us the way on economic growth: low taxes and little regulation. Of course, if the earlier question was what we should give up, there are some very easy choices. We will give up the green transition, give up Rail Baltica and give up hundreds of millions in foreign aid that, in reality, makes its way back through corrupt channels," Helme concluded.

Eesti 200

Eesti 200 chair Kristina Kallas said Estonia's economic growth problem is low labor productivity.

"That means that, figuratively speaking, in one hour of work an Estonian can make seven table legs, while a German can make 100. Labor productivity is simply low. The countries that can bring technology into their economies quickly and intelligently will be among the winners. I do not think Estonia should be embarrassed about the state helping businesses invest in AI technologies, whether through guarantees or growth funds. Those wishing to invest in artificial intelligence could receive state-backed loan guarantees or other forms of support from funds. I consider this extremely important because that is where the next leap in economic growth will come from," Kallas said.

Responding to Helme, however, Kallas said the greatest problem of the century is instead climate change and the disasters it causes.

"These affect both our economy and our population, including migration. Moving away from fossil fuels and transitioning as quickly as possible to 100 percent renewable energy production is critically important. This is important not only in terms of fuels, but also for the natural environment and biodiversity," Kallas said.

Center Party

Center Party chair Mihhail Kõlvart said the tax system should not be used simply to collect money so that it can later be redistributed. The tax system should regulate the economy, but Kõlvart said no such system exists today.

"When it comes to the economy, the most important aspect is political decisions that do not regulate the economy but steer it — and in my view, that is not a focus at all today. If we compare ourselves with other countries, such as Latvia, Lithuania and Finland, over the past four years there has been an understanding that there need to be priority sectors in which the state invests, where it changes legislation and provides appropriate regulation," Kõlvart said.

Kõlvart also noted that every coalition agreement over the past 20 years has included a pledge to attract investment, but that there has never been any systematic effort to do so.

Opinion Festival 2026. Urmas Reinsalu, Mihhail Kõlvart and Lavly Perling. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

"Lithuania shows that it can be done. In a short period of time, 300 financial companies have entered the market there and 8,000 jobs with top-level salaries have been created. All of this has a real impact on the economy, and this is not the only sector. It does not work by simply offering artificial intelligence to the economy and expecting it to solve everything. That requires a little intelligence of our own as well. It often involves risk, but you have to take responsibility and identify the sectors that can drive the economy. Lithuania has made those choices, whether in the chemical industry, financial sector, transport or logistics. The state invests, creates a system and then love follows," Kõlvart joked, adding that middle-aged or older men often talk philosophically about love and demographics, when in reality it is a mathematical problem.

"Over the past 35 years, there has not been a single year in which the fertility rate was 2.1. Four years ago it was 1.4; today it is 1.1 or 1.2. This is a mathematical projection, not some kind of rhetoric. If this continues, in 20 years we will have a demographic hole, but the consequences are already here. This must be our nation's top priority," Kõlvart said.

SDE

Social Democratic Party chair Lauri Läänemets said his party's most important priorities for the next electoral term are, above all, ensuring and improving people's well-being.

"That does not apply only to those who are struggling the most; we always talk about the average Estonian family. You could call it an uncompromising economic focus on investment. First and foremost, that means an uncompromising focus on investing in human capital. We know that regardless of which economic expert we listen to — and many people here today have also talked about this — an aging society needs to keep people in the labor market for as long as possible if it wants long-term economic growth," Läänemets said.

According to Läänemets, talk of taking money away from healthcare actually means taking people out of the labor market, as people become sicker and contribute less. He said this is why investment in healthcare and education is needed, including efforts to curb educational inequality and ensure that tuition-free higher education is accessible to everyone.

"Then there are investment incentives for businesses — not only financial support, but diplomatic assistance and all other forms of support as well. We continue to support investment and business activity without compromise. Ultimately, investment is needed in energy and in modern, accessible electricity generation, because this is currently one of the most significant factors holding back Estonia's economy," Läänemets said.

Läänemets also highlighted security, not only in the military sense, but also internal security and people's sense of security.

"When it comes to that sense of security, I would add something that has already been mentioned here and that I think a large part of today's audience also feels — environmental and climate issues. When we talk about having children, we cannot rely on benefits alone, because the issue is one of security. Can I be certain that a child I bring into the world here will have every opportunity in the future? We cannot deny problems in which climate change is already forcing European nuclear power plants to shut down and causing populations to move. Incidentally, I think Martin Helme is looking in the wrong direction when he looks to Africa in discussing the immigration problem. The first climate refugees will come from Southern Europe," Läänemets said.

According to Läänemets, for example, Germans and French people will move to Northern Europe because of the heat and buy up local real estate for large sums of money, which will in turn drive up property prices.

"All of these things are caused by climate change, and action is needed to ensure families — especially young families — have a sense of security and confidence in their future," Läänemets said.

Opinion Festival 2026 Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

World.title: Omniva sends packages to different towns to manage high delivery volumes
World.content:
Omniva is redirecting packages dozens of kilometers away to manage the high number of parcels sent from third countries, saying it helps goods reach customers faster.

While the €3 customs duty added to goods ordered from China and other third countries, introduced in July, has significantly reduced the flood of parcels into Estonia, Omniva is still struggling to deliver all the packages.

When a parcel locker is full, parcel companies often redirect a shipment to another nearby locker. Unfortunately, in the name of faster service, Omniva decided this summer, for example, to send a parcel ordered to Tapa to Rakvere, 35 kilometers away, or instead of Treimani village to Häädemeeste, 20 kilometers away.

Lylian Peek, head of Omniva Estonia's distribution and postal network, said the situation has been caused by large volumes and faster service.

"Parcels are actually redirected relatively rarely. If we look at Omniva's volumes during the day, our sorting line sorts about 200,000 parcels a day, and 1 percent of those are redirected. To be more precise, 0.8 is the exact percentage that is redirected. Redirection is done based on the fact that our sorting process runs through an automated sorting line. When a parcel goes onto the sorting line, the sorting line takes as its basis everything that is in the address on the parcel. However, people always have the option of choosing their preferences, a first preference and a second preference, to specify which parcel locker is their favorite," Peek said.

This means around 1,600 Omniva customers a day do not receive their parcel at the location to which it was ordered. Other companies also redirect parcels.

However, DPD Estonia commercial director Janek Kivimurd said making sure the parcel is delivered to the chosen locker is a priority for the company.

"For Estonians, a parcel locker is one of the most preferred delivery options, because it is convenient to order a parcel there. It is open around the clock and is supposed to help save the customer's time in particular, and any additional journey or burden for the customer understandably causes dissatisfaction," he said.

"Sometimes it happens that a parcel locker unexpectedly fills up or has a technical fault. Around 1 percent of DPD's shipments are like this, and in order not to leave the parcel waiting, we deliver it to the nearest parcel locker, and for DPD the nearest parcel locker means up to one and a half kilometers away. There is certainly no situation where it is sent from one end of Tallinn to the other, or from one end of Narva to the other, or from Pärnu to the other end of Pärnu. That is certainly not our aim," Kivimurd said.

While the examples given at the beginning of the story concerned mainly smaller places where the parcel locker network is relatively sparse anyway, a customer can also be in for an unpleasant surprise in the middle of Tallinn.

"I run my business in Telliskivi and I have also had to collect my parcels, for example, from a parcel locker on Sõpruse puiestee. But the last time it was sent to Tallinn Kaubamaja, which was quite a big surprise because Omniva has post offices closer by both in Kristiine and at Arsenal keskus. It was strange having to go looking for it there," said Omniva customer Tarieli Lipartia from North Tallinn.

Lipartia added that he also asked Omniva for an explanation, but the company was unable to give any reason.

World.title: Iraq poses ultimate test for OPEC+ cohesion following UAE exit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Three months after the United Arab Emirates officially withdrew from OPEC and the broader OPEC+ alliance on May 1, 2026, the producer coalition has maintained its technical cohesion. However, analysis by European foreign policy journal Modern Diplomacy—monitored by IraqiNews.com on Sunday, August 9, 2026—identifies Iraq as the most critical test for the group’s long-term survival.

While OPEC+ successfully unwound its 1.65 million barrels per day (bpd) voluntary production cuts—capped by a sixth consecutive monthly increase of 188,000 bpd scheduled for September 2026—the structural friction that prompted Abu Dhabi’s departure has shifted directly to Baghdad. Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s administration faces growing internal pressure to expand Iraq’s crude output to fund post-war reconstruction, raising strategic questions over its baseline quota within the cartel.

Key Operational Metrics & Market Analysis

The UAE Precedent: Abu Dhabi exited the alliance after investing $150 billion to expand production capacity to 5 million bpd, clashing over its restricted 3.5 million bpd quota. The move reduced OPEC’s global crude market share to approximately 31%.

The Iraqi Baseline Crisis: As OPEC’s second-largest producer (~4.4 million bpd target) and a founding member, Iraq initially signaled in June that it was evaluating its relationship with OPEC. Though the Ministry of Oil later clarified it has “no current intention” to leave, Baghdad continues to press for higher production allowances matching its full output potential.

September Output Allocations: Under the August 2 OPEC+ agreement, the alliance’s top producers approved a final 188,000 bpd monthly bump for September. Allocation breakdowns from August targets show Saudi Arabia at ~10.4 million bpd, Russia at ~9.9 million bpd, and Iraq at ~4.4 million bpd.

Market Impact: Brent crude stabilized in the $84–$90 per barrel range in early August, driven primarily by residual war-risk premiums near the Strait of Hormuz rather than cartel fragmentation fears.

Energy analysts at the Middle East Institute and UBS note that while OPEC+ avoided an immediate breakdown, several member nations are struggling to hit new production targets due to aging infrastructure and regional transit bottlenecks caused by the recent closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

For Iraq, remaining within OPEC+ maintains market discipline during volatile price swings. However, market observers caution that if the gap between Iraq’s rising production capability and its designated quota widens further, Prime Minister al-Zaidi may face renewed domestic pressure to demand a baseline overhaul—a scenario that would present a far greater threat to the cartel’s foundation than the UAE’s exit.

World.title: Baghdad Appeals Court requests immunity removal for MP Nazim Al-Asadi
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Baghdad/Karkh Court of Appeal officially submitted a request to the Iraqi Parliament on Sunday, August 9, 2026, to lift legislative immunity from Member of Parliament Nazim Muhammad Dwaij Al-Asadi. The judicial step paves the way for legal prosecution regarding his direct financial involvement in unlawful public contracts executed with the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs.

According to judicial documents, the request stems from an anti-corruption investigation revealing that MP Nazim Al-Asadi co-founded a private enterprise—Altadamel General Trading, IT, and Contracting LLC—in direct partnership with former Labor Minister Ahmed Al-Asadi. The firm was subsequently granted an exclusive private employment agency license by the ministry to recruit, process, and import large volumes of foreign manual labor into Iraq in violation of statutory regulations.

Key Takeaways from the Judicial Filing

Immunity Lift Request: Karkh Court of Appeal formally asked Parliament to strip MP Nazim Al-Asadi’s immunity to face criminal prosecution.

Corporate Conflict of Interest: Investigation confirmed the MP co-founded Altadamel General Trading, IT, and Contracting LLC with former Labor Minister Ahmed Al-Asadi to secure state contracts.

Foreign Labor Monopolization: The firm unlawfully obtained official approvals and recruitment licenses to import large numbers of foreign workers into Iraq for commercial profit.

Linked Legal Actions: The request follows the issuance of two separate arrest warrants for former Labor Minister Ahmed Al-Asadi under public contract fraud (Article 319) and illicit enrichment provisions.

The judicial filing against MP Nazim Al-Asadi underscores the expanding scope of the Central Criminal Court for Combating Corruption as it targets political networks profiting from state ministry operations.

By requesting the removal of parliamentary immunity, the judiciary aims to proceed with formal indictment and asset recovery measures linked to ministry-approved labor recruitment schemes, reinforcing Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s zero-tolerance mandate against high-level administrative graft.

World.title: Baghdad Appeals Court issues two arrest warrants for former Labor Minister Ahmed Al-Asadi
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Baghdad/Karkh Court of Appeal issued two separate arrest and search warrants on Sunday, August 9, 2026, for former Minister of Labor and Social Affairs Ahmed Jassim Saber Al-Asadi on charges of public contract fraud and illicit enrichment.

The legal action by the Central Criminal Court for Combating Corruption follows anti-corruption investigations into Ministry of Labor contracts and unexplained asset growth. The warrants authorize judicial police and law enforcement personnel to arrest Al-Asadi and search his properties.

Key Legal Charges & Statutory Provisions

Public Contract Exploitation: The first warrant charges Al-Asadi under Article 319 of Penal Code No. 111 of 1969 (Amended), alleging he directly profited from ministry contracts and works he oversaw by passing unlawful agreements to secure personal and third-party benefits.

Unexplained Asset Inflation: The second warrant charges him under Article 19(2) of the Integrity and Illicit Gains Commission Law No. 30 of 2011 (Amended) due to an inability to prove the lawful origin of a significant increase in his financial holdings.

Parliamentary Immunity Request: As part of the same investigation, Karkh Court of Appeal Chief Judge Dhiyaa Jaafar requested the Iraqi Parliament to strip immunity from MP Nazim Al-Asadi regarding alleged collusion to set up a private firm for foreign labor recruitment contracts linked to the ministry.

The issuance of official judicial warrants comes weeks after Al-Asadi publicly denied being wanted by the judiciary following a high-profile raid on Baghdad’s “Iraq Gate” residential complex, where authorities seized gold, cash, and luxury assets.

The court’s decision signals a continuing intensification of Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s federal anti-corruption drive, which has targeted former senior officials, ministry executives, and political figures accused of misappropriating state funds.

World.title: Iraqi authorities arrest former Salah Al Din Governor Abu Mazen
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi security forces arrested former Saladin Governor Ahmed Abdullah al-Jubouri, widely known as “Abu Mazen,” in Baghdad on corruption charges, according to official state media reports on Saturday, August 8, 2026.

In a related enforcement action, security personnel subsequently detained prominent businessman Muhammad al-Hajaf, a close associate of al-Jubouri, over allegations of illegally appropriating funds tied to public infrastructure and service contracts across Saladin Governorate.

Key Operational Takeaways

High-Profile Arrests: Former Governor and MP Ahmed al-Jubouri (“Abu Mazen”) detained in Baghdad’s Al-Qadisiyah district alongside associate Muhammad al-Hajaf.

Contract Misappropriation: The ongoing probe centers on the misappropriation of public contract funds and financial irregularities in municipal development projects across Saladin Governorate.

Political Background: Al-Jubouri previously served as Governor of Saladin (2013–2014), Minister of State for Provincial Affairs (2014–2015), and a member of the Iraqi Parliament (2015–2022).

Prior Judicial & International Actions: Al-Jubouri was sanctioned by the U.S. Department of the Treasury in 2019 under the Global Magnitsky Act for official corruption and was subject to a March 2026 domestic arrest warrant following a lawsuit filed by Azem Alliance chief Muthanna al-Samarrai.

The arrest of al-Jubouri—who leads the National Masses Party (Al-Jamahir Al-Wataniya)—marks one of the most high-profile enforcement operations under Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi’s ongoing federal anti-corruption campaign.

Judicial sources indicate that investigations into al-Hajaf’s business entities are examining systemic delays and financial improprieties in municipal infrastructure contracts. Neither al-Jubouri nor al-Hajaf has issued an official statement regarding the charges, as federal prosecutors prepare to submit formal audit findings to the judiciary.

World.title: PM Al-Zaidi and French President Macron discuss economic ties and regional stability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com)— Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi held a high-level telephone discussion with French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday, August 8, 2026, focusing on expanding economic partnerships, regional security, and the conclusion of the international coalition’s military mission in Iraq.

According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the leaders reviewed bilateral cooperation across economic and investment sectors, highlighting expanding opportunities for French corporations within Iraq’s infrastructure and energy markets. Prime Minister al-Zaidi extended an official invitation to President Macron to visit Baghdad to solidify a long-term economic partnership between the two nations.

Key Takeaways from the High-Level Talks

September 30 Coalition Exit Benchmark: Prime Minister al-Zaidi reiterated that September 30, 2026, serves as the definitive deadline for the withdrawal of international coalition military forces from Iraq, noting that concluding the mission allows Baghdad to focus completely on economic development.

Sovereignty & Regional Stability: Al-Zaidi stressed Iraq’s commitment to balanced regional diplomacy, asserting that Iraqi territory will not be utilized to threaten neighboring states, while calling for dialogue to resolve ongoing Middle East conflicts.

French Corporate Investment: The discussions highlighted expanding trade and investment channels for French enterprises across national energy, logistics, and infrastructure sectors.

French Support for Governance Reforms: President Macron reaffirmed France’s commitment to supporting Iraq’s anti-corruption initiatives, fiscal reforms, counter-terrorism cooperation, and security force capacity building.

Prime Minister al-Zaidi emphasized during the call that his administration is focused on transforming Iraq into an influential economic hub linking global trade routes, backed by the country’s strategic location and natural resources.

President Macron praised the Iraqi government’s structural economic reforms and confirmed Paris’s continued support for Iraq’s institutional stability and military modernization as the transition toward a purely bilateral security relationship nears completion.

World.title: Iraq oil exports drop 75% amid Hormuz closure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Oil Minister Hayan Abdul-Ghani announced on Saturday, August 8, 2026, that the nation’s crude oil exports have plummeted by 75% due to the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz and regional military escalations. The severe drop in oil revenues has triggered a liquidity squeeze across the federal government, causing widespread delays in state employee salary disbursements.

Speaking at a press conference in Baghdad, Abdul-Ghani revealed that Iraq is currently exporting only a quarter of its pre-war volumes, which stood at approximately 3.5 million barrels per day (bpd) prior to the outbreak of regional hostilities on February 28. He noted that while Baghdad has engaged in diplomatic talks with Iran to permit the passage of Iraqi oil shipments through the Gulf, no operational agreement has been activated.

Key financial and operational highlights

Export Collapse: Iraq’s crude exports have fallen to ~25% of pre-war capacity, cutting off the primary source of state revenue.

Fiscal Pressure & Salary Delays: Reduced export volumes and below-budget sale prices have caused acute liquidity shortages, delaying public sector payrolls.

Corporate Damage Compensation: Domestic Attacks: Baghdad has agreed to compensate foreign energy companies for damages resulting from attacks originating inside Iraqi territory. External Strikes: The government declared itself legally exempt from compensating firms for damages caused by foreign strikes or broader military actions beyond state control.

Alternative Export Bypasses: Baghdad is fast-tracking pipeline infrastructure projects bypassing the Persian Gulf, including routes south toward Turkey’s Ceyhan port, Syria’s Baniyas terminal, and Jordan’s Aqaba port.

To maintain minimal cash flows, Iraq is currently forced to sell its crude at deep price concessions below the baseline benchmark set in the national budget, compounding treasury deficits.

In response to the prolonged maritime chokehold in the Strait of Hormuz, the Ministry of Oil is accelerating infrastructure development along overland export routes.

Priority has been placed on expanding and constructing pipeline corridors connecting southern production hubs to the Mediterranean via Syria and Turkey, alongside long-term transit planning toward the Red Sea via Jordan.

World.title: Iraq activates Kirkuk oil field development contract with BP
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Saturday, August 8, 2026, the official activation of its Kirkuk oilfield development contract with British energy giant BP. The project aims to elevate crude oil production from its current capacity of 320,000 barrels per day (bpd) to a peak target of 420,000 bpd.

Ministry of Oil Spokesperson Salim Al-Rikabi stated that the contract—initially signed in September 2025—focuses on expanding crude extraction while capturing associated natural gas to eliminate routine flaring and feed domestic power generation infrastructure.

Key operational targets & metrics

Crude Oil Output: Increasing current production from 320,000 bpd to a peak target of 420,000 bpd.

Associated Gas Capture: Raising associated gas processing from 255 million standard cubic feet per day (scf/d) to a peak capacity of 400 million scf/d.

Facility Modernization: Upgrading and expanding infrastructure across North Oil Company fields and North Gas Company processing plants.

Power & Social Infrastructure: Constructing a dedicated 400-megawatt (MW) power plant, expanding local employment, funding community development initiatives, and upskilling North Oil and North Gas workforces.

Environmental Impact: Phasing out continuous gas flaring to redirect captured methane directly into national electricity generation.

The activation of the Kirkuk project represents a major component of Iraq’s broader energy strategy to achieve natural gas self-sufficiency and reduce reliance on imported fuel.

By upgrading processing facilities managed by the North Gas Company and constructing a dedicated 400 MW power generation facility, the initiative directly addresses regional electricity shortages while reducing environmental emissions.

The partnership also reinforces BP’s operational footprint in northern Iraq, complementing its long-standing management of the Southern Rumaila field and bolstering state-led efforts to modernize national energy infrastructure.

World.title: India’s Reliance pays record $25 million freight cost for Iraqi crude amid Hormuz crisis
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — India’s Reliance Industries (RELI.NS), operator of the world’s largest refining complex in Gujarat, paid an unprecedented record charter fee of $23 million to $25 million for a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) to transport 2 million barrels of Basrah crude from Iraq, according to shipping sources cited by Reuters on Friday, August 7, 2026.

The extreme freight surge—marking a jump from a pre-war average of $2 million to 12 times the baseline global freight rate—highlights severe shipping chokepoints in the Strait of Hormuz caused by the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict. Daily vessel transits through the strategic waterway have plummeted from a pre-war average of 125–140 ships to a fraction of normal capacity as shipowners avoid military risks.

Key financial & logistics metrics

Soaring Freight Rates: Reliance chartered the VLCC from South Korea’s Sinokor at 1,200 points on the Worldscale freight index—12 times the reference benchmark—up from pre-war levels of 0.8 to 0.9 times ($2 million total).

Deep SOMO Discounts: To offset soaring shipping costs and attract buyers into the Gulf, the State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) offered steep discounts of $25 to $30 per barrel below Dubai regional benchmarks.

Net Margin Offset: Despite the $25 million freight tag, energy analysts estimate Reliance will still save millions on the overall transaction due to Iraq’s heavy crude price reductions.

Limited Carrier Pool: Sinokor remains one of the few international maritime operators willing to navigate the Strait of Hormuz to load cargo at Iraq’s Basra Oil Terminal.

While Asian refiners—particularly across India and China—are actively seeking chartered tankers to capture Iraq’s discounted crude allocations, shipowner reluctance continues to limit available tonnage entering the Gulf.

By offering deep price concessions, Iraq’s oil marketing arm is successfully maintaining crude flow off the Basra coast despite soaring war-risk insurance premiums and maritime transport bottlenecks.

World.title: ED director Rahul Navin gets 1-year extension
World.content:

According to a notification issued by the DoPT on Saturday, âAppointments Committee of the Cabinet has approved extension in tenure of Rahul Navin, IRS, as Director of Enforcement in the Directorate of Enforcement for a period of one year beyond 13.08.2026 i.e.

After three years as director ED, Navin, a 1993 batch officer of the Indian Revenue Service (Income Tax), stands a chance of getting two more extensions and serve till Aug 2029, all through the present tenure of the Modi govt with next general elections due in April-May 2029.

As per service age Navinâs retirement is due on 31 July 2027, but tenure of ED director can continue beyond that as in the case of his predecessor Sanjay Mishra.

On 15th September 2023, he assumed charge as Director (In-Charge) and was appointed as Director of ED on 14th August 2024.





He has also written a book on "Information Exchange and Tax Transparency: Tackling Global Tax Evasion and Avoidance" while being in the tax policy division of the finance ministry.

As ED director, Navin has laid down a new roadmap for his officers of completing all investigations within two years and ensuring attached properties are auctioned and restituted to the rightful claimant and victims of frauds â whether it be banks or individuals â within a specific timeframe.

World.title: DGCA to conduct preliminary probe into Baramati aircraft runway excursion: Centre
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The ministry of civil aviation (MoCA) said on Sunday that a team from aviation regulator, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), is being sent to Maharashtraâs Baramati airfield, where a Cessna training aircraft was involved in a runway excursion earlier in the day.

âThe air safety team from the DGCA is going to the site to conduct a preliminary investigation and ascertain the circumstances and contributing factors leading to the incident,â the ministry statement read.

MoCA further noted that the plane appeared to have sustained damage to its propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear, while no fatalities or injuries were reported.

âThere were no injuries or fatalities reported. The aircraft has sustained prima facie damage to the propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear.

A detailed assessment of the damage will be carried out by the competent authorities,â the statement added.

According to the ministry, the incident occurred around 12:25 pm when the Cessna C172, bearing registration VT-SEX and operated by flying training school Academy of Carver Aviation, veered off the runway at Baramati airfield.

The aircraft was being operated for a Circuit and Landing Emergencies (CL Emergencies) training exercise.





It was under the command of flight instructor Captain Chirag Shashikant Doifode, with trainee Abhijeet Jundre on board.

The plane had taxied out at around 12:09 pm for the scheduled training exercise.

âDuring the exercise, the aircraft entered the runway through Link Bravo and lined up at the threshold of runway 29, where a rejected take-off exercise practice was carried out.

World.title: 'Attempt to murder': TMC MPs blame BJP for attack on Mamata Banerjee's car, claim CM Suvendu link
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

(TMC) MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee on Sunday accused the

of being behind an alleged attack on former West Bengal chief minister

's vehicle, after stones and other objects were reportedly hurled at her car in North 24 Parganas.

Mamata Banerjee was travelling to meet the family of a TMC worker who allegedly died in police custody when the incident took place. TMC MPs Kalyan Banerjee and Dola Sen were accompanying her.

Kalyan Banerjee described the incident as an "attempt to murder" and alleged that the attack was targeted at Mamata Banerjee. He also accused the police of remaining silent spectators while the incident took place.

"The entire car, there was not a single second when stones were not thrown.

Stones were thrown every moment, targeting Mamata Banerjee to assault her," Kalyan Banerjee said, as cited by news agency ANI.

He alleged that hundreds of BJP workers were present at the spot and claimed that the incident took place in the presence of police personnel.

"Hundreds and hundreds of BJP workers were there, and police were remaining silent spectators, absolutely silent spectators," he said.

Kalyan Banerjee also alleged that there was a direction from West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari behind the incident.





"Of course there was a direction given by the CM Suvendu Adhikari," he said.

Abhishek Banerjee alleges ' political violence '

TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee also accused the BJP of unleashing political violence in West Bengal and alleged that Mamata Banerjee was "brutally attacked" while travelling to meet the family of the deceased party worker.

In a post on social media, Abhishek Banerjee alleged that the incident reflected a wider law-and-order failure in the state.

"And now, a former Chief Minister of the state, who was on her way to meet the grieving family, is brutally attacked by goons planted by BJP," he said, as reported by ANI.

He questioned the police response and said the incident represented a "failure of governance".

"This is not merely a failure of the state police. This is a failure of governance," Abhishek Banerjee said.

He also alleged that the police had failed to protect TMC workers and the grieving family, and questioned whether political violence had become a tool of governance in the state.

Dola Sen questions law and order

Rajya Sabha MP Dola Sen said Mamata Banerjee had gone to meet the family of the TMC worker who allegedly died in police custody and questioned whether she should have been prevented from making the visit.

"Our worker died in police custody, an incident akin to a lockup death. His wife is a councillor. You tell me, as a matter of simple, natural justice, should our leader, Mamata Banerjee, not go to meet that family?" Sen said.

She alleged that stones and half-bricks were thrown at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle and claimed that BJP workers and police personnel were present at the spot.

"They attacked her in a targeted manner... BJP goons and police stood in front, throwing half-bricks and stones, cracking the glass of Didi's car," she alleged.

Sen also said Mamata Banerjee's visit was not a political programme but an attempt to meet the family of the deceased worker.

Mamata alleges attack could have caused serious injuries

Mamata Banerjee herself alleged that large stones were hurled at her car in front of police personnel and said the attack could have resulted in serious injuries or death.

"Large stones were hurled at my car by anti-social elements, right in front of the police. The attack on the vehicle was so severe that if the windows had been open, my head would have been split open. We could have all been killed," she said.

She also alleged that the police were providing protection to the BJP and said she had never witnessed such an incident before.

"This happened right in front of the police. I have never seen anything like this. What is going on?" she said.

"Chor bhagao" slogans were also heard from the crowd, according to ANI.

BJP denies involvement, condemns incident

West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya denied any BJP involvement in the alleged attack and condemned the throwing of stones or other objects at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle.

"Let me be clear: the BJP has absolutely no connection to the incidents where mud, stones, or slippers were thrown at Mamata Banerjee's vehicle," Bhattacharya said, according to ANI.

He said the BJP did not endorse such behaviour and called for police action against those responsible.

"It is between the public and TMC," he said, while maintaining that the BJP condemned the incident.

State minister Agnimitra Paul also condemned the alleged attack and said neither she nor the BJP supported such actions.

"Mamata Banerjee may have committed many wrongs or made many mistakes, but we can never support this kind of behaviour, especially against a woman, and an elderly woman. We do not endorse this. If anyone is carrying out such acts while claiming to represent the BJP, they are in the wrong," Paul said.

World.title: People of 'Devbhoomi' always stand firm on national duty, says CM Dhami; commends 'Tiranga Yatra' response

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday praised the people of Devbhoomi for their overwhelming response to the ongoing 'Tiranga Yatras' across the state, stating that the citizens of the state have always stood firm when it comes to national duty.

on August 15.

World.title: Turbulence-hit AI flight captain screening dope test 'not negative, sent for confirmatory test:' Govt
World.content:
An Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi, experienced a sudden loss of altitude of about 300 feet during cruise

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The pilots of Air Indiaâs Aug 4 turbulence-hit Phuket-Delhi flight were subjected to psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival at the destination. The pilot-in-command or captainâs screening test report was not negative and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said on Sunday. The ministry has classified the incident as a serious one which will now be probed by Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB). âFurther action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results,â govt said.Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) rules stipulate that âin case the screening test is non-negative, the employee shall be immediately removed from the safety sensitive duty till a confirmatory report is received. In case of positive confirmatory test for the first time, the concerned employee shall be referred by the organisationâ for de-addiction.The aviation ministry on Sunday said: âOn Aug 4, Air India A320 (VT-EXO), operating flight AI 2379 from Phuket to Delhi, experienced a sudden loss of altitude of about 300 feet during cruise, following which the aircraft stabilised and subsequently landed safely at Delhi. During the occurrence, injuries were reported to a few passengers and cabin crew members on board.The aircraft was carrying 137 passengers, including three infants, and eight crew members comprising two pilots and six cabin crew. ââAs standard operating procedures following such an occurrence, both flight crew members underwent the prescribed psychoactive substance screening test. The screening test in respect of the pilot-in-command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing. Samples have accordingly been sent to the designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis, and the final report is awaited,â it added.Pending investigation, both pilots have been taken off flying duty by the DGCA. âThe aviation ministry and DGCA remain firmly committed to maintaining the highest standards of aviation safety and ensuring that all such occurrences are thoroughly investigated and appropriate action is taken in accordance with the prescribed regulations and procedures,â the statement added.The Airbus A320 with 145 people on board had encountered severe turbulence near Odisha and then suddenly dropped 300 feet. On arrival in Delhi, 13 passengers and four crew members were hospitalised. People in the know say authorities are probing this case from all angles including whether the handling of this turbulence event was correct; whether the event happened due to weather or some other reason; the likely impact on the aircraft like did it suffer hydraulic failure due to impact and whether it should have flown all the way to Delhi after the episode and not diverted to some nearby airport like Varanasi or Lucknow.DGCA rules stipulate that a pilot testing positive for consumption of psychoactive substances for the first time be referred to for de-addiction and rehabilitation. Such crew member can return for active duties with a negative dope test report.But after resuming flying if the same person tests positive for psychoactive substances again, their licence will be suspended for three years. And if after resuming flying the same person again tests positive for the third time, the flying licence is cancelled.

World.title: India, Russia to be linked by rail? Moscow floats proposal, calls it 'viable'
World.content:
Russian Deputy Prime Minister Marat Khusnullin has called on Moscow and New Delhi to explore the feasibility of a direct rail link to the Indian Ocean, aimed at reducing transit risks associated with the Bosphorus strait and Strait of Hormuz.

According to Khusnullin, potential routes could pass through Turkmenistan, Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan, adding that any corridor providing connectivity to India would be considered âviable.â

If realised, the proposal would create a direct overland rail freight link between Russia and India.

âA rail link to the Indian Ocean should also be explored. Risks related to the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz might require alternative routes: through Turkmenistan, Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan.

Any options providing access to India are acceptable,â Khusnullin was quoted as saying by TASS.

The proposal comes amid disruptions to maritime trade through the Strait of Hormuz following the escalation of hostilities between the US-Israel and Iran. On February 28, the US and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran, targeting key urban centres, including Tehran. Iran responded with missile and drone attacks on Israeli targets and US military bases across Bahrain, Jordan, Iraq, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE and Saudi Arabia.





Tehran subsequently announced a maritime blockade of the Strait of Hormuz targeting vessels linked to the US, Israel and allied countries involved in the conflict. The strategic waterway handles around 20% of global oil trade and nearly 20% of worldwide LNG shipments.

âThe construction industry is already capable of handling an additional one trillion rubles annually. However, if such a volume is secured for the next five years, it would be possible to expand capacity and build even more,â he added.

World.title: AINRC to contest polls in T.N., says Lakshminarayanan
World.content:
Leaders of the Puducherry- based All India N.R. Congress (AINRC) on Sunday announced the party has plans to expand its footprint in Tamil Nadu.

The party celebrated birthday (August 4) of the AINRC founder and Puducherry Chief Minister N Rangasamy, in Chennai on Sunday.

Former Minister and senior party leader K. Lakshminarayanan said many people from Tamil Nadu especially youngsters “who were impressed by Mr. Rangasamy’s leadership”, had expressed their desire to contest in Tamil Nadu on behalf of the party. “We have plans to contest in the next elections,” he said.

Puducherry Minister P. Rajavelu, said he was “amazed to see the kind of support that Mr. Rangasamy had in Tamil Nadu”.

The party also celebrated the birth anniversary of former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister K Kamaraj in advance. Former MLA and Member, Pondy Backward Classes Commission, M. Ilango recalled he and Mr. Rangasamy had met Kamaraj at the same time in 1974 during the elections. “We went as a group. We both became first time MLAs at the same time.”

Leaders including V. P. Sivakolundhu, N. S. Jayapal and Khaliyan Kandaswamy participated in the celebrations.

World.title: Disaster response force deployed to trace missing trekker at Shivagange
World.content:
The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) has joined the police operation to locate a 32-year-old trekker who went missing on Friday (August 7) near Dobbspet in Nelamangala. However, the teams are finding it difficult to conduct the search due to constant rain, said a police officer.

Advaith Upadhyaya, a private company employee residing in Mythri Layout in East Bengaluru, went trekking early on Friday on a rental bike and climbed Shivagange Hill.

An investigator involved in the operation told The Hindu that they had found CCTV footage of Mr. Upadhyaya parking the scooter, climbing the hill and also being at the top of the hill, but they had not found any footage of him climbing down.

“We are exploring two angles, an accident or a case of attention diversion. We haven’t ruled out any angles yet,” the officer said. Two police teams from Kadugodi, along with several teams from the Nelamangala and Dobbspet police stations, are involved in the search operation.

According to officials, the relentless rain has made it difficult to even establish his final movements and ascertain what might have happened to him. However, teams have been deployed at Shanthala Drop, where the last CCTV footage showed him.

When the mobile network was traced, his last location was found to be near the Kudur Road deviation near Dobbspet. As his mobile phone remains switched off, the police have not ruled out the possibility of attention diversion and have deployed teams in the areas surrounding the hill to check whether Mr. Upadhyaya appears in any CCTV footage.

According to the police, Mr. Upadhyaya, who hails from Indore, had gotten engaged to a woman a few months ago. After multiple phone calls to him went unanswered, his fiancé reached out to the Kadugodi police station, which then informed the Dobbspet police station and sent special teams to locate the missing person. The officer said the search operation would continue.

World.title: Jharkhand students protest updates: Students announce march to Assembly on Monday, Govt announces probe; Jharkhand Governor accepts resignations of three JPSC members
World.content:
Ahead of the planned ‘Vidhan Sabha gherao’ march by JPSC-JSSC aspirants in Ranchi on Monday (August 10, 2026), three members of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) resigned on Sunday (August 9), while the State government announced a multi-pronged action plan, including Crime Investigation Department (CID) and Enforcement Directorate (ED) probes into alleged recruitment irregularities.

Also read | Jharkhand protest: CID summons three serving members of JPSC in exam row

However, protesting students remained firm on their demand for a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) inquiry and said the Assembly march would continue peacefully. Jharkhand Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar accepted the resignations of JPSC members Ajita Bhattacharya, Anima Hansda and Jamal Ahmed following recommendations from the State government.

Also read | Jharkhand protest: CID summons three serving members of JPSC in exam row

The resignations came amid three days of discussions between the Jharkhand government and representatives of protesting JPSC-JSSC aspirants. After the talks, Jharkhand Minister Sudivya Kumar Sonu said the government had agreed to several demands raised by the students, including cancellation of the 14th JPSC examination and backlog recruitment examinations of 2023 and 2025.

Also read | Years of delayed exams, bribery allegations provoke Jharkhand protests

“We are hopeful of a positive outcome over our demand of cancelling the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination and reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC),” a student leader said earlier before the meeting.

World.title: Jharkhand government cancels JPSC exam; protests to continue till CBI probe ordered, say students
World.content:
The Jharkhand government on Sunday (August 9, 2026) agreed to cancel the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) preliminary examination and the JPSC backlog examinations held in 2023 and 2025 following six hours of discussions with protesting student groups.

Also Read: Jharkhand students protest updates on August 9, 2026

However, the students remained firm on their demand for a CBI probe into the alleged irregularities in the JSSC-CGL examination and said the agitation would continue, including a march to the Jharkhand Assembly on Monday (August 10, 2026). The announcement came even as all three JPSC members resigned and Chief Minister Hemant Soren assured protesters that “justice will be delivered with full transparency”.

Aslo Read: Hemant Soren asks student protesters not to be misguided by political parties

The State’s Technical and Higher Education Minister Sudivya Kumar said the government has accepted “98% of the demands”.

“The government has agreed with the demand for cancellation of the 14th JPSC and backlog examinations of 2023 and 2025,” he said, adding that the State cannot recommend a CBI probe into JSSC-CGL “as we don’t have jurisdiction over JSSC-CGL exams that happened in line with High court and Supreme court directions.”

The groups, led by Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) and JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, said they want cancellation of JSSC-CGL and all exams connected to the TSR Data Processing Private Limited Agency, a blacklisted entity.

Mr. Kumar said the panel “held positive dialogue with students... and they will take a final call whether to withdraw the agitation or not.”

Responding to the demand over JSSC-CGL, the government said a committee will be formed under a retired judge for a judicial probe and the CID will investigate the criminal angle. It has not yet agreed to cancel exams conducted by the TDPL.

Piyush Kumar, a student delegation member, said that the resolution was “unacceptable”. “We first want the cancellation of the exam and then the investigation,” he said.

The four-member committee of State Ministers informed the protesting groups that a fast-track court will be established for the speedy disposal of cases on the alleged exam irregularities. The court will file a charge-sheet within 90 days, Minister Kumar said. “A panel will also be formed with experts drawn from IIT-ISM Dhanbad, IIM Ranchi and XLRI Jamshedpur to suggest examination reforms,” he said.

But Chandan Kumar, another delegation member from JLKM, said that there is “no clarity over the timeline.”

Earlier, the talks started around noon, and the delegation members returned to the protest site at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium around 6:30 p.m. The government representatives met with the three student delegations, including one from AISA, separately and then with all the groups together.

Protesters from all over the State continued to join the agitation and are expected to participate in the Monday march. Five aspirants continued their indefinite hunger strike, including Devendra Mahto, whose hunger strike entered the eighth day.

World.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends Chief Justices for four HCs
World.content:
The Supreme Court Collegium headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has recommended Chief Justices to four High Courts. The Collegium, in a meeting held on August 6, the resolution of which was published on Sunday (August 9, 2026), has proposed new Chief Justices to the High Courts of Patna, Calcutta, Bombay and Punjab and Haryana.

Delhi High Court judge, Justice V. Kameswar Rao, has been recommended for elevation as the Chief Justice of Patna High Court. Justice Rao was appointed Additional Judge of the Delhi High Court in April 2013 and became a Permanent Judge in March 2015. He was transferred to the Karnataka High Court in 2024 and repatriated to the Delhi High Court in July 2025.

Justice Ravindra V. Ghuge, a Bombay High Court judge, has been recommended for the Calcutta High Court Chief Justiceship. Justice Ghuge is presently serving as the acting Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court after the appointment of Justice Shree Chandrashekhar to the Supreme Court. He was elevated as a judge of the High Court in 2013.

The Collegium has proposed Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, a judge of the Allahabad High Court, for elevation as the Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court. Justice Tripathi was elevated as an Additional Judge of the Allahabad High Court in September 2013 and made a Permanent Judge in April 2015.

Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra, whose parent High Court is Allahabad and currently serving on the Punjab and Haryana High Court Bench, has been recommended for the Chief Justiceship of the Punjab and Haryana High Court. He took the oath as an Additional Judge in February 2014 and was made a Permanent Judge in February 2016. Justice Mishra was transferred to the Punjab and Haryana High Court in July 2025.

World.title: ED Director Rahul Navin gets one-year extension
World.content:
The Enforcement Directorate Director, Rahul Navin, has been given a one-year extension, as approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet.

Mr. Navin’s tenure as the ED chief has been extended by one year beyond August 13, 2026, “including extension in service beyond the date of his superannuation i.e. July 31, 2027, or until further orders, whichever is earlier”.

The 1993-batch Indian Revenue Service (Income Tax) official had joined the agency as a Special Director in November 2019. He was given the additional charge as ED Director in September 2023. In August 2024, he became full-time chief.

In May 2026, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) Director, Praveen Sood, had been given another one-year extension. The 1986-batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer was earlier granted a one-year extension in May 2025 after completion of his two-year term as CBI Director.

World.title: Census 2027: Ladakh to lead caste enumeration in independent India
World.content:
Ladakh, one of the country’s two youngest Union Territories, is set to lead the way in demonstrating how caste will be enumerated for the first time in independent India. The second phase of the Census—the Population Enumeration (PE)—which starts on August 17 in Ladakh and other snow-bound areas, is likely to ask questions on 40 parameters and provide an open-ended column for caste enumeration.

Open-column methodology

As reported by The Hindu on July 6, the rehearsal, or the “pre-test” for the PE phase, was conducted from July 1 to 20 in 16 States and Union Territories, where respondents, other than Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes, recorded their castes in an “open column”, or the enumerator noted a resident’s caste as declared by them. The methodology is likely to be retained in the final form.

While the ongoing Census is India’s first digital Census, officials are making an exception for Ladakh by printing a sufficient number of paper schedules. The move takes into account the presence of large defence establishments in the region bordering China and Pakistan, whose locations cannot be geo-tagged because of security concerns. The digital Census mandatorily requires enumerators to geo-locate the structures on a mobile App. Respondents who self-enumerate on Census portal are also required to do the same.

Though the questionnaire or the schedule is yet to be notified by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI), preparations have begun in Ladakh and snow-bound areas of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand to conduct Population Enumeration—the second phase of Census—from August 17-September 30, ahead of the rest of the country, where the exercise will be conducted in February 2027.

The Directorate of Census Operations, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, has concluded a three-day Master Trainers’ Training Programme for Census 2027 population enumeration, marking the next phase of field preparedness ahead of operations scheduled to begin on August 17 with the self-enumeration phase.

According to Chief Principal Census Officer Amit Sharma, the three-day programme provided comprehensive training on all aspects of Census 2027 population enumeration, covering census concepts, caste and demographic data collection, digital tools, self-enumeration, interviewing techniques and hands-on use of the mobile application.

Ladakh’s case is peculiar as it was not among the 16 States and UTs where a “pre-test” or rehearsal of the questions to be asked during the second phase, was held in July.

A senior government official said that, in the absence of the pre-test, the master-trainers are being trained based on tentative questions, around 40, which are likely to be notified this week.

“The broad contours have been conveyed to us. This time the questions are descriptive and will also include caste. The caste column will be open-ended, and enumerators will record the name of the caste as provided by the respondent,” said the official.

The official added that since the Census envisages counting all structures and buildings, enumerators are being told to exercise caution and record defence structures along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) as “special charges” on paper schedules.

The open-column methodology had resulted in the 2011 Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) returning over 46 lakh different “caste names”, largely owing to the differences in what people understand by caste. Significantly, the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led government has consistently maintained over the last decade that the 2011 SECC’s caste data was unreliable because of “errors” in data collection.

The total number of castes recorded during the 1931 Census was 4,147. The SECC was conducted as a survey and was outside the purview of the Census Act, 1948, and had no statutory backing. The data was never released by the government.

On August 3, the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India notified in the gazette of India that “the conduct of Census of the population shall be undertaken in the Union territory of Ladakh and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir and the snow-bound non-synchronous areas of the States of Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, from 1st September, 2026 to 30th September, 2026 with a revisional round from 1 October, 2026 to 5th October, 2026”.

An option for self-enumeration will be available from August 17 to 31, before the start of house-to-house population enumeration, the notification said.

World.title: ‘Penance’ padayatra: Bidadi hoardings take jibe at BJP-JD(S)
World.content:
A newspaper  and hoardings put up across Bidadi in the name of farmers who allegedly suffered due to the red zone imposed on lands in Bidadi took a jibe at the joint padayatra undertaken by the JD(S) and BJP against the Bidadi Township Project.

The banners described the padayatra as a penance by the BJP and JD(S), whose own erstwhile government had initiated the Bidadi Township Project. The banners sought to highlight the contrast between the JD(S) and the BJP having started the project and now opposing it.

The hoardings featured animated images of Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy walking by holding the hand of his son and JD(S) Youth Wing president Nikhil Kumaraswamy, and former Chief Minister B.S. Yediyurappa holding the hand of his son and BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra.

Reacting to the posters, Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R. Ashok questioned why the Congress was pursuing the project, asking what penance it wanted to undertake.

Meanwhile, Mr. Kumaraswamy also reacted, saying that he knew which real estate person was behind the banners and s, while hinting that it was not farmers who had put up such banners.

World.title: Pak-Saudi-Turkiye defence pact open to any other country in region, 'purely defensive': DPM Dar
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister said on Sunday that the defence pact signed between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye remained “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles.

He also clarified that the agreement was “purely defensive” in nature.

The indication that an expansion of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed in the Saudi city on Friday, was possible came a day after the Turkish foreign minister said Egypt could be joining the pact.

The pact aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Dar further elaborated on the pact, which he referred to as the Makkah Accord, in a post on X.

“The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement […] reflects the depth of the brotherly relations between the leadership and peoples of the three countries.

“The Makkah Accord is the culmination of years of discussions and coordination, with a common desire to strengthen strategic cooperation in addressing multifarious peace and security challenges and advancing regional peace, stability and prosperity,” he said.

He clarified that the pact did not abrogate or replace any existing bilateral or multilateral agreements between the signatory countries, or with other countries or organisations.

Reiterating that any external armed attack on any one of the three countries would be considered an attack on all under the pact, he said it was consistent with the inherent right of individual and collective self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter.

Moreover, he said, the accord was “purely defensive” in nature.

“It is not targeted against any country and its sole purpose is to further strengthen our ongoing efforts towards peace, stability and prosperity in the wider region.”

“The Makkah Accord remains open to any country in the region willing to uphold its fundamental principles and resolve differences through mutual respect, cooperation and peaceful means,” he said, adding that the pact was consistent with the fundamental pillars of Islamabad’s foreign policy.

“Pakistan looks forward to continuing to work closely with all brotherly countries in the region towards lasting peace and stability. We remain committed to advancing the cause of peaceful resolution of all conflicts and building a more secure, stable and prosperous future for our peoples,” he concluded.

Later in the day, Dar and Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand exchanged views on the regional situation, including the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

Dar informed Anand of the “essence of the agreement and the joint resolve of the three countries to contribute to regional peace, stability and security”.

Egypt likely to join: Turkish FM

Earlier, on Saturday, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan also said he believed Egypt could join the pact once several technical issues were resolved.

“Egypt is already our natural partner on all issues. I believe that at the next stage, Egypt will also be among us in the alliance. We already act toward one another as if we were alliance members. There are a few technical issues. Once these are implemented, there is no reason for Egypt not to be part of it,” he told Turkiye’s state-run Anadolu news agency.

Other countries had expressed interest in joining the agreement, but the founding members had debated how the expansion should be handled, he further stated.

Some countries that wanted to join asked not to be named, he said, adding that the preferred model was for Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to remain the three core founding countries, responsible for establishing the principles, standards and long-term structure of the alliance, while other countries could join with the approval of the core members.

“Under our president’s vision, we should not remain limited to three countries. We should grow,” Fidan said.

Fidan also said the initiative was broader than the traditional definition of the Middle East because of Pakistan’s participation.

Pakistan’s geographical position meant the initiative went beyond the conventional definition of the Middle East and represented a broader regional perspective.

‘Same as Nato’s Article 5’

Fidan further elaborated on this, saying the pact was technically the same as Nato’s Article 5 mutual defence agreement.

Article 5 of the North Atlantic alliance specifies that an attack on one ​of its members is an attack on all of them. It obliges allies to take action they deem necessary to assist the country under attack, including potentially the use of military force.

While the Makkah defence pact stipulates the same, Fidan explained that its text contained general commitments whose practical implementation would depend on discussions and decisions by relevant bodies.

A country would need to make a request for assistance and would determine the type of support it needs, he said, adding that the requests could be of different kinds, ranging from intelligence and logistics to ammunition or, if necessary, military units, depending on the scale of the threat.

The signatories, he said, would decide through consultations what degree, form, and format of ​support they would ask for in the event of an attack, but that no country would be considered a ​threat as long as a member state is not attacked.

Fidan also said that the new alliance was not directed against Iran or any other country, but rather served as a general pledge to support the three signatories’ security.

He further told Anadolu that discussions on the initiative began before the current war environment, when there was no US-Israel war on Iran and other regional countries had also been involved in the talks leading to the agreement.

Fidan said its signatories were countries that did not have expansionist policies. “They are countries concerned with their own borders, their own problems and their development, and, if possible, they want to contribute positively to their environment through good relations and good neighbourliness.“

The three countries, he said, had different styles and capacities, but when brought together, they naturally formed a defence-oriented organisation rather than an offensive one.

“It is not an approach of going on the offensive and saying, ‘Let’s do this or that together.’ Therefore, unless it is attacked by a country, whether from inside or outside the region, this alliance cannot have any dispute with any country. But, of course, the power composition we have put forward will make a constructive contribution to regional stability,” he said.

He termed the pact the “most important step” toward bringing lasting stability to this region.

How will the alliance function?

According to Fidan, the pact would be operational under a political and military committee comprising foreign and defence ministers and chiefs of general staff, similar to Nato structures.

The committee would translate the vision set by the leaders into decisions and carry out related work, while a secretariat would be established to implement those decisions, he explained.
