World.title: Armenian Catholicos Garegin II attends first hearing in criminal trial
World.content:
Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

A court in Armenia‘s Armavir region has begun hearing the criminal case against the Catholicos of All Armenians and six bishops who serve on the Supreme Spiritual Council. Garegin II attended the hearing in person.

Clergy members and politicians gathered outside the courthouse. Lawmakers from the opposition Armenia Alliance and I Have Honour Alliance left parliament during the afternoon and travelled to Etchmiadzin to show their support for the Catholicos. Dozens of worshippers also gathered outside, periodically chanting “Your Holiness” and singing traditional Armenian church hymns (sharakans).

Prosecutors accuse the Catholicos and the senior clergy of obstructing the enforcement of a court ruling.

Garegin II removed Bishop Gevorg Saroyan, head of the Masyatsotn Diocese, from his post. Saroyan is one of the senior clerics who joined Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s campaign to “reform the Church”. The bishop challenged his dismissal in court. The court ordered his temporary reinstatement as head of the diocese until it reaches a final decision in the case. However, before the court could rule on the merits, the Supreme Spiritual Council, led by the Catholicos, also defrocked him. The council argued that the courts have no jurisdiction over the Church’s internal affairs.

Lawyer Ara Zohrabyan says the Catholicos faces criminal prosecution for carrying out his “ecclesiastical and canonical duties”.

He argues that state interference in the Catholicos’s decisions violates the principle of Church autonomy, the constitutional relationship between the state and the Church, and freedom of religion.

“In this criminal case, the court will examine not only the charges against specific individuals, but also another fundamental question: whether the secular authorities can interfere in the internal life of the Church and criminalise the exercise of the canonical authority of the Catholicos of All Armenians,” the lawyer said.

The trial comes after tensions between the government and the Church steadily escalated.

About a year ago, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called for the Catholicos to step down. He first argued that Garegin II could not lead the Church because he had broken his vow of celibacy and had a daughter. He later accused the Catholicos of having links to foreign intelligence services. The ruling Civil Contract party has also included the removal of the “de facto head of the Church” in its election manifesto.

Members of the ruling party accuse the Church of interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy. The parliamentary opposition rejects that claim. Opposition lawmakers argue that it is the government that is unlawfully interfering in the Church’s affairs.

First hearing ends after 30 minutes as judge recuses himself

Shortly after the hearing began, Judge Hakob Manukyan announced that part of the proceedings would take place behind closed doors because they would involve “personal information”. He said the information concerned both himself and the Catholicos’s lawyer.

“A few minutes later, lawyer Ara Zohrabyan told journalists: “The judge has recused himself. He has withdrawn from hearing this case.”

According to Zohrabyan, the judge said he had once granted him his licence to practise law, which could “raise doubts about his impartiality”. Zohrabyan said he did not believe this constituted valid grounds for recusal.

“However, he refused to take part in this disgraceful trial. The very fact that the Catholicos is standing trial is deeply troubling. The case will now go to another judge.”

After the hearing, the Catholicos of All Armenians and his supporters headed to the cathedral to attend a church service and pray together.

Garegin II: “The authorities are trying to bring the Church under their control”

After the service, the Catholicos addressed those gathered outside the cathedral. He said the authorities were taking steps to undermine the Church’s authority, restrict its autonomy and bring it under their control.

“The authorities are persecuting the Church and the clergy. They have arrested and restricted the freedom of a number of clergymen, benefactors and other patriotic individuals through unlawful and fabricated criminal cases,” he said.

The Catholicos dismissed the charges against himself and the six clergymen as groundless.

“We remain steadfast in our faith and determination to defend our rights, which are guaranteed both by our country’s Constitution and by the fundamental principles of international law.”

Opposition declares a “day of shame”

Marianna Gakhramanyan, an MP from the opposition I Have Honour Alliance, said:

“Today is a day of shame. The Catholicos of All Armenians, our spiritual father and the head of our Church, is standing trial in Etchmiadzin. It is shameful and unprecedented. This is an attack not only on the independence of the Armenian Apostolic Church but also on Armenia’s Constitution, which clearly states that the political authorities have no right to interfere in the affairs of the Church and that the Church is separate from the state.”

“Who is defending the Church – us or you?” asks ruling party MP

Commenting on opposition lawmakers who came to support the Catholicos, Civil Contract MP Artur Hovhannisyan said:

“The Church has begun interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy.”

He also referred to the allegations that the Catholicos had violated his vow of celibacy:

“We are the ones standing with the Church. We are the ones defending the Church. You are defending clergymen who broke their vow of celibacy, who engage in politics and use religion and the Church to protect themselves from the consequences of breaking that vow and taking part in politics. Anyone who has broken the vow of celibacy should leave the Church.”

The ruling Civil Contract party’s election manifesto also outlines plans to reform the Church. Under the proposal, the “de facto head of the Church”, as Pashinyan’s team refers to the Catholicos, should leave office. The plan calls for the election of a locum tenens, the adoption of a new Church charter containing “mechanisms to preserve centuries-old traditions”, and, ultimately, the election of a new Catholicos.

Comment

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan told Reuters:

“Pashinyan has come to see the Church as a political threat and as an institution capable of supporting the opposition and various political parties in their efforts to gain power.

“The case against the clergy fits into a broader pattern of selective justice pursued by Pashinyan’s government, under which leading opposition figures have been arrested and some of their property has been confiscated by the state.”

Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

World.title: Azerbaijan FM in Kyiv: gas for Ukraine, visit to Irpin, Ukrainian drones
World.content:
Azerbaijani FM visits Ukraine

Azerbaijan‘s Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov paid an official visit to Ukraine on 6 August.

It was the first visit by an Azerbaijani foreign minister to Kyiv since the start of Russia‘s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Bayramov began his visit with a trip to Irpin, where he viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones and laid a wreath at a memorial to fallen defenders at Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry.

He also held meetings with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, President Volodymyr Zelensky, Head of the Presidential Office Andriy Yermak, Defence Intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and National Security and Defence Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

One of the most notable announcements was Azerbaijan’s stated willingness to supply Ukraine with natural gas if needed.

The two sides also discussed the possible use of Ukraine’s underground gas storage facilities to strengthen regional energy security.

These developments are significant both regionally and internationally, particularly in the context of Azerbaijan’s relations with Russia.

In mid-July, Bayramov met Sergei Lavrov in Moscow and said the “difficult period” in bilateral relations was over and that ties had been fully normalised. A few weeks later, in Kyiv, he reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also signalling Baku’s interest in expanding energy cooperation.

The visit illustrates Baku’s multi-vector foreign policy. While maintaining dialogue with Russia, Azerbaijan has continued to provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and has expressed its readiness to support the country in the energy sector if required.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

Symbolic and practical significance of the Irpin visit

Irpin was one of the towns where the Russian advance on Kyiv was halted in 2022. Hundreds of civilians were killed during the fighting, and more than 70% of the town’s housing stock was destroyed.

Azerbaijan has contributed to Irpin’s reconstruction.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

The minister laid flowers at the bust of academician Zarifa Aliyeva in the park named after her, and visited the Zarifa Aliyeva Linguistic Lyceum and Irpin Central City Polyclinic, both rebuilt with Azerbaijan’s support. He was also briefed on future reconstruction projects, including plans to restore the town’s House of Culture.

In his statement, Zelensky said Bayramov had visited a school, a hospital and a rehabilitation centre supported by Azerbaijan. The visit to Irpin was seen as a demonstration of humanitarian solidarity with Ukraine, as well as Azerbaijan’s willingness to share its experience in rebuilding territories recovered from occupation.

I received Azerbaijan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, @Bayramov_Jeyhun. This is the Minister’s first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion. He began his visit in Irpin, where he visited a school, a hospital, and a rehabilitation center supported by… pic.twitter.com/7HTLIaz3EF — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) August 6, 2026

The visit to a town devastated by Russian forces, together with Bayramov’s review of reconstruction efforts and Azerbaijan’s continued support, was seen as underscoring Baku’s intention to reaffirm its longstanding position despite the “normalisation” of relations with Moscow, particularly its commitment to the principle of territorial integrity.

Following the official welcoming ceremony at the Foreign Ministry, Bayramov and Sybiha viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones. They then laid a wreath at the Memorial to the Fallen Defenders of Ukraine and observed a moment of silence in their honour.

Meetings and gas supply pledge

During expanded talks with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, the two sides discussed their strategic partnership, trade, energy, transport, humanitarian cooperation and regional security. Bayramov reiterated the need for an early end to the fighting and a diplomatic settlement based on international law, while reaffirming Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders.

He said Azerbaijan’s total humanitarian assistance to Ukraine had exceeded 50 million US dollars. Bayramov also highlighted reconstruction projects in Irpin and rehabilitation programmes for children.

During his meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky, the discussions focused on Russian attacks, the situation in the Black Sea, the disruption of grain export routes, defence cooperation, and cooperation in the energy, oil and gas, and agricultural sectors.

Zelensky thanked Azerbaijan for its energy and humanitarian assistance, as well as for maintaining constructive dialogue. Bayramov, in turn, spoke about the post-conflict situation in the South Caucasus and reconstruction efforts in the territories regained by Azerbaijan.

As part of his official visit to Ukraine 🇺🇦, FM of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 @Bayramov_Jeyhun visited the Embassy of Azerbaijan in Kyiv.



The Minister met with the Embassy staff and received a comprehensive briefing on the Mission’s activities. pic.twitter.com/UPqN5Hn9rx — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

At a joint press conference, particular attention was drawn to Bayramov’s remarks on possible gas supplies: “If the need arises, we will be ready to supply gas to our friendly Ukraine.”

He highlighted SOCAR’s long-standing presence on the Ukrainian market, as well as the importance of Ukraine’s underground gas storage system – the largest in Europe – for regional energy security.

The statement can be seen as signalling Azerbaijan’s willingness to contribute to the diversification of Ukraine’s energy supplies, while also supporting alternative routes for Caspian gas exports to Europe. Against the backdrop of Russia’s strikes on energy infrastructure in southern Ukraine, Baku’s offer also underscores the importance of competition and diversification in the energy sector.

During meetings with Kyrylo Budanov and Ihor Klymenko, the sides also discussed regional and international security, as well as prospects for energy cooperation. They reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of state sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of internationally recognised borders.

Expert: “Azerbaijan will continue to provide Ukraine with political, economic and humanitarian support”

lkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Atlas Research Centre and a political commentator considered close to the Azerbaijani authorities, wrote that the visit is being closely watched by Russia:

The Kremlin will closely monitor Jeyhun Bayramov’s meetings in Kyiv. Azerbaijan’s partnership with any country is an exclusive sovereign right, and no other state has the right to interfere in that process.

At the same time, Russia, which is waging a war of conquest against Ukraine, closely watches those who cooperate with Kyiv. President Ilham Aliyev‘s response to the same question from Ukrainian journalist Gordon, asked at the Shusha Global Media Forum two years in a row – that ‘Ukraine should not reconcile itself to occupation’ – angered chauvinistic circles in Russia. They believe Azerbaijan should accept the annexation of Crimea and the occupation of Ukrainian territories.

Just as Jeyhun Bayramov visited Moscow some time ago, he has now travelled to Kyiv. Ukraine is Azerbaijan’s partner, and Baku will continue to provide it with political, economic and humanitarian support.”

World.title: Giga Avaliani case: Two more arrested 10 months after Georgian teacher’s murder
World.content:
Two more arrested in Giga Avaliani murder case

Two more suspects have been identified in the high-profile murder case of a 28-year-old teacher in Georgia. On 5 August 2026, two teenage girls – Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili – were arrested.

Giga Avaliani, a mathematics teacher, was killed in October 2025. Five people have already been convicted over his murder, while the trial of a sixth defendant is still under way. With the arrest of the two girls, the total number of suspects in the case has risen to eight – all of them minors.

The arrests of Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili, after several convictions had already been secured, mark an unexpected and significant development in the Giga Avaliani case.

Nia Imnadze was one of Giga Avaliani’s former students and the girlfriend of the principal defendant, Aleksandre Gabashvili. Prosecutors accuse her of incitement to commit the crime.

According to local media, Anastasia Beruashvili is a friend of both Nia Imnadze and another convicted defendant, Giorgi Rikadze. She has been charged with failing to report the crime.

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics tutor, was returning home late on 1 October 2025 when he was attacked outside his apartment building. He fell into a coma following the assault and died on 24 October without regaining consciousness. Investigators say the attack was motivated by jealousy and what they describe as “unwanted communication with a girl”. The defendants have given a similar account. According to their version of events, Avaliani sent sexually explicit messages to his student Nia Imnadze, who told her boyfriend, prompting him to confront the teacher. Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, rejects that account. She says Nia had been skipping lessons and that Avaliani informed the girl’s mother, angering the student. According to Kupatadze, the attack was planned afterwards.

The Giga Avaliani case has become one of Georgia’s most high-profile criminal cases in recent years. Much of the public attention surrounding it has been driven by Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, who campaigned for what she said should be a thorough and impartial investigation. Her efforts also helped generate significant public pressure over the handling of the case.

From the outset, Kupatadze maintained that Nia Imnadze bore primary responsibility for what had happened and repeatedly called for her arrest. The recent detention of the two girls has therefore raised new questions.

But the key question remains: if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, why were the two girls not arrested earlier? Was their detention the result of new evidence, or did it come only after sustained public pressure and Eka Kupatadze’s campaign?

Detention of two girls

Both girls were arrested late on the night of 5 August, in what appeared to be coordinated operations. News of the arrests first emerged through a video of Nia Imnadze’s detention, which was released by her lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili.

The footage is deeply distressing. It shows a large number of police officers arriving at Nia’s home. Her mother, visibly distressed, pounds on the front door, shouting: “Come in, all of you!”, “Maniacs!”, “Murderers!”, “Do you know that Niako is innocent?!”

The girl’s father, meanwhile, tells the police: “You are going to make me do something the whole of Georgia will be talking about. If you treat my child so unjustly, I will do it.”

Police officers try to calm the distraught parents.

“Why are you taking my child? On what grounds? What does the court order say?!” the mother asks.

“The lawyer has reviewed the court order,” one of the officers replies.

“Giorgi, on what grounds are they arresting her?” the mother asks the lawyer.

“On the basis of a court order containing only formal wording, nothing specific,” the lawyer replies.

Nia sits in the hallway on a sofa, curled up with her face buried in her hands. The video is being filmed by her lawyer, who occasionally strokes her hair.

Shortly after the video was released, reports began circulating on social media that the second girl, Anastasia Beruashvili, had also been detained. No footage of her arrest was made public, but the Ministry of Internal Affairs later confirmed that she had been taken into custody.

During her arrest, Nia Imnadze became unwell and was taken to hospital, where she spent the night. On 6 August, she was transferred to a pre-trial detention centre. Anastasia Beruashvili was also taken there.

Minors charged in Giga Avaliani's murder case in Georgia – read more Five people have already been convicted in connection with Giga Avaliani’s murder: Aleksandre Gabashvili – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. He was the principal defendant in the case and was found guilty of organising a group assault and intentionally inflicting grievous bodily harm as part of a group, resulting in the victim’s death. Giorgi Rikadze – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. A friend of Aleksandre Gabashvili, he was convicted on the same charges. Demetere Chikovani – sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was convicted of attempted intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm in the Avaliani case, as well as organising group violence in connection with the case and four other incidents. Ani Naskidashvili – sentenced to five years and three months’ imprisonment. She was found guilty of failing to report a particularly serious crime. Another minor – sentenced to three years’ imprisonment. He was convicted of giving false testimony. The nature of the false statements has not been disclosed. His case was heard behind closed doors, lawyers involved in the proceedings are bound by a non-disclosure order, and the teenager’s parents have declined to speak to the media. According to TV Pirveli, the boy is named Luka Klatkin. Giorgi Malania – arrested in July 2026 and charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. Malania is the son of a former senior Interior Ministry official, who served as deputy interior minister between 2016 and 2019. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered.

Eka Kupatadze’s reaction

“Georgia has won another battle against the killers of a healthy, innocent and talented young man – Giga Avaliani!” Eka Kupatadze said in response to the girls’ arrests.

Giga Avaliani’s family has always maintained that those who carried out the attack were not the only people involved. They have consistently called on investigators to identify and prosecute all those who may have played a role in the crime.

The family has paid particular attention to the alleged role of the two girls. Eka Kupatadze has repeatedly said that they knew the attack was being planned.

Until recently, however, prosecutors had taken no apparent action against additional suspects, prompting repeated criticism of the investigation from Avaliani’s family.

Kupatadze even appealed for help to Ekaterine Khvedelidze, the wife of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder of the ruling party and widely regarded as Georgia’s “informal ruler”. Khvedelidze replied to her letter, expressing sympathy and support for the mother who had lost her son.

“As far as I am aware, the investigation has not yet been completed. I am confident that the relevant state authorities will see it through to the end and that all the circumstances will be thoroughly examined, so that no question surrounding the terrible tragedy that has befallen you remains unanswered,” Ekaterine Khvedelidze wrote in her reply.

Formal charges

On the evening of 6 August, both girls were formally charged.

Nia Imnadze at the time of her arrest

Nia Imnadze has been charged with incitement to intentionally inflict grievous bodily harm committed by a group. The offence carries a maximum sentence of 13 years’ imprisonment.

Anastasia Beruashvili has been charged with failing to report a particularly serious crime, an offence punishable by up to seven years’ imprisonment.

Under Georgian law, sentences imposed on minors are reduced by one quarter.

“The investigation conducted by the Ministry of Internal Affairs under the supervision of the Prosecutor’s Office established that, in September 2025, Nia Imnadze began taking mathematics lessons with Giga Avaliani. The accused, Nia Imnadze, told her friends Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Malania that her teacher, Giga Avaliani, had allegedly shown her excessive attention. By doing so, the accused incited Aleksandre Gabashvili to attack Giga Avaliani together with his accomplices,” the Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement.

According to the statement, Aleksandre Gabashvili, together with Giorgi Rikadze, Giorgi Malania and Demetere Chikovani, “decided to act on that incitement.”

What defence says

The defence has denied all the charges.

According to Nia Imnadze’s lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili, there is no evidence in the case to support the allegation that she incited the attack.

The lawyer also rejected reports that prosecutors had obtained data and messages from Meta, and that the arrests followed an examination of those materials.

“Criminal proceedings cannot be based on suspicion. They must be based on lawfully obtained evidence, and no other standard can override that principle,” Lekishvili told reporters.

Ketevan Vardanashvili, the lawyer representing Anastasia Beruashvili, made similar arguments. She said Anastasia had not witnessed any crime and that she and Nia Imnadze had seen each other only once, for a few minutes.

“They had no friendship and no contact,” the lawyer said.

As for Anastasia’s relationship with the convicted defendant Giorgi Rikadze, Vardanashvili said that “even if she was his girlfriend, that does not mean she had any knowledge of the crime.”

Complaint or incitement?

The arrests of the two girls have sparked intense debate on social media. Many commentators agree that everyone responsible for Giga Avaliani’s death should be held accountable and that justice should be served. Many have also expressed sympathy for Eka Kupatadze.

At the same time, some have questioned the actions of the law enforcement authorities. They have asked whether prosecutors have sufficiently strong evidence against the two girls, particularly Nia Imnadze, who faces a lengthy prison sentence if convicted.

The Prosecutor’s Office statement says only that Nia Imnadze told her friends that Giga Avaliani had allegedly shown her excessive attention. It does not explain whether she knew an attack was being planned or whether she urged her boyfriend to take any specific action.

“Does complaining to friends amount to incitement?” some social media users have asked.

Others have also questioned why, if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, the girls were arrested only 10 months after the murder. Some have asked whether the arrests were prompted by Eka Kupatadze’s campaign, and whether political influence may have played a role.

Those questions also remain unanswered.

Timeline of Giga Avaliani's case – read more 1 October 2025 – The attack

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics teacher, was attacked outside his home in Tbilisi. 24 October 2025 – Death

After spending 23 days in a coma, Giga Avaliani died. November–December 2025 – First arrests

Four minors were arrested: Aleksandre Gabashvili, Giorgi Rikadze, Demetere Chikovani and Ani Naskidashvili. April 2026 – First convictions

Tbilisi City Court found Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Rikadze guilty and sentenced each to 10 years and six months’ imprisonment. Demetere Chikovani was sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was later convicted over separate violent offences committed at a different time, increasing his total sentence to nine years and nine months. June 2026 – Another conviction

The court sentenced Ani Naskidashvili to five years and three months’ imprisonment for failing to report the crime. July 2026 – Another arrest

Giorgi Malania was arrested. According to prosecutors, he was charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered. August 2026 – Two more arrests

Two more minor girls were arrested: Nia Imnadze, Giga Avaliani’s former student and the girlfriend of the principal convicted defendant, and Anastasia Beruashvili, described as a friend of Nia Imnadze and the girlfriend of the second convicted defendant.

Broader picture

From the outset, the Giga Avaliani case came to represent more than a single criminal investigation.

It exposed a range of systemic problems, most notably a lack of public trust in investigative authorities. The case also highlighted shortcomings in Georgia’s juvenile justice system, as well as concerns over the protection of the rights of both victims and defendants.

Many observers questioned the release of footage showing Nia Imnadze’s arrest, particularly as it was made public by her lawyer. Some argued that the video was intended to generate public sympathy for his client.

“Unfortunately, public trust in the justice system – the police, the Prosecutor’s Office, the courts and other institutions – is now so low that victims, defendants and lawyers increasingly see shaping public opinion as the only way to obtain justice. They then seek to use public pressure to their advantage,” lawyer Londa Toloraia wrote.

In her view, this reflects a profound crisis affecting both citizens and the justice system itself.

“You no longer trust the state, even when it may actually be making a lawful decision.”

Toloraia also raised a number of questions about the arrests of the two girls: What evidence were they based on? Why did they take place 10 months after the murder? And why were they carried out at night, when Georgian law restricts procedural actions during nighttime hours, particularly in cases involving minors?

“How much influence does public opinion have over the justice system? A great deal. It is extremely difficult to withstand public pressure. And where institutions are fully politicised, it becomes virtually impossible to make a decision that is unpopular with the public,” she argued.

She stressed that legal standards must be upheld even when dealing with those accused of serious crimes – especially when the defendants are minors.

The Avaliani case has also exposed a darker side of public reaction. Following Nia Imnadze’s arrest, social media was flooded with hostile comments directed at both her and her family. Many users described her as the main culprit and called for severe punishment. Others went further, posting comments about the suffering they believed awaited her in prison.

A second group of social media users expressed concern about the tone of those comments. Toloraia addressed the debate in a lengthy social media post.

“Children are not born criminals. Before demanding that they be lynched, we should first ask why they became who they are,” she wrote, adding that juvenile crime in Georgia has reached one of its highest levels in recent years. She argued that the state’s response has focused on opening a “special prison” for children rather than preventing youth crime. A state in which parents who have lost a child must seek justice through public mobilisation, while institutions make decisions according to fluctuations in public pressure, is a broken state,” Toloraia concluded.

World.title: Odesa in summer 2026: Life between sea and war. VIDEO
World.content:
Beaches, bomb-damaged homes and explosions in broad daylight. In the summer of 2026, Odesa is caught between its traditional seaside resort atmosphere and the constant threat of Russian attacks. While some people relax by the sea and stroll through the city centre, others sift through the rubble left by the latest strike.

JAMnews visited Odesa to show what life in the city looks like today.

Odesa and the surrounding region remain frequent targets of Russian strikes. Residential neighbourhoods, critical infrastructure and port facilities have all come under attack.

Russia has carried out combined attacks using drones and missiles, seeking to overwhelm Ukraine‘s air defence systems.

The impact of these attacks is visible across the city. Residential buildings have been damaged, windows blown out and flats destroyed. Strikes have also hit Odesa’s historic centre, including heritage buildings and universities.

Ports in Odesa Region, along with the logistics hubs and warehouses that support them, are also regularly targeted. Attacks on port infrastructure have disrupted Ukraine’s transport network and Black Sea export routes.

The strikes often occur in broad daylight, when the streets are busy, cafés and shops are open, and beaches are filled with residents and visitors. At any moment, the familiar sounds of the city can be interrupted by explosions, air defence fire or the buzz of attack drones.

On several occasions, missiles have been intercepted directly over the coastline while beaches were crowded with people.

Today, it is possible to spend the day at the beach and the night in a bomb shelter.

World.title: “Russia’s annexation of Georgia’s regions would not go unanswered” – embassies on 18th anniversary of August war
World.content:
France, Germany, Italy, Britain: Russia’s annexation of Georgia

France, Germany, Italy and the UK issued a joint statement marking the 18th anniversary of the 2008 Russo-Georgian war, reaffirming their support for Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

18 years after the Russian aggression, we reaffirm our full support to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Georgia within its internationally recognized borders. We welcome Republic of Naoero’s decision to withdraw its recognition of the so-called independence of Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

We urge states that have established diplomatic relations with these entities to follow this example,” the statement said.

August 7, 2026 marks 18 years since the start of the Russo-Georgian war over South Ossetia. In the 2008 war, 412 Georgian military personnel and civilians were killed, along with 365 people on the Ossetian side. Some 20,000 ethnic Georgians were displaced. Georgia also lost control of 125 more villages in the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia).

The independence of South Ossetia and Abkhazia is recognized by Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela and Syria.

August 7, 2026 marks 18 years since the start of the Russo-Georgian war over South Ossetia. In the 2008 war, 412 Georgian military personnel and civilians were killed, along with 365 people on the Ossetian side. Some 20,000 ethnic Georgians were displaced. Georgia also lost control of 125 more villages in the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia). The independence of South Ossetia and Abkhazia is recognized by Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela and Syria.

France, Germany, Italy and the UK condemned Russia’s military presence in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

ЭWe reiterate our condemnation of Russia’s ongoing military presence in the occupied breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia in violation of international law as well as Russia’s obligations under the six-point agreement of 12 August 2008.

Russia’s ongoing militarization of Georgia’s occupied territories poses a serious threat to the security of Georgia and to regional and European stability,” France, Germany, Italy and the UK said.

The statement also referred to rulings by the European Court of Human Rights.

In October 2025, the court found Russia responsible for a number of violations in the occupied regions, including the use of excessive force, ill-treatment, unlawful detention and restrictions on movement between Georgian-controlled territory and areas occupied by Russia.

“We urge Russia to implement the rulings of the European Court of Human Rights relating to this situation and to fully fulfil the commitments it made on August 12 and September 8, 2008,” the statement said.

The four countries also expressed concern over recent developments in South Ossetia.

They said the so-called “Agreement on Deepening Alliance and Cooperation,” signed by Moscow and the de facto authorities in South Ossetia on May 9, 2026, further violates Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and is incompatible with international law.

“This is a clear violation of international law. This document, as well as the appointment of a Russian citizen to head the region raise concerns on a possible full-fledged annexation of the region, which would not go unanswered,” the statement said.

Support for the Geneva International Discussions, co-chaired by the EU, OSCE and UN, was reaffirmed.

They said it is the only format that allows the parties to work towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict.

The statement also stressed the importance of the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia and said its work would continue to be supported in the future.

World.title: Paramilitary promises footage of supreme leader unseen since March
World.content:
Video footage of Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei who has not been seen in public since he assumed the role in March, has been promised by a paramilitary leader according to Iranian state media.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei around the start of the president's third year in office in late July, but has given differing accounts in recent weeks about his access to Mr Khamenei.

On July 21, the president said interactions with the supreme leader were "increasing day by day", but in early August he said communicating with Khamenei was "very difficult".

Mr Khamenei was reportedly seriously injured in the February 28 strike that killed his father and predecessor, Ali Khamenei on the first day of the US-Israeli war on Iran. He had also generally kept a low public profile before becoming supreme leader.

Three sons of Iran's slain leader Ali Khamenei appear at his funeral in Tehran.

The report on the Iranian judiciary's news outlet Mizan appeared to be aimed at quashing speculation about his health. Senior Iranian sources have said he suffered facial disfigurement.

Deputy Qasem Qoraishi from the Basij Organisation, a component of Iran's revolutionary guard said on Sunday that footage would be released in the future.

Mr Qoraishi said the footage would "once again bring disgrace upon the enemies and detractors of the Iranian people".

The comments appeared to be aimed at countering speculation about Mr Khamenei's health and lack of public appearances.

Alternate shipping route proposed

On Sunday, local time, Iran said that a deal with Oman defining new shipping lanes in the Strait of Hormuz was in its final stages but reiterated that the strait would only reopen once the United States met other conditions.

A US official told Reuters on Friday that an agreement between Iran and Oman was close and could soon reopen the waterway, which carried a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments before Iran blocked it in response to US and Israeli attacks.

Iran reiterated that the strait would only reopen once the United States met other conditions.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday an agreement on the strait that lies between the two countries was in the "final stages" but reiterated comments made on Saturday that it would not re-open the strait unless other conditions were met.

The agreement would set out the new shipping lanes to be used once the US fulfils those conditions and the strait is reopened, Iran's Mehr news agency quoted him as saying.

Iran says deal on Strait of Hormuz is 'close' Iran and Oman are "very close" to reaching an accord on a new shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's foreign minister says. This is your three-minute briefing on the key developments overnight in the Middle East.

Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday, local time, that Iran and the US are not engaged in talks and Tehran will not start them as long as Washington breaches an interim deal signed in June, adding that messages are being exchanged via intermediaries.

Mr Araqchi repeated Iran's position that an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz between Tehran and Muscat was in the "final stages" but would not reopen the strategic waterway.

In comments reported by Mehr news agency, he said the agreement would set out the new shipping lanes to be used once the US fulfils other conditions and the strait is reopened to traffic.

Israel rejects Trump's peace plan

Israel has rejected US President Donald Trump's board of peace 15-point plan for Gaza, and will not withdraw until Hamas fully disarms, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday morning, local time.

US President Donald Trump last month announced there had been a breakthrough in his plan to end the war which both Israel and Hamas agreed to last year. (Reuters: Evelyn Hockstein)

Mr Trump announced last month there had been a breakthrough in his plan to end the war, which both Israel and Hamas agreed to last year and which started with the ceasefire.

Israel has continued to carry out strikes on Gaza since agreeing to the ceasefire last October.

Mr Trump said that Hamas, which ruled Gaza for nearly two decades before carrying out the October 7, 2023, attack on Israel that triggered the Gaza war, had agreed to lay down its weapons.

Houthi attacks

Iranian strikes on Strait of Hormuz shipping have been coupled with increased attacks by its Yemen-based allies, the Houthis.

In recent weeks, Houthis have targeted ships at another oil choke point on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula between the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.

What the Houthis' Saudia Arabia blockade means The Houthi rebels, described as one of Iran's "merchants of chaos", have threatened to widen the conflict in the Middle East by declaring a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia. Here's what could happen next.

The Houthis also declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea last month in response to what they said was a Saudi siege on them in Yemen, an allegation denied by Riyadh, which backs Yemen's internationally recognised government.

The group said they had attacked Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on Sunday, two days after the kingdom signed a defence pact with Sunni Muslim allies Turkey and Pakistan in response to growing regional instability from the US-Israeli war on Shi'ite Iran.

The Saudi energy ministry said a fire had broken out at the refinery but was later extinguished with no injuries and authorities were dealing with the incident, without giving a cause.

The Houthis used a drone to target the refinery, military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a post on social media.

The group had struck Aramco sites before in Jazan, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day in south western Saudi Arabia.

It was not clear whether or how either Pakistan or Turkey would join in any Saudi response to the latest attack.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said the new alliance was not directed against Iran or any other country, but rather served as a general pledge to support security.

The allies would decide through consultations what degree, form, and format of support they would ask for in the event of an attack, he said.

Reuters

World.title: Zelenskyy says 50,000 North Korean troops will help Russia in war
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says up to 50,000 North Korean soldiers will be deployed to fight for Russia, while calling on South Korea to provide support for its air defence.

Mr Zelenskyy said on X on Saturday that "a decision has been made for 30,000 to 50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on the territory of Russia", a higher figure than his estimate of 30,000 in July. He did not elaborate on how he obtained the information.

He said Kyiv had found some North Korean missiles in Ukraine's territory, without disclosing their locations.

"It is absolutely clear that North Korea will continue to build its experience in modern warfare, receive licenses from Russia, and receive all kinds of military tools from them," he said.

Urging Seoul to have closer cooperation with Kyiv, Mr Zelenskyy said that Ukraine "would very much like to receive support from South Korea in an area where we have a shortage", referring to its air defence systems.

"We are ready to work on the Drone Deal and other areas as well," he said, adding that Ukrainian diplomats "are in contact" with Seoul to push potential deals.

Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un signed a comprehensive strategic partnership treaty during Mr Putin's June 2024 visit to Pyongyang. The pact includes a mutual assistance provision if either country faces external aggression.

Russia's President Vladimir Putin and North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un meet in Pyongyang, North Korea June 19, 2024. (Reuters: Sputnik/Gavriil Grigorov)

North Korea has cast its deployment as assistance to a treaty partner.

Zelenskyy just scored an 'own goal' The Ukrainian president's decision to fire his popular, tech-savvy 35-year-old Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov last week baffled many. Analysts say what happens next could be pivotal to the war.

North Korea has sent so far an estimated 14,000 soldiers to Russia's Kursk Region in 2024, helping Moscow beat back a major incursion into the region by Ukrainian forces.

This month, a Ukrainian military intelligence official said that a North Korean missile unit has begun deploying to western Russia and could be equipped with 120 ballistic missiles and six launchers for strikes against Ukraine.

Ukraine is very short of high-end air defences and Russia has tried to exploit this by using more ballistic missiles, which are particularly hard to shoot down.

North Korea has supplied Russia with millions of artillery and mortar rounds, ballistic missiles, long-range artillery and multiple-launch rocket systems, according to Ukrainian and independent assessments.

Reuters

World.title: Alleged Irish international crime boss extradited from UAE
World.content:
The United Arab Emirates has handed over alleged Irish crime gang boss Daniel Joseph Kinahan to authorities in Ireland, the UAE state news agency reported, citing a joint statement.

Kinahan, who was arrested in Dubai in April, was named as one of three leaders of the Kinahan Organised Crime Group by the United States in 2022 when it offered a $US 5 million reward for the trio's arrest.

An Irish government plane took flight on Saturday to extradite the suspected transnational cartel boss from Dubai to face trial in Dublin over alleged serious crime offences, local media reported.

Ireland's justice ministry declined to comment and Irish Garda police said it would not comment on media reports, adding that Kinahan's case "remains a matter for the authorities in the United Arab Emirates at this time".

Police in Ireland issued a warrant for Kinahan's arrest for "alleged serious organised crime offences". (Facebook: An Garda Siochana)

The 49-year-old Irishman allegedly ran a group out of Dubai that has been linked by US and European authorities to a vast criminal enterprise dealing in drug smuggling and money laundering.

He was arrested in Dubai in April after a warrant was issued in Ireland for "alleged serious organised crime offences" and lost appeals against extradition.

On arrival in Ireland, Kinahan is expected to be taken to the Special Criminal Court in Dublin amid a large security operation, local broadcaster RTE reported.

Cartel's long legal history

The transnational group, known as the Kinahan Organised Crime Group (KOCG), is alleged to be the most powerful organised crime outfit in Ireland with wealth estimated by Irish police at over 1 billion euros ($1.6 billion).

Kinahan is expected to appear in Dublin's Special Criminal Court. (Reuters: Lorraine O'Sullivan)

Kinahan would be the second senior figure in the cartel to be extradited from Dubai.

Sean McGovern, described by a judge as "senior lieutenant in the cartel", was the first senior associate to be extradited after his arrest in 2024.

In June, he was sentenced to 24 years in prison in Ireland after pleading guilty to directing organised crime and attempted murder.

The case related to a long-running violent feud between the Kinahan cartel and the rival Dublin-based Hutch gang.

Sanctioned by US

The US government in 2022 imposed sanctions on Kinahan and other members of his family identified as leaders of the cartel.

The US Treasury alleges that Kinahan was the cartel's kingpin. (AP: Patrick Semansky/file)

It designated them as running a narcotics trafficking organisation active in Ireland, theUK and throughout mainland Europe, and engaging in "money laundering, firearms trafficking, and murder".

The US Treasury said Kinahan was believed to run the cartel's day-to-day operations, while his brother Christopher was also designated.

Their father, also named Christopher, aka the Dapper Don, oversaw the gang's property, the US government said, offering up to $US5 million ($7m) for information leading to the arrest of the father and sons.

Europol also designated the three men as "high value targets".

Wires/ABC

World.title: New Fremantle Traffic Bridge to open ahead of schedule
World.content:
The new Fremantle Traffic Bridge is set to open before the end of the year, months ahead of schedule, with many locals and businesses saying the impact of the closure has been better than expected.

In February, the 86-year-old wooden bridge was closed to allow for the construction of the new bridge, which has the same number of traffic lanes but wider pedestrian paths and a higher clearance for boats.

WA's Deputy Premier Rita Saffioti said while the closure had been expected to last for 12 months, the bridge would now reopen to road users before the end of the year.

"This is an incredible piece of infrastructure and the progress has been rapid," she said.

"The concrete deck has been completed and now the work really is about finishing the bridge, in particular the roads in and out."

The new Fremantle Traffic Bridge has a price tag of $596 million. (Supplied: WA government)

Half billion dollar price tag

The joint state and federal government project came with an initial price tag of $430 million, updated to $596 million in the most recent state budget.

It is the first "extradosed" bridge to be built in Australia, combining both cantilevers and cable stay supports.

"We're very proud of what we're delivering and in fact it's an alignment that was supported by the community and it's enabled us not to have significant impacts to the businesses, the residential and the whole traffic movement around here," Ms Saffioti said.

The closure has left Stirling Bridge as the only traffic crossing on the western side of the Swan River.

Authorities implemented a number of changes to the local transport network to accommodate the closure, including additional train and bus services, more free parking bays for SmartRider users and increased monitoring of traffic via CCTV.

Federal member for Fremantle Josh Wilson said the local community had risen to the challenge in terms of dealing with the impact.

Josh Wilson says the project "represents the delivery of high quality, beautiful 21st century infrastructure for the next 100 years". (ABC News: Briana Shepherd)

"A lot of incredible preparatory work done by the deputy premier and the people here in Western Australia from a transport coordination and public transport and local road modification point of view that meant that we were able to deal with that disruption effectively," he said.

"And I also want to credit the broader community for the way that they've supported local businesses."

Community support 'amazing'

MJ owns and runs a coffee shop in North Fremantle, an area particularly affected by the closure.

MJ says while there had been an impact from the bridge closure, the community had rallied around local businesses. (ABC News: Briana Shepherd)

"We did notice an impact, especially in the first month it [business] dropped significantly but our local community and support from our locals was magnificent; they were coming, bringing their friends; so community here, it's amazing," she said.

MJ said communication with the authorities about the bridge closure had been excellent, and she was looking forward to the reopening, hopeful it would bring more foot and bike traffic past her cafe.

"I just want to thank the community and our customers and everyone from North Fremantle for supporting me and the rest of the business," she said.

People born on Fremantle Bridge bid farewell before demolition Eighty people with a special connection to the Fremantle Traffic Bridge are invited to cross it before it is demolished and rebuilt.

Increase in freight on rail

The deputy premier said the closure of the bridge had coincided with a significant increase in freight on rail, meaning fewer trucks on the road system.

More than a quarter of all containers from Fremantle Harbour were shipped in and out via rail in 2025–26, a new record for the state, and the highest proportion in the country.

"As part of the work we undertook before closing the bridge, we worked with logistics companies … on how we can better support them through supporting some extra capacity in their distribution warehouses to get more freight onto rail, so another big win in getting trucks off road," Ms Saffioti said.

She credited the rail freight subsidy scheme the Labor government introduced in 2017, in which a $50 subsidy is paid per 20-foot equivalent unit of cargo, for the increase.

An exact date for the opening of the new Fremantle Traffic Bridge has not yet been set but Ms Saffioti said likely before Christmas, with the day to be celebrated with a community event.

World.title: Taylor Swift songs removed from Donald Trump social media posts
World.content:
Several Taylor Swift songs have been removed from social media videos posted by Donald Trump's campaign and the White House, reviving the long-running political feud between the world's biggest pop star and the US president.

The Trump campaign and White House have used several Swift tracks in TikTok videos, including songs from her more recent catalogue as well as earlier hits.

Among them was Swift's 2020 song August, used in a Team Trump video showing the president and First Lady Melania Trump watching fireworks.

The account appeared to acknowledge the provocative nature of the choice, tagging Swift and suggesting she would be "super excited" that her music had been used.

Songs from Swift's 2025 The Life of a Showgirl album had been used by Trump officials. (Supplied: Universal Music Group)

The audio has since disappeared from the post.

Other Swift songs, including Father Figure and Opalite, have also been removed from Trump-related TikTok videos, and several other tracks have disappeared from White House and campaign posts.

Some of the affected videos now display notices indicating the music is unavailable because of a copyright claim or has been made unavailable by the copyright owner.

Neither Swift nor the White House immediately responded to requests for comment. There has been no public statement from the 36-year-old singer explaining whether she personally authorised action against the videos.

The removals have attracted attention because of Swift's history with Mr Trump, who likes to use well-known pop songs to motivate his supporters.

The Village People's YMCA song has been a feature of Donald Trump rallies in recent years. (AP: Evan Vucci)

Mr Trump and his political operation have repeatedly invoked Swift, despite her opposition to him.

During the 2024 election campaign, Trump shared AI-generated images that falsely suggested Swift and some of her fans were supporting him.

Swift subsequently cited the fake images as one of the reasons she decided to make her own voting intentions clear.

The latest dispute also comes amid broader tensions between the Trump administration and musicians over the political use of their work.

Artists including Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter have objected to their music being associated with Trump or his administration.

Swift's political journey and Harris endorsement

Taylor Swift became more political during the 2018 midterm elections in the US. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for TAS Rights Management)

For much of her early career, Swift carefully avoided partisan politics.

That changed dramatically in 2018 when she publicly entered the political arena ahead of the midterm elections in Tennessee, where she was registered to vote.

After Taylor Swift was called a childless cat lady for supporting Kamala Harris, it became a popular social media meme. (Supplied: Museum of Australian Democracy)

Swift endorsed Democrats Phil Bredesen for the US Senate and Jim Cooper for the House of Representatives while criticising Republican Senate candidate Marsha Blackburn.

She said she had previously been reluctant to reveal her political opinions but had changed her approach following events in her own life and in the US. Ms Blackburn ultimately defeated Mr Bredesen.

Swift became more outspoken during Mr Trump's first presidency.

In May 2020, during the unrest following the death of George Floyd, she accused Mr Trump of inflaming racial divisions and told him: "We will vote you out in November."

Beyonce (right) joined Taylor Swift in endorsing Kamala Harris ahead of the 2024 US election. (AP Photo: Annie Mulligan)

Later that year she formally endorsed Democratic candidates Joe Biden and Kamala Harris, saying their leadership offered America an opportunity to begin a "healing process".

Her involvement intensified during the 2024 presidential campaign.

After initially remaining silent about the contest, Swift joined a long list of show-business identities in endorsing Ms Harris immediately following her September debate against Mr Trump.

Swift told her enormous Instagram following that she was supporting Ms Harris because the vice-president fought for rights and causes that she believed needed "a warrior" to champion them.

She described Ms Harris as a "steady-handed, gifted leader" and said the US could achieve more if governed by "calm and not chaos".

Donald Trump took aim at Taylor Swift on Truth Social last year. (Supplied: Truth Social/@realDonaldTrump)

She signed the endorsement "Taylor Swift, Childless Cat Lady", a pointed reference to controversial comments previously made by Mr Trump's running mate JD Vance.

Mr Trump responded furiously.

"I HATE TAYLOR SWIFT!" he posted on social media shortly after her endorsement.

His attacks continued even after he defeated Ms Harris and returned to the White House.

In 2025, Mr Trump mocked Swift again, questioning whether she was still "HOT" since he had publicly declared his dislike for her.

Despite the exchanges, Swift has largely avoided commenting publicly on Mr Trump during his second term.

ABC/Wires

World.title: Blues start AFLW season with 26-point win over Saints
World.content:
Carlton has held off a St Kilda fightback to claim the opening win of the new AFLW season by 26 points in an entertaining game that made a case for more double header fixtures.

The Blues made the preliminary final last season and entered 2026 with high expectations.

Carlton led by as much as 31 points but withstood a fourth-quarter comeback from St Kilda before sealing the 9.12 (66) to 6.4 (40) victory.

Loading Instagram content

Sunday's game was held at Docklands Stadium ahead of the men's AFL clash as one of five double headers this season.

The concept already appears a winner and will prompt calls for more alignment with the men's season.

Several thousand fans were in for the start of the game, with the crowd ticking over 10,000 just after half-time and reaching 20,455 when the attendance was officially counted in the fourth quarter.

Despite missing young dynamo Sophie McKay (calf), best and fairest winner Keeley Sherar (quad) and ruck recruit Lauren Bella (calf) through injury, the Blues were on top early.

The Saints couldn't capitalise on early centre clearance dominance and were swamped by Carlton's classy midfield.

Skipper Abbie McKay (32 disposals, nine clearances), Mimi Hill (28 disposals), Lila Keck (21 disposals, two goals) recruit Claudia Whitfort (27 touches) and Irish star Dayna Finn (22 disposals) collected plenty of the ball, while Lily Goss kicked two goals.

Young gun Poppy Scholz was the fire starter, brushing off a defender to kick the first goal, kicking 1.4 and appearing a constant threat with her athleticism and smarts.

Scholz's opener started a run of four straight Carlton goals.

Tyanna Smith was comfortably St Kilda's best, racking up 625 metres gained, eight clearances, 19 disposals and two terrific goals on the run, with support from Georgia Patrikios (27 disposals)

Amber Clarke provided a spark with two superb fourth-quarter goals.

Overwhelmed by Carlton's running power early, the Saints got a foothold in the game when recruit Sophie Butterworth nailed their first goal.

St Kilda smashed Carlton around the ball in the third term and cut the deficit to 23 at three-quarter time.

Clarke soccered through a wonderful skidding goal from a tight angle to spark St Kilda just 27 seconds into the final term, then snapped another to cut the lead to 11.

But Darcy Vescio's second goal put a dagger in St Kilda's hearts late on before Keck sealed the deal.

St Kilda's J'Noemi Anderson suffered a hamstring injury.

Mathew Buck's Carlton next host Adelaide at Princes Park while Nick Dal Santo's St Kilda travel to Geelong.

AAP

World.title: Body found in suitcase in southern NSW
World.content:
A crime scene has been set up up in southern New South Wales after a body was found in a suitcase.

Police say they were called to Wolgon Road at Oallen, about 60 kilometres south-east of Goulburn, just before 1pm.

Officers attached to the Hume police district attended and located a body in a suitcase.

The body is yet to be identified but police say it is believed to be female.

A crime scene has been established and the suitcase has been seized to undergo forensic examination, as detectives start their investigation.

In the Southern Tablelands region of NSW, the rural locality of Oallen, on the Shoalhaven River, is 109km north-east of Canberra and 254km south-west of Sydney.

World.title: Fraser’s Blues on cusp of finals spot as injury-ravaged Saints’ season slips away
World.content:
SportAFLAFL 2026 Fraser’s Blues on cusp of finals spot as injury-ravaged Saints’ season slips away Marc McGowan August 10, 2026 — 2:21am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

St Kilda coach Ross Lyon has described losing Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera to a potential season-ending hamstring injury as like an “arrow through the heart” as Carlton edged closer to an unlikely finals berth. In a rare Sunday night game at Marvel Stadium, the Blues’ revival continued under interim coach Josh Fraser as they took a major step towards qualifying for the AFL’s inaugural wildcard round with a 44-point triumph over the Saints, who played without Wanganeen-Milera for all bar the first nine minutes. Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera suffered a left hamstring injury in the first nine minutes of St Kilda’s loss. Getty Images Carlton had a single win from nine matches when Michael Voss resigned as coach in May, but this was their 10th victory in 12 games since Fraser took over – and propels them two games clear of injury-ravaged St Kilda. The 10th-placed Blues can lock in a wildcard spot if they defeat the Western Bulldogs next Sunday, strengthening Fraser’s chances of being Voss’ permanent replacement.



Related Article Four Points

AFL 2026 King-sized heroics: Why a Melbourne flag is no longer unrealistic Fraser, who played 218 games for Collingwood and Gold Coast, will make a call this coming week on whether he officially applies for the job, but Carlton fans made no secret about what they want, chanting “We want Fraser” in the fourth quarter and post-match. “If I’m brutally honest, I’m not comfortable with it, purely because I feel like I’m a product of a lot of people around me – but I appreciate it,” Fraser said. “I appreciate that they feel connected to us as a club at the moment. I think that’s a really important thing for us moving forward. We live in reality that we’ve got work in front of us, and we’ve got to continue to build our style and build something that’s sustainable. “But, I absolutely appreciate the sentiment and the well-wishes.”



St Kilda mustered only eight goals and 62 points in total, marking the eighth time in Fraser’s tenure that the suddenly stingy Blues conceded fewer than 80 points as they again dominated uncontested possession. Playing for his third club, Francis Evans produced arguably a career-best performance with 22 disposals, 12 inside 50s, 10 score involvements and a goal to headline Carlton’s performance. It was party time for Harry McKay and the Blues on Sunday night. Getty Images George Hewett had 20 of his 26 disposals by half-time, when the Blues already led by 25 points, while Marc Pittonet (two goals) took the ruck honours over ex-teammate Tom De Koning and Rowan Marshall, and Harry McKay booted three goals. The Saints, in 11th, remain mathematically in the race with a fortnight to go in the home-and-away season, but their hopes are fading.



Related Article AFL 2026 Daicos-inspired Pies down Eagles to lock in AFL finals spot They must beat Richmond and Gold Coast in the last two rounds to keep their finals chances alive – but also need the Bulldogs and Carlton to stumble in both their remaining clashes. Lyon’s men resembled the walking wounded on a night they honoured the late Danny Frawley in the sixth annual Spud’s Game. Wanganeen-Milera barely trained all week because of a hip issue, then hobbled from the ground early in the first quarter after suffering a left hamstring injury in a chase on the wing. St Kilda ruled out their $2 million match-winner soon after, and his season is probably also over. Nothing which followed that devastating blow could make the Saints’ night worse, but Mason Wood (calf) joined Wanganeen-Milera on the sidelines before half-time, while De Koning (right shoulder), Liam Ryan (left shoulder) and Bradley Hill (left knee) soldiered on despite their own issues.



Jack Silvagni also played a week after dislocating his right shoulder after the club’s medical staff gave him the green light. “I’ve been through it before. I’ve had lots of stuff happen. Obviously, when it’s ‘Nas’ [who gets hurt], it’s an arrow through the heart, in a sense,” Lyon said. Ross Lyon and his Saints could miss the finals for the third year in a row. Getty Images “But my job’s to lead people under pressure, and stay composed [but] I knew coming in it would be hard... “I’m not sure what the worst case is [for Wanganeen-Milera], but I would think, what I saw – and I don’t know much about hamstrings, but you’re [looking at] minimum three weeks. He’s not going to play in the home-and-away season.”



Related Article AFL 2026 ‘Incompetent or deceitful’: Geelong Hall-of-Famer questions club’s concussion waiver Lyon said he and Wanganeen-Milera shared a hug at half-time, but that the club’s staff were perplexed at his and Wood’s soft-tissue setbacks after an eight-day break between matches and not having a particularly arduous week of training. Hill’s return to the match was particularly surprising after he hyperextended his knee landing from an aerial contest in the second term before being helped from the field. The 33-year-old gathered a match-high 31 disposals to be among the Saints’ best players, along with Max Hall, who starred with 30 touches, two goals and 10 clearances. Expectations were high at Moorabbin after an off-season spending spree scored them De Koning and Jack Silvagni from the Blues, on top of Ryan and Sam Flanders, but St Kilda are in jeopardy of missing the finals for the third season in a row.



Adding insult to injury, Silvagni and De Koning were greeted with boos from the Carlton fans all night. Flanders played only 12 matches before sustaining a season-ending Achilles tendon rupture, and De Koning missed more than a month mid-season recovering from a punctured lung and broken ribs. Bradley Hill brushed off a jarred knee to play out the match. Getty Images Co-captain and dual club champion Jack Sinclair’s campaign also ended in June with a calf injury. Perhaps worst of all, injury-cursed spearhead Max King’s first match in 757 days ended prematurely two weeks ago with his own hamstring strain, which followed injuries to both his knees. Barring a Houdini-like escape from his side in the weeks ahead, Lyon will enter the final season of his contract next year under significant pressure to turn the long-suffering Saints’ fortunes around.



“I’ve got to wear it. I’m fine. I’m a big boy. I’m happy to take what comes,” he said. “Leaders shepherd, protect, nurture and challenge their people under pressure, and that’s my job. I’ll continue to do it until I’m either tapped, or I tap myself.”

World.title: VietJet to offer international flights from Western Sydney
World.content:
Exclusive BusinessCompaniesAviation VietJet to offer international flights from Western Sydney Chris Zappone August 10, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Vietnam-based low-cost carrier VietJet is set to become the third international airline offering flights from Western Sydney International airport, with an announcement expected as soon as Monday to confirm planned services likely to begin with flights to Ho Chi Minh City. The airport and the airline are likely to formalise VietJet’s entry to Australia’s newest international airport to meet growing demand for Australian travel to Asia and cater to diverse communities in Western Sydney, industry sources told this masthead. VietJet is expanding rapidly, and likely to fly between Ho Chi Minh City and Western Sydney. Paul Rovere VietJet will begin offering two weekly return flights between Western Sydney and Ho Chi Minh City from January, stepping up three weekly return flights from March, said sources with knowledge of the deal. Full details will be released on Monday. VietJet may also provide an update on the prospects of a launch of domestic services in Australia in what would be a major boost to competition in a market dominated by Qantas Group and Virgin, as Vietnam’s President To Lam embarks on a state visit to Australia and New Zealand this week.



Related Article Aviation Flying into night sky, first cargo plane from Sydney’s new airport sparks parcel frenzy The budget airline has already requested the 2252 take-off and landing slots from the slot coordinator for Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport. Industry sources say that even if VietJet plans to initially fly between Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane, the airline would still be months away from offering its first flights. To date, Western Sydney Airport has secured international flights from Air New Zealand, to launch in October, and Singapore Airlines to launch in November, as well as Qantas and Jetstar, which will begin in October. VietJet and the Western Sydney Airport were contacted for comment. The low-cost carrier operates daily return flights to Ho Chi Minh City, formerly known as Saigon, from both Sydney Airport and Melbourne, offering seven weekly services for each city. It also offers five weekly return flights between Brisbane and Ho Chi Minh City, as well as three weekly flights between Perth and Ho Chi Minh City. Basing flights from Western Sydney International Airport could appeal to historically Vietnamese communities in south-western Sydney suburbs such as Cabramatta, Canley Vale and Canley Heights.



VietJet’s website currently allows searches for flights between Ho Chi Minh City and Western Sydney International, although none are offered yet. VietJet is in expansion mode across the region with subsidiaries in Thailand and the Central Asian nation of Kazakhstan. Headquartered in Hanoi, the airline has 107 planes primarily based in the Vietnamese cities of Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Cam Ranh and Hai Phong. It has placed orders for 100 A321neos and another 20 A330neos. In total, the airline has planned orders to receive more than 600 Airbus and Boeing aircraft over the next decade. It also has plans to lease 10 Chinese COMAC-made C909s. In June 2025, in announcing the new Airbus order, Vietjet chairwoman Nguyen Thi Phuong Thao said she had a “vision and the determination to make Vietnam a regional aviation hub for passenger transportation, technical services, logistics, training, research, global supply chains, and aviation infrastructure”.



It has 40 wide body aircraft on order. Vietnam has become a popular vacation destination for Australians with flight capacity between the two countries rising to 263 per cent of pre-COVID levels in April of last year, according to Corporate Traveller, a division of Flight Centre Travel Group. World.title: Free GP visits on the rise as 1400 clinics ditch out-of-pocket fees
World.content:
PoliticsFederalMedicare Free GP visits on the rise as 1400 clinics ditch out-of-pocket fees Michelle Griffin August 10, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Bulk-billing rates continue to climb on the back of the Albanese government’s multibillion-dollar signature Medicare incentive, as the latest health department data shows increases in the number of free consultations for patients in all states and territories. The national bulk-billing rate for the June 2026 quarter rose to 84.1 per cent, almost 4 percentage points higher than in the same quarter last year. Almost four out of five patients aged 16 to 64 had their doctor’s appointment bulk billed in the June quarter – an increase of 8.2 percentage points year on year. Bulk billing for consultations with the elderly, which are typically more complex and lengthy, has lagged.



The strong results reinforce the record 7 percentage point rise in the take-up of bulk billing by GPs since November 2025, when the Albanese government began paying incentives to doctors not to charge out-of-pocket fees. The fastest take-up was in the Northern Territory, up 13 percentage points in the June quarter to 90.8 per cent. Almost nine in 10 patient visits in NSW and Victoria were bulk billed in the same quarter, 87.5 per cent and 85.7 per cent respectively. Bulk billing for older patients, who often have more complex needs and require longer with their doctor, is lagging. Virginia Star The laggard is the Australian Capital Territory, where only 59.3 per cent of visits in the last quarter were bulk billed, up 2.4 percentage points. A wealthier enclave than other states and territories, the nation’s capital has trouble recruiting doctors to meet a local shortage and does not meet the criteria for the regional incentives to attract GPs. More than 1400 practices have switched from mixed billing to bulk billing since the incentives were introduced, according to the federal health department.



The steady increase means Labor is on track to meet its $8.5 billion pledge ahead of the 2025 election to make nine of 10 GP visits free by 2030. Many GP clinics had previously restricted bulk billing to children and concession-card holders, but the new incentives give doctors extra payments if they waive out-of-pocket fees. For a standard consult by doctors in metropolitan areas that is about $63.50. Clinics that bulk bill all their patients receive an extra quarterly payment set at 12.5 per cent of the practice’s Medicare billing. Opposition health spokeswoman Anne Ruston claimed during June’s Senate estimates that some Labor MPs had bullied clinics into signing up for bulk billing.



She said MPs were “putting pressure on a practice by expressing great disappointment that they’re not bulk billing, when the department’s own figures suggest that 30 per cent of practices would be worse off if they went to a full bulk-billing model”. “You’ve got your MPs out there making these comments, trying to bully, as I say, their local GPs.” Related Article Exclusive

IVF Rose had two heartbreaking IVF losses. Then her specialist clocked one crucial detail A Senate estimates hearing was told by health department officials that their modelling showed 4800 practices out of 6600 studied would be better off if they shifted to bulk billing with the new incentives – meaning 27 per cent of practices would not be better off. Dr Michael Wright, president of the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners, said that while the incentives helped doctors bulk bill, they did not cover the costs for many practices – “even the government’s own modelling [indicates] it was never going to cover the costs for all practices”.



“General practices are small businesses, you know,” Wright said. “No one wins if practices close their doors because they can’t afford to keep their doors open. If politicians really want to help people all around Australia have affordable access to general practice care, the best way to do that is by increasing Medicare rebates, particularly for the longer and more complex consultations, because that’s the care that GPs are increasingly providing for our patients. But the way Medicare is structured, there’s sort of a disincentive for providing that longer care.” The government is reviewing the way it costs individual consultations for different issues, through a review of the Medicare Benefits Scheme. Health Minister Mark Butler said the increased bulk-billing rates were “good for patients’ hip pockets and good for their health”. “Across the country more and more GP practices are becoming fully bulk-billing clinics meaning all patients need is their Medicare card, not their credit card,” he said.
